“No.” Zuko doesn’t want to know what a man like this would do to a boy that young.

“That your favorite word, no?”

“Nope.” …Probably overly antagonistic, but Zuko’s fire is itching up his throat, responding to the threat in the soldier’s body language, and impulse control on top of pulling back his fire has never been Zuko’s strong suit.

“A regular old comedian over here,” the soldier says slowly, crossing arms ropy with muscle. “We haven’t had one of those around here in a while.”

“We don’t want trouble, Gow,” the merchant says. “We’re just trying to do some business.”

“Well, don’t let me stop you, Jian.” A nasty smirk. “I’ll just take our usual donation.” Zuko stiffens as Gow reaches out, purposefully invading Zuko’s personal space in a way that reminds him of Zhao and makes his skin crawl as the soldier grabs the water and salt off the counter.

“Hey, that’s—”

“Don’t,” the merchant says, low and quick and urgent, cutting off Zuko’s protest and earning an incredulous look.

“Better listen to old Jian there, boy,” Gow laughs, clearly enjoying Zuko’s frustrated anger.

“I’m not a boy,” Zuko snarls, eyeing the water in Gow’s hand and wondering if the waterskin would even survive a struggle for it.

“No? Well, if you aren’t then that means you’re old enough to be conscripted.” Zuko is almost knocked off the edge of his anger, at the idea of being conscripted into the Earth Army. “You’re probably a draft-dodging coward as it is, *boy.*” A smirk when Zuko twitches. He *hates* being called a coward. “Don’t worry, you won’t be running for long. They’re going to need more fresh meat for the Fire Nation now that Omashu’s gone.”

The words hit Zuko like a blow to the back of the head, unexpected and sudden and leaving him dazed and off-balance. He mumbles his way through paying for feed and half sack of rice as the soldiers saunter off, leaving the rest behind. Omashu is…gone? Fallen? To the Fire Nation?

A little voice pipes up from his right. “Thanks for not ratting me out!”

Omashu is so close to the coast and the Colonies that it had always vaguely surprised Zuko that the city hadn’t been taken years ago. If the Fire Nation decided to finally attack the Earth Kingdom in earnest again, instead of just defending territory, Omashu would be a good place to start from a strategic and symbolic perspective. Far more so than Ba Sing Se.

“We can feed your ostrich horse for you!” Zuko barely glances down at the little boy trying to tug on Jasmine’s reins.

What would start a sudden press into the Earth Kingdom, though? But Zuko immediately realizes that’s a dumb question. It would be the same thing that led to a sudden attack on the Northern Water Tribe after years of mutual noninterference: the Avatar’s return disrupting the delicate balance the world had found for itself.

“Please? Come on, I owe you!”

Sokka had said something about Omashu in that weird waking dream. But how could Zuko’s mind have possibly conjured something like that up when Zuko hasn’t heard of a single plan to take Omashu in earnest since…Zuko’s heart skips a beat or two. Sokka had said something about seeing *Azula* in Omashu. That…would make sense, if Sokka had actually said it instead of Zuko’s mind conjuring it.

“We even have meat for dinner tonight!”

Zuko breathes carefully through the numb disbelief that he and Sokka could have actually exchanged words, the feeling quickly overshadowed by creeping horror that Azula might not be chasing him. Agni’s balls, of course the Avatar would win out in the balance between bringing the Avatar or Zuko home in chains. Which means that Zuko and Uncle might not have actually needed to flee so far so fast in the first place.

It should be a relief, to have some confirmation that catching two exiled former Crown Princes is…an ancillary concern, for the Fire Lord. Instead, Zuko spins and spins between what is real and what could be true, between what’s only conjecture and what’s purely make-believe born of a wanting so deep it actually appears in front of you. Zuko feels untethered within his own thoughts until the sound of pig chickens abruptly jolts him out of his distraction enough to realize that in his buzzing panic, he somehow accepted an invitation of work from the small egg-throwing child.

*Fuck*.

&#45;-

The family offers feed, shelter, and food that includes meat, and Zuko points out that he has never helped shingle a roof before, but everyone insists it’s easy enough and Zuko is used to muddling through by this point. He hadn’t planned on lingering in the first place, let alone after the confrontation with the soldiers, but the boy’s father, Gansu, seems kind in an exhausted and beaten down type of way. And the mother, Sela, has a weary practicality about her that somehow reminds Zuko of Lieutenant Jee, enough to calm some of his still-spinning thoughts.

And they don’t ask why he laughs when the boy says that his name is Lee, or press for his name in return, so Zuko decides to stay.

&#45;-

Considering the boy is bold enough to throw eggs at members of his own military—hostile as they might be to the local populace—Zuko isn’t surprised that Lee is bold enough to follow him up onto the roof and spend the afternoon tossing over nails and shingles and prying personal questions.

Gansu just sighs and sends Zuko an apologetic look, so Zuko tries to tune out things like “where are you from” and “what’s it like there” and “do you miss it” and focus on learning how to put a shingle on right. It requires more finesse than Zuko’s usual jobs, but enough concentration that he at least doesn’t physically flinch every time Lee thinks of something new to ask.

Zuko wants the kid to leave but he doesn’t know how to make it happen without saying something that will probably get him tossed off the farm. Gansu didn’t exactly seek out help in the first place, to need Zuko to stay enough to put up with Zuko’s usual prickliness. But Zuko doesn’t know what to do with this child. He hasn’t been around a kid in…ever? Years? Does the Avatar count? Does it count if Zuko was still a child himself?

Lee’s insistence on knowing everything about everyone regardless of anyone else’s feelings on the matter reminds him of Azula. Zuko’s fairly certain he can’t treat the kid the same way. --

Zuko lies awake that night propped against Jasmine’s side, staring out of the lean-to they’ve been given for the night. The stars are bright, a new moon in the sky. Zuko usually sleeps best on nights like this, but he can’t seem to quiet his mind enough to get anywhere close to unconsciousness. After hearing about Omashu dreaming suddenly feels like a risk in a whole new way.

Could it actually be possible that his waking dream, what he took for a sun-induced hallucination or the early edges of insanity, wasn’t a dream at all? Sokka had said things about Omashu and Azula, things that Zuko couldn’t have possibly known on his own. Though it *could* be a product of his own mind, it’s not like certain voices in Caldera never speculated about taking the city.

But…’Crazy Blue’? That didn’t come from him. Zuko would never think of Azula that way, even subconsciously. Which means…what?

If that dream wasn’t actually a dream, if it was somehow Sokka doing weird Spirit things again and reaching across distance and space to Zuko and connecting…Agni’s balls, they truly were idiots, the both of them. Because Sokka had so clearly thought it was all imaginary, too. What was it, between them, that they somehow keep revealing things without realizing that the other could hear them? That unknowingly seems to be the only way they can be open to each other?

Zuko shifts, murmuring an apology when Jasmine chirps a sleepy protest. Fuck, he hasn’t let himself think this much about Sokka in…a long time. But in the quiet of the night, under the safety of the new moon, he decides to not fight it for once, to let his thoughts wander where they will. Immediately he pictures the annoyed scowl on Sokka’s face from that maybe-dream, recalls the unthinking way Sokka had reached out to touch him, as if Sokka always wanted his hands on Zuko and it was only his waking mind that ever held him back.

Zuko shivers and rolls away from Jasmine, suddenly too overheated and too restless to stay against her side. The night air is a whisper of coolness after the heat of the summer sun and Zuko shivers again beneath it, far more than the temperature warrants, remembering the feeling of a late spring breeze against his face and the sound of masks clattering to the ground.

Agni, Zuko *wants*, so much more than he should, wants until he feels like he is on fire with it. Like the lightning of the storm is still hiding in his veins even though Zuko knows he worked the last of it out days and days ago. He wants to see Sokka’s eyes warm with laughter, wants to see the unsteady pulse beating in the hollow of Sokka’s throat. He wants to feel Sokka’s hands and heat and smile pressed to his own skin. He wants Sokka wrapping himself around Zuko’s body, wants to twine himself around Sokka in turn and sink into the wild, chaotic pulse of his not-fire.

Zuko would give so much, to have that. He would let go of so many things for the chance, if it weren’t already too late.

Zuko opens his eyes to the night sky, suddenly feeling chilled in the summer night even as his inner fire blazes in his chest. It’s all too late. Zuko had his chance and didn’t take it, had multiple chances, and now he needs to live with the consequences of his inaction. He needs to remember that this isn’t for him, not anymore, no matter how easy it is to conjure the memories. He needs to remember that it never was, not really.

Zuko forces his breathing back under control, ruthlessly yanking his inner fire back like he hasn’t in days. The underside of his skin no longer tingles from the press of fire but now his muscles twitch with a pulsing kind of restlessness. Zuko growls silently, rolling to his feet, hands easily finding his swords in the darkness. The ground around the lean-to seemed flat and smooth when there was light enough to see it. It’s a good space for working with his swords and thoroughly exhausting himself, because Zuko knows himself enough to know that he won’t find any sleep tonight, not when his body is throbbing like this, not when there’s no way he could take care of it the usual way in this half-room with only the illusion of privacy.

So he will train instead, throwing himself into a physicality that isn’t what his body wants but is all that Zuko can give it. His swords hiss through the air as he begins to run through his katas, starting with the basic forms and moving through the intermediate and advanced sets and improvising when he runs out of even those. Slow and fast, grounded and light, heat moving beneath his skin in time to his motions until that’s all that he is, movement and hunger and burning.

&#45;-

Zuko isn’t asleep but he isn’t moving anymore by the time Agni finally peeks over the horizon, sending a fizzle of energy through his blood. As if Zuko needs any more of that. Still, it’s enough to have him opening an eye, and his tiredness and Jasmine’s calm are enough to have him only going immobile instead of scrambling up in surprise to find Lee sitting across the yard, looking at him.

“It’s early, kid,” Zuko finally rasps, voice hoarser than usual as if he spent all the night shouting instead of just drowning in images of all the things that could make him scream.

“You’re good with your swords.”

Zuko blinks. “Thanks.” The kid is like a more open, less sharp Azula.

“Can you show me?”

“What?” It sounds like Lee saw plenty already and Agni’s tits, Zuko is deeply grateful that he decided to reach for his swords and not himself, last night.

“Can you teach me?” Lee rocks forward in his eagerness. “I want to be just like you!” A more open, less sharp Azula back before she learned what the world was.

“Fine,” Zuko sighs, only grunting a little as he sits upright and practice-worn muscles protest the additional usage. “But you aren’t going to get good in just a day.”

“That’s okay!” Lee chirps, jumping to his feet. “I’ll practice lots!”

Really far too much like his little sister.

&#45;-

Walking Lee through the basics of not cutting his own face off comes surprisingly easy to Zuko. But then, Zuko’s been stuck on the basics for most of his life, for most things.

They don’t even touch the swords, much to Lee’s disappointment, but Zuko isn’t a complete idiot even if the whole thing reminds him too much of the first time he showed Azula how to climb her favorite tree. *That* had been a mistake, when Zuko came plummeting out of it a few hours later. He puts a stick into Lee’s hand and uses his own to prod at the boy’s feet, to tap his arm when his shoulder starts to sag.

Lee is ridiculously proud of himself by the time he finally leaves for his morning chores after managing to mostly-not-stumble his way through the first half of the most dumbed-down kata Zuko could come up with. And Zuko feels surprisingly calm, more so even than how he felt after all his training last night, like concentrating on something simple and uncomplicated was all he needed to untangle his thoughts. It almost feels a bit like meditating to start the day, something that Zuko hasn’t been able to do since the *Wani* blew up beneath him. Or like someone looking up to him, something that Zuko hasn’t had for far longer.

&#45;-

Zuko sets out after breakfast, much to Lee’s great disappointment and Gansu’s visible relief. Extra help making a roof waterproof during a drought doesn’t exactly outweigh the risks of having a sword-wielding, nameless, taciturn stranger eating your food and drinking your water.

Zuko sets Jasmine on a path to skirt around town entirely and doesn’t know why he’s surprised when he finds Gow and the other soldiers lounging across the road like they’ve been waiting for him.

“You enjoy your night at Gansu’s place, *boy*?”

Which, apparently, they have been.

“I’m surprised they let you go at all.” Gow picks at his teeth, eyes half-lidded and malicious. “I thought for sure they were going for replacement son, just like the little brat was looking for a new big brother.”

“What?” Zuko frowns, the word popping out against his better judgment. He really doesn’t want to engage with whatever this is, but Zuko doesn’t like how fixated Gow and his cronies are on the little farm.

“They didn’t tell you all about it?” One of the soldiers laughs. “Little Sensu went off to the war a year or two back and hasn’t been heard from since. At least not until now.”

Zuko eyes the vicious little smile on the soldier’s lips and wonders how hard it could be for the Earth Kingdom army to have just one competent person in it to weed out people like this. Just one. Are they really that desperate, to want their colors on someone barely a step up from running a protection racket?

“We just got word to give to the family, Gansu and Lee and Sela.” Zuko twitches at the way the soldier lingers over Sela’s name. “Little Sensu’s whole regiment got captured by the ash eaters. And you know how the ash eaters like to play with their prisoners.”

Zuko shifts uncomfortably in the saddle. He does not, actually, know about that. He knows the codes of conduct that are meant to guide every aspect of the Fire Nation military’s interactions. He knows the rules of war that all nations are supposed to adhere to. But looking at these thugs in their Earth Kingdom uniforms, Zuko suddenly wonders how many others actually try to adhere to the codes as closely as Zuko did.

“That family’s going to be begging for you to come back, even as scrawny as you are,” Gow laughs. “Sensu is about to get himself dressed up in Fire Nation armor and crushed by his own countrymen. Or maybe they’ll do that thing where they see how long you can go without screaming when you end up face to face with some real fire.” Gow’s eyes linger on Zuko’s scar. “I bet you got some experience with that, boy.”

“Why are you doing this,” Zuko finally asks, voice tight with frustration despite his best efforts not to let them see that they’ve hit a nerve. “They’re your own people.”

“You’re right,” Gow grins. “They *are* my people. This is my town. I can do whatever I want here. And you better get out of here. I don’t like *strangers* in my town, and we got news to share with a grieving family.”

Zuko feels ill at the eagerness on Gow’s face even as he nudges Jasmine forward, taking the offered escape and hugging the edge of the road to avoid needing to walk between them. He doesn’t stop feeling ill, thinking about their words. Not just about Lee’s family, but what they said about Fire Nation prisoners of war. Zuko doesn’t want it to be true, doesn’t want to believe that people like Gow could say anything truthful. But Zuko knows from living with Azula that a lie is never as good as a painful truth. And Zuko has seen enough of the Fire Nation and its commanders to know that what Gow said isn’t outside the realm of possibility.

Did Uncle ever do anything like that in Ba Sing Se? Or did he maybe brew a pot of tea and look the other way when it happened? A commander has to take special measures to keep troop morale high during a multi-year siege, after all, and Zuko thinks it would take more than just regular music night to do it when there’s actual fighting involved.

For the first time, Zuko really thinks about what it means for Uncle to be the Dragon of the West. What it would have taken to earn the title, beyond just an impressive parlor trick. What it means that the General gave Zuko a knife from the Earth Kingdom as a gift. It feels impossible for Zuko to picture his smiling, patient Uncle as someone who could condone torture like that. But then, Zuko would have said that it was impossible to do something that would brand himself a traitor, too, and look where he is now.

&#45;-

Zuko can’t stop thinking about the threat in Gow’s words even as Jasmine continues to carry him away from the farm. There was a taunting viciousness in the soldiers’ eyes, clear delight in inflicting emotional anguish on others. Would they have been so eager for that if Zuko hadn’t been there to rile them up? Would they have fixated on Lee’s family if Zuko hadn’t caught their attention first?

*Fuck.*

Zuko’s steps slow to a stop in the late morning. Jasmine immediately begins investigating his broad-brimmed hat for anything good to eat as Zuko tilts his head back to Agni’s light, sighing. Zuko isn’t so far away from the farm that going back will throw him off all that much. And it’s not like Zuko has anywhere that he’s going *to*. He can afford to turn around. Even if Zuko can already feel the premonition of the prickling embarrassment he’s going to feel when he returns to the farm to find a family grieving and nothing more, everyone perfectly okay outside of the loss of a son.

&#45;-

Everyone is not okay.

Sela’s story is garbled, jumping and circling back on itself as she flutters over Gansu, who just sits grim and stone-faced at the kitchen table. It’s easy enough to piece together, though.

Gow and his men had delivered their news and then tried to take Gansu with them, because every family needs to give a man to the Earth Kingdom army and Sensu was as good as dead now so suddenly Gansu’s family was giving nothing. Lee had taken issue with that and had attacked Gow with a kitchen knife, so the soldiers had taken Lee instead. If the boy was so eager to draw blood, then he might as well be doing it for the King.

Zuko could barely breathe through the telling of it, arms folded tight across his chest like that could somehow protect him from his own stupidity. He hadn’t even shown the kid how to use a knife, had barely shown him the basics enough for Lee to one day find himself in the vicinity of a sword without cutting his own toes off. The two didn’t even *translate*, the reach and balance and motions of knife work and swordsmanship were totally—

Zuko chokes off that particular line of thought. He has no excuse. A child asked him to play with sharp things and instead of saying no, Zuko acted like the kid was Azula and this was Caldera and of course children should know their way around a weapon, of course a child needs to know how to make others bleed. Stupid, stupid, stupid. It was an awful impulse back then and an even worse one now, but of course Zuko had done it again because Zuko *never* *learns*.

“What happens if I get him free?”

Sela slowly unfreezes at his low words, the first ones to break the silence since hers finally ran dry…however long ago that happened. “What?”

“If I got Lee free from wherever Gow took him,” Zuko clarifies. “What happens then? Do they just come back and take him again?”

“No…” Gansu says slowly. “No, we could…we could spread the word in town. He’s too young. People will be afraid that their other children could go too, if Lee goes. The town would make sure he stays.”

Zuko considers Gansu’s words, wondering why the town isn’t already making sure that Gow’s men fuck off and leave them alone if they have the power to fold Lee back into their protection. “But you would have to go in his place.”

Gansu shrugs, bleak. “Every man has to fight eventually.”

Zuko glances at Sela, who is grim and resigned and already saying goodbye even if she hasn’t voiced the words yet. She holds his eyes for a long moment, longer than Zuko is comfortable with now that he spends so much time hiding his Fire Nation gaze, but finally jerks her head into a tight nod. Zuko sighs and rubs his hands briefly over his face, wondering how he became so fucking *involved* in the space of a day. He’s pretty sure that isn’t how being a refugee or traitor or whatever it is that he is, is supposed to work. But it’s done now. And Zuko can fix this if that’s how they want it fixed.

&#45;-

The town square is deserted when Zuko rides in, bareheaded in preparation for the coming fight, eyes constantly moving as he takes in the emptiness and unnatural stillness. He can see the shape of Gow and his men, backlit by the sun, and the shape of Lee, tied to the back of a cart like some kind of prisoner. If his inner flame weren’t already pushing at his skin, the sight of the child trussed up like that would certainly have been enough to do it on its own.

As it is, Zuko just pushes that rage into a spot in his mind where it can be useful fuel instead of distraction, wondering if the soldiers actually expected him to show up like their formation suggests they did. Zuko might need to reconsider his own predictability after this is done. “I told you that you’re going to pay for this!” Lee pipes out as he catches sight of Zuko, defiant and righteous and painfully young.

“So you did,” Gow laughs, eyes tracking Zuko as he slides off Jasmine and draws his swords. “We got a fortuneteller over here!”

“Let the kid go,” Zuko says, calling on his breath control to project his voice across the square. He’s good at that. And if Zuko can figure out how to avoid goading them, maybe it can all end a little easier.

“You’ve got some balls, boy, I’ll give you that,” Gow shakes his head, cracking his knuckles in anticipation. “Coming into my town and trying to tell me what to do?”

“You don’t deserve the uniform you wear,” Zuko growls, prowling forward with careful, balanced steps. “You don’t even deserve to die under a Fire Nation boot.” So much for not goading.

Gow grins like Zuko has just given him exactly what he had hoped for, waving up the other soldiers behind him. “You hear that, fellas? This boy here thinks he can just wander in and insult us. Are we going to stand for that?”

Zuko shifts, angling his right side to keep the three soldiers in view as they snarl denials and threats and begin to spread out across the square, spears glinting in the sun. Zuko clenches his swords, then forces his muscles to relax. Does fighting Earth Kingdom soldiers makes him a patriot, these days? Or still a traitor? Then the soldiers close in and Zuko doesn’t think of anything at all.

The swords aren't as good as his old dao but they still sing for him in his hands. Zuko whips under the first attack, sliding easily beneath the spear and rising up to sink his hilt-wrapped fist into the man’s stomach. The man buckles forward and Zuko kicks him down to trip his comrade, already turning to catch a second spear with one blade. He redirects it into the air and steps into the soldier’s overbalanced lunge, closing distance to punch him in the face.

The man drops, eyes rolling back, and Zuko lets his momentum swing him around, squaring up as the tripped soldier finds his feet, foot already tracing a perfect crescent to kick the weapon out of the soldier’s hands. The crack of the spear haft is satisfying, as is the soldier’s numb surprise as he stares down at the two halves of his weapon until Zuko drops him with a twisting elbow to the temple, blade pressed flat underneath his forearm. Zuko turns to the last one standing, the first one Zuko punched, still on his knees and clutching his gut and at the perfect level for Zuko to plant a boot into the man’s face and relieve him of his consciousness.

Zuko assesses for a moment, confirming that their bodies are still, fire licking underneath his skin. Then he turns back to Gow, distantly registering that they’ve accumulated an audience of curious faces peeking through windows and cracked doors. There are a few hastily muted whoops from inside. “Let the kid go.”

“I don’t think so, little punk,” Gow snarls, drawing dual hammers from his belt, giving them an easy spin and a few casual swings through the air. Zuko takes a deep breath and settles into his stance a little deeper. This is going to get interesting. War hammers aren’t common and Zuko’s pretty sure he would struggle to lift even one of them, let alone swing them so casually.

*Momentum*, he thinks, angling his swords slightly into a more defensive position*. Evade, tire* *him out. Then use his momentum against—*

Gow stamps on the ground, the earth shuddering beneath Zuko’s feet, and that’s all the warning he has before a jagged rock is flying toward him. Zuko reacts on instinct, crossing both swords into a deflection that almost mirrors a firebending block, squinting against the shards of stone streaking past his face. More rocks follow in quick succession as Gow laughs from far out of Zuko’s reach. Or what would be his reach, if Zuko had any ability to spare a thought for offense as he dodges one rock, cuts through another, shatters a third but takes the cloud of debris to the face, the fourth unseen as it takes him in the stomach and throws him off his feet.

Zuko lets himself spin over the ground with the force of it. He uses a quick controlled burst of heat to burn the grit from his face—better ash than dirt—and finally gets control of the roll. Zuko faintly registers calls of encouragement as he finds his feet, eyes focused wholly on Gow as he reassesses the battlefield.

The new distance allows for easier blocking, which is in Zuko’s favor. But Gow looks like he’s out for a fucking morning stroll and Zuko knows he’ll tire of dodging rocks far earlier than Gow will tire of throwing them.

*Make him work for it, then.*

Zuko darts into motion, not forward but to the side, moving in jagged bursts that force Gow to twist and follow and constantly rise from and fall into his deep stance. Zuko is distantly aware that the buildings at his back might be in danger—not that the shouting and cheering from inside give any indication—as Gow slowly looks like he is having less and less fun, sending bigger and bigger rocks faster and faster.

Zuko deflects and slides and ducks and weaves, but he needs to find a way to break this pattern, and soon. He leaps *toward* the next boulder instead of spinning around it, planting his feet and launching himself forward, banking on the element surprise and Gow’s overconfidence—*please, let it be overconfidence*—as Zuko comes down on the man from above in a whirling flash of spinning blades.

Gow grunts, falling back away from Zuko’s attack, avoiding being hit but also losing his root. It earns Zuko a brief respite from dodging boulders and puts him solidly into hammer-swinging range and fuck, maybe the boulders were preferable. Each block of hammer on blade vibrates through Zuko’s arms with numbing force, nearly shaking the swords right out of his hands and making his scarred ear ring in sympathy, and Zuko still doesn’t have time to attack, can only defend. Except now he is tight, close, with no time to think or do anything except throw himself from block to dodge to block.

Gow drops a two-hammed blow that shudders down Zuko’s blades, Zuko’s short gasp of surprise breaking his breath control and his rhythm. Fuck, his swords aren’t going to get up in time for the next strike. Zuko drops, the short bristles of hair on his head moving as the hammer flies above him. A save, but a mistake, because now Zuko is crouched low, in a position to let Gow put even more power into his downward swing. Zuko hurls himself backward, rolling over his shoulder to flip to his feet just in time to catch a boulder square in the chest.

Zuko flies off his feet, gasps and cries sounding from around the square when he skids to a stop and doesn’t get up. He stares up at the pale sky, mouth open, trying to force his lungs to work again, squinting against Agni’s harsh light, the ground trembling as Gow stalks closer. Zuko’s body isn’t working right, fingers spasming around the hilts of his swords, chest frozen instead of sucking in breath, heels scrabbling weakly against the dirt, sense of balance pulsing in time with the ringing in his bad ear. His head is fuzzy, spinning, distant, like maybe he shouldn’t be conscious now except that it’s almost impossible to knock an Imperial firebender out during the daylight, even one as weak as Zuko.

Azula, Zuko thinks, will be disappointed if she never has a chance to finish her lightning strike on him. Would it have felt the same as the storm did? Or would it have more of Azula’s personality behind it, something sharp and biting and cold?

Then Gao is blocking out the sun, looming, hands rising to finish the fight, and Zuko’s lungs unlock to let him gasp in a hard breath and cut his fire free.

Zuko windmills to his feet, blades flashing and flames erupting outward. Gow drops his hammers in shock, stumbling backward and Zuko pauses, assessing as he pulls his fire back toward him and lets it spill down his swords. Gow’s eyes so wide Zuko can see the white all around them. Then they narrow in determination, the man’s hands curling into fists and the earth rumbling in response and Zuko flows onto the attack for the first time, blades singing and fire chasing after.

Zuko can feel a savage grin on his face as he throws himself forward, nothing but instinct as he fights with sword and flame in nearly perfect harmony. He closes distance and keeps Gow on the defensive, breaking the earthbender’s root over and over until the soldier finally stumbles and trips, dropping his guard enough for Zuko to land a whirling kick to the head that sends Gow crashing down.

Zuko stays light on his toes, poised and ready, inner fire howling in delight when Gow can only stay prone, glaring up dizzily from the ground. Zuko easily pulls his fire back to him when the soldier makes no move to rise, feeling it swirl back into his core vicious and wild and triumphant, like calling to like.

“Who…who are you?” Gow finally rasps, blood trickling down his face.

“My name is Zuko,” he says, pulling the last of his fire back beneath his skin. It feels like nothing to offer, but a sudden clamor of panicked murmuring jerks Zuko’s attention off the fallen soldier and to the rest of the square. The townspeople have crept out of their houses, close enough to hear his declaration, close enough that he can see their faces twisted and white with a fear that makes his stomach lurch.

Right. A firebender wouldn’t be welcome here. Not in the Earth Kingdom and especially not so far from the coast, where even there they’re barely tolerated outside the Colonies.

Zuko tamps down the churning sensation and turns toward the center of the square and the cart, relieved to see that Sela is already there, fumbling at Lee’s bonds. She looks up at his approach, face tight, shifting in front of Lee. It takes longer than it should for Zuko to register the movement as a defensive one.

“Not one step closer,” she says, shaky with desperate fear, reaching back to keep her son behind her body. “Not one more. I‘m warning you.”

“Sela…” Zuko comes to a stop, slowly sheathing his swords. As if it were his *blades* that she was afraid of.

“I know the name Zuko,” she spits, eyes on him as she continues to fumble with the rope around her son. “I’ve heard about the prince who was cast out because even the Fire Nation couldn’t stomach his crimes.” Her eyes fasten onto his scar, face twisted. “I’ve heard about how his father was forced to mark him so that no one would be fooled by him again.”

Zuko can’t breathe. “That’s—that’s not—”

“We will not be fooled by you, *Prince Zuko*,” Sela hisses, finally jerking the last rope free and urging Lee off the cart, never taking her eyes off Zuko. Off the threat.

Zuko can’t move under the disgust on her face. He glances helplessly to Lee, who glares with a ferocity that should be foreign to someone so young. “We don’t want you here,” Lee shouts. “Go! We hate you!”

Zuko falls back a step without realizing he’s even in motion, tearing his eyes away to look around the square, something tight and shaky in his throat when he sees the hostility around him, the impromptu weapons in hands, the slow bunching of the strongest to the front. Getting ready to do something about Zuko’s presence when only moments before they were cheering for his victory.

“I’ll go,” Zuko says quietly, taking another step back, keeping his hands carefully extended. As if anyone here would ever trust a firebender’s hands to stay dry.

Lee turns away, face closed, not fighting as Sela steps up to protect her son from Zuko’s eyes. Zuko’s fire itches, uncomfortable beneath his skin as he strides back toward Jasmine, using everything in him to keep his face calm and his face still. All the eyes suddenly feel far too much like an audience, like spectators, like sea vultures eager to pick over the carcass of what used to be a Crown Prince.

Zuko leaves town with their hatred at his back, an about-to-boil-over hostility that they never gave the soldiers abusing their position. Agni’s tits, Zuko was stupid, stupid, stupid, to think that he could play at being some kind of hero. That anything he did would have any impact other than to make things worse. He was stupid to forget that no one ever wants Zuko for what he is. Even Sokka had only wanted Zuko without the Fire Nation parts that weren’t convenient. Even Uncle doesn’t want the jagged edges that don’t fit neatly into the space Uncle envisions for him. Even Zuko himself had only tried to turn himself into something different, something better, something more worthy than this version of himself he wants so desperately to leave behind.

## Chapter 6: Meetup at the No Name Corral

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Warnings for canon-typical violence and injury

### Text

Zuko doesn’t know if he’s ever dropped to the ground so fast in his life. One second, he’s contemplating a particular shrub, trying to remember if these are the berries that you can eat or the ones that send you into the fetal position for half a day. Then a shadow passes over the glade, too quick for a cloud, too quick to really even see. But Zuko’s subconscious recognizes it immediately.

He hits the ground, body locked tight, heart racing and breath control gone and fire sparking on his fingertips before the shadow even makes it halfway across the clearing. In the space of a few too-fast beats of his heart, Zuko manages to throw a quick plea to Agni—he isn’t quite sure for what—and drag his eyes up into the sky in time to watch an orange-clad figure coasting away.

…Fuck.

Maybe that wasn’t the Avatar on his glider. Maybe Zuko’s body is just reacting to something it *thought* it saw. Maybe Zuko is hallucinating. Delayed onset sun sickness even though he left that arid stretch of Earth Kingdom territory behind days ago. Maybe there’s another airbender out there.

“Fuck,” Zuko whispers, dropping his face into the grass. “*Fuck.”*

That was definitely the Avatar on his glider. And Zuko knows he actually saw it, that it was no hallucination.

Agni’s flaming dick, the universe must be playing one giant fucking *joke* on Zuko, that in the middle of trying to make his peace with his complete and total failure as a Crown Prince—his complete and total failure as anything, really—here comes his mission and chance at redemption, fucking *following him*. Like maybe if Zuko hadn’t spent *years* chasing the Avatar, maybe if he had just sat on his ass and done *nothing*, the kid would have waltzed up to him already in chains and Zuko would never have had to deal with any of this *shit*.

…If that was the Avatar then Sokka must be nearby. And Azula.

Zuko goes still for a whole other reason then. He throttles back the automatic urge to reach out with his heat sense and see if he can feel that almost-inner-flame of Sokka's nearby, because Zuko is *not* going to fuck around with that when it comes to him.

Zuko takes a deep breath instead, forcing his thoughts into order, beating back the fluttering edges of something that might be panic. He saw the direction the Avatar went in. He could just follow. With Jasmine, Zuko would be almost as quick, at the pace the glider had been moving. But if the Avatar changes directions Zuko would have no way to know. And it’s not like he can start asking around the way he used to. Uncle isn’t here to smooth over ruffled edges, and Zuko doesn’t know if the towns around here are big enough to even *have* brothels to start asking in, so staying on the trail would—

Something white and fluffy comes gently to rest on his head. Zuko twitches in annoyance, shaking it off and staring for an endless moment at the tufts of fur that could only belong to the sky bison. Another flutter of white draws his eyes forward as more hair falls to the grass, marking the path the Avatar took.

“Fucking universe,” Zuko mutters, scrambling up, already moving, calling for Jasmine and feeling like he started to jog along the trail of fur without ever telling his feet to go, without being sure if he’s chasing down his old life or a new one, only knowing that he can’t stay still.

&#45;-

Zuko is embarrassingly relieved when the Avatar finally comes to a rest in an abandoned town rather than some wide field or bustling village. Zuko’s more than familiar with slinking into places like this by now, hugging shadows and finding alleys and thoroughly assessing what he’s walking into before he ever rides Jasmine down the center road. This particular dried-up remnant of humanity doesn’t seem like the Avatar’s kind of place, though—is it a spot of spiritual significance? Agni’s tits, Zuko hopes not—and he can’t figure out what the Avatar is just doing nothing, even if Zuko appreciates the time to evaluate and get his bearings and his shaking hands under control.

The Avatar looks listless, the airbender tired and resigned and isolated in a way that has Zuko itching to leap out of his hiding spot. The Avatar never traveled alone, before. Where is Sokka? Where is anyone who’s supposed to be looking out for him? Agni’s balls, Zuko could probably just *walk* over and throw him over his shoulder with the state the kid’s in. Mission accomplished. Avatar captured. Honor restored. His old life, ready and waiting, if Zuko can just make himself move. If Zuko’s inner flame weren’t vacillating wildly between thready tightness and restless bursts. If Zuko could trust his senses when the acrid smell of blasting jelly is thick in his throat and his fingers are tingling with cold.

This is probably a trap. This *has* to be a trap. Zuko might be out of practice with the Avatar’s particular brand of slippery reasoning, but he knows that nothing is ever straightforward when a thousands-of-years-old bridge between worlds is involved. There’s no way the Avatar could actually be here, alone. Absolutely no way. Sokka would never allow his friend to just glide off on his own, even if it still really, really looks like that from Zuko’s current vantage point. Even if Zuko hasn’t seen signs of another living thing and he’s been watching for…a long time now.

…Fuck, what if the Avatar *is* alone? Maybe this is actually the perfect thing. Maybe Zuko can approach him without Katara’s suspicion or Sokka’s distracting heat and…what? Make amends? Ask to tag along, because Zuko doesn’t really know what to do with himself these days but would really like to get his hands and hopefully his mouth on the Avatar's top advisor?

Somehow Zuko doesn’t think that will sound particularly good out loud. It already sounds bad enough in his own head.

Agni’s tits, of course the one time that Zuko actually finds himself in proximity to the Avatar when he’s alone and weakened and maybe actually *napping* and all around perfectly capturable and approachable, Zuko would just crouch here paralyzed by indecision. This situation right here? This would be exactly why Uncle is always telling Zuko to plan *before* he acts. Not that Zuko has ever been particularly good at that even when he does try. But Agni, he wishes he was. Zuko feels so unmoored right now.

&#45;-

Zuko’s working up the nerve to make himself known when a chittering hiss has his heart stuttering. He knows that noise. He hasn’t heard it in years, but mongoose lizards are rather distinctive. And Zuko has been dreading the sound of one at his back ever since he and Uncle made it off Azula’s ship.

There’s the trap, then. It just isn’t the Avatar's.

Zuko carefully, slowly turns his head, pressing himself flatter into the deep shadows of the alley, good eye scanning back toward the edge of town. He isn’t surprised to see Azula. Not really. But the sight of her still makes his inner flame tense and writhe. Her armor is polished to a high sheen, her hair perfectly tied back, lipstick a bright pink that really isn't her shade but that works anyway, her hands relaxed on the reins. Confidence and power and resources and the attention of the Fire Lord, all wrapped up in one fourteen-year-old body. Zuko struggles to breathe.

“I’m here,” the Avatar calls, tugging Zuko’s attention partway off his sister. Zuko wavers— dangerous, dangerous, dangerous—unsure which threat to keep on his right side. “You’ve caught up with me. Now who are you, and what do you want?”

“You mean the Water Tribe peasant didn’t share his theories?” Zuko goes cold at the arch, amused question. There’s no question which threat is greater. “I could tell that he had some.”

“What?”

“I guess you didn’t spend as much time staring at my brother as he did,” Azula drawls, and Zuko can hear her smirk. “I’ll give you three clues. Who has poor taste in hairstyles, is obsessed with his honor, and can’t use half his face?” Shit. Zuko didn’t realize she had noticed how blurry his vision was on the left. “Come on, it’s okay. You can laugh, it’s funny!”

“…You’re Zuko’s sister?”

“Got it in one! Aren’t you a smart one.” Zuko shudders at her tone even though it’s not directed at him. He knows what happens when Azula sounds like that. Fuck, fuck, fuck. Zuko might not be quite sure what he wants the Avatar *for*, but Zuko knows he needs him either way.

“So what now?” The Avatar finally asks, wary and quiet and not nearly wary enough.

“Now? There’s nothing now, silly. You’re *exhausted*. You have no place to go, no allies, nowhere to hide. It’s over. You can run but I’ll catch you.” Azula sounds like she would enjoy it if he did.

“I’m not running,” Aang says, resolute and finally rising to his feet. Zuko winces, then lets out a controlled exhale, his fire spinning out from his core to press against the underside of his skin, biting and ready. For what, he isn’t sure.

“Do you really want to fight?” Azula seems delighted by that too in a way that Zuko is more than familiar with, in a way that has his body aching with the echo of long-ago blows. He feels trapped, immobile and motionless between two possible paths, overwhelmed by possibilities, inner flame trembling in his grip. He could watch. He could leave. He could just stay out of this because none of this is supposed to matter to him anymore.

But Zuko needs the Avatar. And Azula will take things too far. She always does, especially with someone new, and Zuko can’t just stand here and do *nothing*. And he doesn’t know *what* to do but agonizing over it clearly isn’t getting him anymore.

Zuko takes one last bracing breath and draws his blades, stepping out of the shadows at an angle to keep Azula in his good eye and the Avatar in her periphery. “Yes, Azula. I really do.”

“Zuko!” The Avatar half-shouts, jerking in a way that almost has Zuko setting him on fire. Zuko’s inner flame is spitting and tense at the possibility of those tattoos lighting with spirit energy.

“Zuzu,” Azula laughs. “What a pleasant surprise!” Her grin is full of teeth as she falls into a relaxed, almost lazy firebending stance except for its casual precision. “That’s so sweet. I want to fight you, too.”

For an endless moment they’re frozen, the three of them. Zuko with blades pointed toward both Azula and the Avatar, heart pounding just as hard for either. Azula with two hands raised, lips curled in something that could be a smile. The Avatar with his staff at the ready, eyes darting between the siblings.

Azula strikes first like Zuko knew she would, aiming for him rather than the Avatar, and Zuko expected that too. Her strike sends his feet skidding back over the packed dirt even as her fire breaks around his block. Zuko feels a moment of concern—he’s weaker than he thought from his travels, he should have been able to hold his ground—but quickly shakes it off, sheathing his blades to free his hands for fire now that he knows for sure how this is going to go. There’s no space for doubts, between Azula and the Avatar.

Azula has already moved like a blaze across a summer field by the time Zuko looks up, streaking after the Avatar. The airbender drops out of the air—he *would* try to flee—to spin away her lance of blue flame. The Avatar lands between the siblings, behind Azula, and Zuko reacts on instinct to the threat suddenly so close, punching out a sheet of flame that forces the Avatar to duck down and stay out of the sky.

The Avatar yelps and somersaults below the attack, landing on a porch and giving Zuko a half-fearful, half-wounded look. Zuko stares back for a beat, waiting for those eyes and tattoos to light with power. Both of them throw themselves to the ground instead, clumsy and off-guard as blue flame spears toward them. Zuko comes up hands blazing, launching into a series of hard, precise punches and strikes, closing distance, sliding between offense and defense as sheets of flame and blades of air spin around him.

The fight moves so fast that Zuko has no possibility of thought even if he knew what to think, going from the ground to railings to rooftops to half-standing interiors and back into twisting alleys. Zuko isn’t used to this pace anymore, to asking so much of his body when he’s given it so little for so long. His breaths are starting to rasp in his throat, his flames starting to feel more and more ragged around the edges. He can’t stop, though. He needs to keep Azula at bay, needs to keep the Avatar grounded, needs to keep them both off-balance enough to not hit massacre-causing levels of anger.

But Zuko is finding himself more and more on the defensive, chasing instead of dictating the field of battle until he feels like he’s just hanging onto the edge of their fight, an interloper in a private struggle. It fills his fire with an impotent kind of rage, and it’s almost expected, finally, when Zuko mistimes a block and barely manages to call another shield of fire against dual strikes of air and flame. It’s not enough—it never is—and Zuko flies backward off the awning they’ve worked their way onto.

He collides with a half-rotted shed in a spray of wood shards and dust, going straight through the roof, straight onto a support beam, unable to do more than grunt as solid wood—probably the last solid piece in the whole fucking town—catches him across the back and forces what air he has left out of his body. Zuko crashes to a stop when his body meets the ground, mercifully managing not to skewer himself on the debris.

For a moment all he can do is stare, head ringing and balance swimming, vision fuzzy and soft in that way that would probably be unconsciousness, if Agni ever granted him that relief. Then Zuko gasps in a hard breath in a sudden rush, then another, reinflating his lungs, flexing his fingers and toes to make sure they still work, that nothing is broken. He can feel what has to be a quarter of the town on fire around them against his fire sense, can feel the particular shape of Azula’s blue flames moving further and further away.

The uncontrolled fire in her wake makes something in Zuko feel wild, his inner flame snapping and surging in echo, eating away the exhaustion clinging at his limbs. Zuko bares his teeth at the call of that rising blaze and flips over, intending to rage back toward the seething heart of the town. He doesn’t even get more than halfway to his feet before his body locks into shocked motionlessness, suddenly face to face with Uncle. With Katara. With… some random girl.

With Sokka.

Zuko’s stomach lurches as they gape at him—well, three of them do, the girl doesn’t seem bothered in the slightest. His heat sense rushes outward, reaching for the not-flame blazing bright and loud against his awareness. It touches, light and eager and exhilarating before Zuko yanks it back with enough force to feel the sting of it through his whole body.

“What—”

“No time,” Zuko snaps, for all of them but mostly for Sokka, an explanation and apology all at once as he shoves to his feet and scrambles toward the growing heat of Azula’s fire. Zuko distantly registers pounding feet at his back, gaining on him as he sprints toward a half-collapsed meeting hall and reaches for the fire already climbing the walls. He can see Azula silhouetted against the flames, feet grounded, hands extending into a form Zuko doesn’t need to see more than once to recognize.

“*Fuck.”* Zuko calls flame to hand, tries to whip up the blaze beneath her, knowing it won’t be fast enough with how tired he already is.

“What is it?” Sokka pants from behind him.

“Lightning.”

“On it,” Katara snarls, fresh and energized. Water lashes toward Azula, knocking her hand aside with more precision and control than Zuko has ever seen from the waterbender. Fuck, he'll worry about that later. Azula whirls, reacting so instantaneously it could be choreographed, fire blazing toward Katara even as her body drops smoothly underneath Sokka’s boomerang. She pops into a smooth leap over Aang’s counterattack, then another gliding dodge of the boomerang on its return, casually raising a wall of fire to flick away Zuko’s attack.

What follows would take Zuko’s breath away, if he had any left to give. Azula lunges, spins, kicks, fire streaking from her fingers, from her heels. She bends herself around Sokka’s club, flips over Aang’s blasts of air, sends Katara’s water disappearing into steam as her blue fire superheats the air. Her grin is fierce, sharp, deadly as she shoves fire roaring out in a perimeter around her, everyone stumbling back. She looks immovable, unstoppable, perfect, up until the ground heaves beneath her feet, breaking her stance and sending her to one knee.

“I thought you guys could use a little help,” a voice drawls, and Zuko jerks to put a building at his back and bring this new threat into view without taking his good eye off Azula. It’s the girl from earlier, the one Zuko didn’t recognize. An earthbender then. Probably some prodigy, by the looks of it. She would be.

Movement on his left has Zuko snapping back toward Azula as she darts away in that moment of distraction. Zuko follows without thinking, like he always does, far more familiar with darting through Earth Kingdom alleys than she is. But Azula hasn’t had weeks of sparse rations and sparse water, has always been the fast one. Zuko can’t close the distance between them, is barely keeping her in sight as she whips between narrow passageways. He skids around a corner, nearly shooting fire before he registers her choked-off sound as one of annoyance rather than attack. It takes him a few rapid heartbeats to make the scene make sense—Azula backed into a corner, Uncle blocking her path forward, Sokka and the others coming up behind Zuko to block her retreat.

Azula doesn’t seem phased as they fan out around her, expression amused and mocking even as she retreats before then. “Well look at this,” she says, breathless in that controlled, perfectly trained way. “The gang’s all here. Enemies and traitors—” Her eyes settle on Zuko. “—All working together. Almost like you’ve done it before.” Her gaze shifts to Sokka.

Zuko twitches, he can’t help it, and Azula laughs. “Really, Brother, you have a true talent for finding new ways to make things hard for yourself, don’t you?”

“You’re not in an easy spot yourself, Azula,” Zuko snaps, refusing to take his eyes off her even though his skin itches from the weight of all the stares on his face.

“You’re right, Zuzu.” He tenses at that, at her little twist of a smile. “I know when I’m beaten. A princess surrenders with honor.”

Uncle relaxes at her words, hands lowering and attention shifting, because Uncle has never understood Azula, which means he has always underestimated her. Zuko dives forward, nearly before Azula starts moving but still far too late. Her form is as precise and sharp and powerful as her first strike of the battle, blue fire catching Uncle square in the chest.

“*NO!”* Zuko throws himself across the alley with barely a cursory wall of flame to cover his lunge. Azula lets Zuko pass untouched, turning to face the others as a boomerang, water, earth, air all impact the sphere of fire she whips around herself. There’s a shuddering explosion, smoke filling the air, and Zuko can distantly feel fire suddenly racing uncontrolled over the tinder-dry shell of the city.

He skids to Uncle’s side as the smoke clears, hands hovering and frantic over the burn across Uncle’s chest and arm. Zuko is vaguely aware that Azula’s gone and couldn’t care less about her in this moment. Uncle’s still breathing, thank Agni, but his eyes are closed, skin raw and ugly. Firebenders can handle burns better than most, but Zuko knows that that means nothing when the burn is bad enough. Azula’s flames have always been especially hot.

Crunching feet across the debris of the alley has Zuko twitching into a defensive crouch, scrambling to put Uncle behind the protection of his body. Sokka, Katara, the new girl, and the Avatar are still arrayed across the alley, all of them looking tense and ready to fight. Zuko’s pulse pounds in his ears, inner flame thready, guttering but beginning to gather as Zuko breathes through the idea that he’s going to need to defend Uncle against them, now, after all of this. Zuko doesn’t know where he stands with any of them anymore and the uncertainty sits like acid in his throat. He might have been cast out of the Fire Nation, might have taken Uncle down with him, but that doesn’t mean any of the others *know* that. And Zuko can’t think, can’t find the words, can’t breathe, because Uncle is injured and Sokka is here and Zuko doesn’t know how things *work* anymore between them all.

“Zuko,” Sokka finally says, taking a step forward and rocking to an immediate stop as Zuko’s eyes snap to him. Zuko feels dangerously desperate as he tries to read something on Sokka’s face, any clue of what’s about to happen, of how he’s supposed to act. “Are—”

“Let me see,” Katara demands, water swirling around her hands as she strides forward, eyes thin chips of ice.

Zuko’s heart stops. His fire surges in answer, responding before Zuko can even think of reacting, bursting out in an arc as his hand slices through the air. “*No.”*

Katara falls back in surprise, hands half-raised, and Zuko can feel his face settling in a snarl of warning. His inner flame is burning through his fear, turning toward rage and self-recrimination, and Zuko knows what to do with those, at least. He never should have engaged Azula, never should have left Uncle in the first place, never should have followed the Avatar here as if Zuko ever had a real chance of claiming…something, he doesn’t even know what, and that just makes Uncle’s prone form scald even worse.

“It’s oka—” the Avatar starts to say, taking his own step forward. The flames from the burning buildings flicker off his gray eyes like they’re lit from within and Zuko’s inner flame turns wild with terror.

“Stay back!” He shouts, fire spitting along with his words.

Katara scowls, fingers clenching into fists. “Just get out of the—”

“We just need to—"

“Don’t—”

“Let us—”

“*GO AWAY!”*

The sudden silence trembles with rage and fear and violence. Zuko’s eyes bounce frantically over them, jumping between the Avatar and Katara and the earthbender, skipping over Sokka entirely. Zuko’s already too overwhelmed for anything he might see there.

“Zuko,” Sokka says softly, stepping slowly forward again and waving Katara and Aang back. “Look at me.”

Zuko can’t do that, can’t take his eyes off potential assailants, which Sokka seems to realize because he gestures the others away more forcefully until they finally move back with visible reluctance. The distance loosens Zuko’s tension enough for him to finally meet Sokka’s eyes, though not enough for him to read anything except deep exhaustion on Sokka’s face.

“Is it okay if I come over?” Sokka asks quietly, bending to set his boomerang on the ground, then his knife, reaching out with empty hands.

Zuko stares at Sokka’s palms a moment too long before jerking his head in a tight nod. His fists clench, clumsy and sloppy as he yanks his fire back into his hold. Sokka follows the retreating flames until he’s crouching in front of Zuko, hands extended. Offering. Waiting for Zuko to calm enough to shake the fire off his fingers. Zuko needs to get the fire off his hands. He can’t get near Uncle’s burn if he can’t touch him without flames.

“Can you take a deep breath for me?”

Zuko glares—Sokka sounds like Uncle, acting like Zuko doesn’t know how to breathe. But that thought makes Zuko want to gasp in pain, which makes him realize that his chest is burning, which makes him agree that, probably, he should take a deep breath.

“Zuko, we want to help,” Sokka murmurs, low. Zuko takes a breath, then another, the words sliding off him, unable to penetrate his buzzing thoughts. “Can you let us help?”

Zuko tries. He really tries. But he can’t make his muscles unlock, can’t bring himself to shift aside and bare Uncle’s wounds, to leave him undefended. The air saws in Zuko’s throat, fists clenching convulsively as he tries and fails. His eyes skitter away from Sokka, unable to face whatever disappointment might bloom there that Zuko can’t bring himself to step into that space that used to exist just for them.

Zuko wants to trust him, wants to place himself in Sokka’s hands. But it wouldn’t just be Sokka. And it wouldn’t be just Zuko. He’s willing to risk so much, for Sokka. But not Uncle.

“Zuko…” Sokka whispers, reaching out, and Zuko can’t control his flinch even as his chest flares with immediate regret at the pain that flashes over Sokka’s face. But Zuko can’t let himself be touched right now, not by anyone and especially not by Sokka. Zuko wants it, wants to push into the heat of him and let it burn everything away and he knows he can’t let himself slip like that. Not when Uncle’s breathing is ragged with pain. Not when Uncle is relying on Zuko to keep it together and keep him safe. Not when Zuko might trust Sokka but can’t even imagine letting the others approach and can’t imagine how he’d say no if Sokka asked him with his hands on Zuko’s skin.

“I…” Zuko can’t find his words, his voice, and Sokka bites his lip and that just makes it even harder.

Sokka takes a deep breath, studying his hands before peeking at Zuko from beneath his lashes and *Agni,* it shouldn’t but the glance hits Zuko like a kick to the gut. He has *dreamed* of that look. “Can you—"

“Don’t,” Zuko warns, desperate, pinning his eyes to Sokka’s knees where they’re pressed against the ground—is that any safer to look at? His head is spinning—and catching the aborted movement of Sokka’s hand like it’s about to reach. Zuko can’t be weak right now. “Don’t.”

“Don’t what?” Sokka frowns, shifting like he wants to try touching again, stilling when Zuko tenses.

“Don’t…use this. Please don’t.” Zuko won’t be able to hold out, if Sokka does, won’t be able to deny him anything he asks even if it kills Zuko to give away something he shouldn’t.

“Use…I don’t understand.” Sokka’s words are tight, and Zuko can feel something jagged and sharp that might be a laugh sitting in his throat, at the protest.

“Don’t use *this,*” Zuko presses, finally meeting Sokka’s eyes, feeling like his own must be naked with wanting. “To get what you…Don’t—seduce me—Or…”

“*Seduce* you?” Sokka yelps, jerking back on his heels, face wide open with shock before he leans forward, voice going intense with horror. “Is that what you think? Is that what you fucking think this is?”

“I don’t…” It’s hard to breathe again. Zuko wants to close his eyes, wants to shut this out, feels like he’s being torn slowly apart, but he can’t risk taking his eyes off the alley. “I don’t know, Sokka,” he admits, aware that he’s laying himself far too bare but unable to stop himself from spilling out onto the dirt, undefended and raw. “I don’t know why you would want…what else was I supposed to think after—you weren’t getting anything *back*.”

“I wasn’t getting anything—” Sokka’s bites off his words, hands grasping his hair as if he needs to do something to hold himself together. Zuko understands the feeling. “How can you think that about me? After I—I *told* you about being used like that. I *wrote* to you.”

“About the resistance fighter.”

“…Yeah,” Sokka confirms quietly, his eyes intent on Zuko’s face, searching. Someone makes a strangled little gurgle that Zuko isn’t going to bother with if Sokka isn’t going to worry about it. “About him.”

Zuko exhales a gust of angry heat at the reminder, his inner flame pulling back underneath his skin enough for Zuko to flick the last sparks off his hands. It shouldn’t work like that. Not when his fire is still high and raging inside, because Zuko can still get so mad when he thinks about what happened to Sokka. But something about the shift from tense dread to protective anger is familiar enough, comfortable enough, to let Zuko’s inner fire settle.

“Zuko.” He reluctantly meets Sokka’s eyes again, swallowing a sad little noise at the wounded look there. “Do you really think that?”

“…I don’t know what to think,” Zuko whispers, hating himself for making Sokka hurt, for pleading, knowing he has no right to ask for this. Or anything, really. “I just don’t…why would you—with *me*…”

“I told you why. I wrote that too.”

Zuko remembers. Zuko can never stop remembering, to be honest, even when he knows there’s no point in thinking about it because remembering never changed anything. He still can’t make himself move.

The silence draws out then and Sokka bites his lip, considering. “Zuko, do you trust me?”

Zuko makes himself stop and actually consider, because Sokka deserves that and it’s the least Zuko can give him. “I trust *you*,” Zuko finally says, and he can see the understanding sweep over Sokka’s face, chased quickly by regret and resignation.

“You won’t let us help, will you?” The words are heavy.

“It’s *Uncle*,” Zuko tries to explain, because if anyone can understand what exactly that means to Zuko, how important it is for him to get this right, it would be Sokka.

“…Okay,” Sokka says, slumping and sounding more tired than Zuko has ever heard him. “Okay.”

They’re quiet a moment, Zuko still trembling with tension, Sokka limp and dejected. It’s hard for Zuko to stay on edge with Sokka so loose and close, but he can’t ignore the Avatar hovering at the edge of his vision, Katara at his side. There’s too much long-ingrained anxiety there for Zuko to relax completely. Too much time spent hunting to be able to turn off the instinct, or to be comfortable feeling like prey.

“You need to leave,” Zuko finally says, forcing conviction into his voice even if it comes out softer than he wants. It would be a stronger statement if he could meet Sokka’s eyes, but Zuko can’t seem to look away from the hollow of Sokka’s throat.

“What? Why?”

“You can’t stay here.” Zuko won’t be able to concentrate on Uncle if they’re here. But also… “You don’t know that Azula’s really gone. You should go.”

“We can help defend you,” Sokka says quietly. “Even if you don’t want us near your uncle, we can help with Crazy Blue.”

Zuko’s heart stops, eyes snapping up, voice sharp. “What did you call her?”

Sokka hesitates, uncertainty crossing his face. “…Crazy Blue?”

“You’ve called her that before.” Zuko can’t believe this. “To me.”

“What?” Sokka frowns, leaning back. “No, I haven’t seen you since we first met her in—”

“—Omashu,” Zuko finishes with him. He feels numb. Those things Sokka said in that misty, apparently-not-at-all-imagined place, the things Zuko said back…he doesn’t regret it, he can’t, but Agni, if he knew he could have said so much *more*.

Sokka’s face goes blank before slow realization begins to settle on his features. “Well, fuck,” he finally mutters. “Fuck. Fucking…Spirit shit.”

Zuko feels like this is probably something big, huge and momentous in some way that Zuko doesn’t have the metaphysical or interpersonal understanding to grasp. But also—he doesn’t have time for this. Zuko can’t leave Uncle lying in pain, so he forcefully shunts aside the revelation. He can panic over it later. “You still need to leave.”

“Even more reason for you to come with us,” Sokka scowls, but Zuko can hear that he doesn’t have full conviction behind the words. Sokka still looks wrong-footed from the realization that their shared hallucination was, well…shared.

“I’ll be fine,” Zuko sighs, scrubbing a hand over his face, refusing to think about what his answer would have been if Sokka had asked yesterday. Agni, even an hour ago.

“But…Azula.” Zuko could laugh, at that. Sokka speaks like she is a concern, someone to be wary of. Like he has a vague sense of the threat she represents, without nearly the right amount of horror.

“It’s different for me,” Zuko shrugs, scowling when Sokka flicks an incredulous took to Uncle. “It is. I promise. Just…you need to go. I can’t…” Zuko flicks his eyes toward where Katara and Aang are hovering. “Unless *you’re* staying?”

“No,” Sokka says immediately, sadly. “I can’t leave them.”

Zuko nods his understanding, because he does understand—that’s who Sokka *is—*and forces himself to keep meeting Sokka’s concerned, anxious stare. “So you need to go then. I won’t be the reason she catches you.” The words are all Zuko can offer Sokka, all that he can give.

Sokka absorbs them in silence, frowning down at his hands, finally nodding and blowing out a hard breath. “Do you have what you need? Food and water and medical supplies?”

“Yes.” A firebender always has what he needs to treat burns.

“Stay safe, then,” Sokka whispers, rising to his feet, lingering a moment like he wants to do something more, reach over or say something or just stay. Zuko wants him to stay, more than anything. But he can’t ask Sokka to choose. Not when Zuko never chose him.

“You too,” Zuko whispers, angling his head to keep the others in his periphery but letting Sokka fade into the blurred vision of his left side. Zuko can’t watch him leave while also feeling the subdued brightness of him pulling away from his heat sense. He can’t handle it, not when he already feels like he’s been ripped into pieces, placed at a crossroads between the three things that anchored him to life through weeks floating on the sea and made to realize that they were incompatible with each other, that in the end there’s no choice at all except for Uncle.

&#45;-

“Sokka.”

“Just…leave it, Katara.” His head is thick and muddled with tiredness, overfull with revelations.

“He—” She still can’t really say Zuko’s name without tripping over it, which Sokka usually finds amusing these days. “—said something about a resistance fighter.”

“Katara,” he warns. “Don’t ask if you don’t want to know.”

“Well, *I* want to know.” Toph butts in like she never left, like Sokka didn’t just spend hours of his life panicking that he had lost their newest friend just weeks after finding her.

Sokka and Katara look at each other in shared horror at the idea of talking about Jet. “…No.”

“Later,” Sokka tacks on when Toph huffs, not wanting to reignite the tension from earlier. “When we’ve had time to *sleep*.” The last word comes out like a prayer. Sokka hasn’t stayed away this long since…the Battle for the North, probably. Which isn’t something he likes thinking about.

“Well can you at least tell me why we’re leaving a wounded old guy back there before you go take your nap, Snoozles?”

“Because he wanted us to go,” Sokka sighs, the image of Zuko panicked and shielding Iroh bright and painful in his mind.

“And we just…do what that guy wants all the time?”

Katara lets out a burst of surprised laughter, Aang’s giggle just this side of hysterical. “I wish,” Sokka mutters, then louder. “Not usually. But…he asked us to go.” And Sokka had been helpless in the face of Zuko’s plea, a demand edged with a breakdown that Sokka knows Zuko wouldn’t have wanted seen. Sokka doesn’t fully understand why but for whatever reason Aang and Katara’s presence was shoving Zuko closer and closer to the limits of his control, and for whatever reason Sokka still cares about shielding him from that.

“Didn’t you tell him that we could help, though?” Katara frowns, tiredness exaggerating the expression. Her fingers twitch toward her water skin like she’s barely stopping herself from marching back and forcing a healing on Iroh regardless of Zuko’s wishes.

“Of course I told him,” Sokka snaps. “He didn’t want help.”

“Why not?”

“Because he doesn’t *trust* you.” Sokka regrets the words the minute they slip past his tired brain. They’ve had more than enough sniping at each other, but Tui and La, of *course* Sokka tried to offer their help. What does she think Sokka was *doing*? He braces for a biting comment in response, but Katara doesn’t push back, her mouth snapping shut and face twisting with something that looks marginally close to regret.

“So…” Toph sounds like she’s about to kick over a small avalanche and is looking forward to it. “Anyone want to tell me about that, then?”

“Huh?” Aang asks eloquently.

“You knew that guy. Sokka’s heartbeat was going craaaazy. And so was Sparrowkeet’s back there.”

“*Sparrowkeet?”* Aang gasps, half-horrified, half-delighted.

“His heart was going a mile a minute the whole time,” Toph shrugs. “It felt like my mom’s pet sparrowkeets used to.”

“Sparrowkeet,” Aang whispers in awe, turning to Sokka with wide eyes as Katara covers a smirk. Sokka just drops his head into his hands, trusting that someone will stop him if he is about to walk into anything dangerous.

“So why were their hearts going off like that?” Toph presses. Sokka can only imagine what she was feeling with those feet of hers. Seeing Zuko again like that, unexpected and fighting and wearing *green* and with *hair*. It was a shock, to say the least.

And to fight *beside* Zuko instead of against him? Sokka had barely had time to think in the midst of it all, to absorb what it was like, but those brief moments had lit him on fire. And then seeing Zuko and Crazy Blue—*Azula*, he reminds himself, *it’s Azula?* It had been brief but eye-opening. Sokka had recognized the cast of her features back in Omashu but seeing the way they interacted, seeing the prodigy Zuko had written of in the flesh, the way she taunted Zuko—and Sokka’s stomach lurches, that *he* was the thing she had taunted him with —it had all been horrifying and fascinating in equal parts. A lot of things about Zuko suddenly made a lot more sense.

Sokka sighs when he realizes that Aang and Katara are still stumbling through an explanation for Toph that includes a lot of ‘well you see’ and ‘so you know how the Fire Nation is after Aang.’ “He’s someone that I used to know,” he cuts in, rolling his eyes at Katara’s relieved glance.

“Seems like someone you all used to know,” Toph points out, skeptical.

“Sure,” Sokka laughs humorlessly. “I guess you could say that.”

Toph lapses into silence for a moment, long enough that Sokka can feel his mind starting to drift towards a state that’s dangerously close to sleeping on his feet.

“So…” Toph trails off and Sokka tilts his head to show he is listening. “Were you doing it?”

“*What?”*

“You know,” she grins as Aang makes a choked sound and Katara slaps her hands over her ears. “Knocking boots. The old in and out. Buttering the biscuit. Did you *know* him?”

“No!”

“He said you *seduced* him,” Toph points out, drawing out the word with relish as Sokka flinches from not-nearly-recent-enough pain and fear and frustration. Toph can read heartbeats, but she apparently can’t read the emotion behind them.

“I—That—Don’t—”

“But you wanted to.” She sounds absolutely thrilled to be teasing him.

“Drop it, please,” Katara begs, hands over her ears. “I don’t want to hear this about my brother!”

“That wasn’t a ‘no,’ Sokka,” Toph sing-songs. Sokka just groans, covering his face, cheeks on fire. This is cripplingly embarrassing in the worst way, even more so because part of Sokka thinks that it’s actually…nice, in a way. To have this thing with Zuko be an object of teasing and fun instead of guilt and shame. That part feels good—in a wildly inconvenient way, considering Toph can hear his heartbeat—but Sokka’s tired and exhausted and unprepared to see Zuko and just…can’t stop thinking about it, now that the floodgate is open.

Zuko had looked…not good, exactly. But familiar. Barely restrained motion, molten eyes, firebender heat pressing out like a touch. Zuko had looked the way he did in that swamp hallucination, *just* like he did then, which…fucking Spirit mumbo jumbo. It was the same clothes, the same dust, the same hair even if it was a bit longer now and Sokka *still* can’t get over the way that cap of thick black hair softens Zuko’s face and takes the edge off his ever-present glare. Would it feel the same between his fingers as it had back in the swamp, if Sokka had reached out and touched it?

The thought makes his heart pound a little quicker—he refuses to look at Toph when she lets out a little bark of laughter. Somehow, impossibly, that vision had been *real*. Sokka has encountered stranger things by this point when it comes to spirits, but something about sharing that experience, and sharing it with Zuko of all people, makes his head spin. The things Zuko had said, the naked vulnerability on his face and in the way he chased Sokka’s touch. The fact that Zuko had openly regretted not choosing a different path. Would he have ever admitted that if he thought Sokka was actually listening?

It’s a dangerous thing to think about when Sokka knows that Zuko was in that fight with Azula and Aang but doesn’t quite know what Zuko was fighting *for*. It’s risky, when Sokka is trying so hard to hold onto the conviction that he deserves happiness, that he deserves someone who will choose him back. And Zuko hadn’t exactly reached for Sokka back there. He had basically begged Sokka not to make him choose in that moment. And Sokka could give Zuko that, a reprieve from bringing whatever there was still between them to a head when he was clearly panicking over his uncle’s injury. A part of Sokka had even been relieved to be the one to walk away this time—fuck, that he *could* walk away—even as the memory of leaving Zuko alone and cradling his uncle tightens his throat.

Aang appears at his side as if summoned by his worries. “Are you okay?”

“Yeah,” Sokka assures him, managing to summon a half-smile. “Are you?”

“I’m fine,” Aang says, twisting his glider in his hands. “She’s scary.”

Sokka just grunts at that. ‘Scary’ doesn’t quite do Azula justice.

“I did want to say,” Aang begins slowly, privately, like he isn’t quite sure if his words will be welcome. “I don’t think Zuko was fighting to hurt me.”

“That’s good,” Sokka mutters, suddenly feeling the weight of his exhaustion. Not trying to hurt Aang isn’t at all the same as helping him, as being on their side. Sokka might forgive himself more easily for it these days, but he’s still tired of his heart battering itself against hopeless things.

“I just thought you should know.”

“Whatever you’re saying to Sokka,” Toph calls from behind them. “Say it louder! I want to hear whatever is making his heart do that.”

“Leave him be,” Katara chastises, too tired to put any real bite behind it.

“You guys are no fun,” Toph pouts, kicking at the road and sending a small boulder rocketing off into the brush.

“Toph,” Sokka calls back, reaching for some levity because they finally seem to be in an okay place and he can’t have this sliding back into tension. “You couldn’t handle how fun I can be.”

She perks up instantly. “With Sparrowkeet back there?”

Sokka lets his smirk into his voice. “I never kiss and tell.”

“No one will tell me anything,” Toph wails, stomping loose another boulder and only partially faking her outrage. Katara laughs, speeding up to bump his shoulder and Sokka lets himself take the moment to enjoy the loud sound of their banter and feel nothing but pure relief that somehow all the people he holds in his heart are still alive.

## Chapter 7: Wasted Potential

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

No particular warnings for this one!

### Text

Zuko knows a lot about burns, and a lot about Uncle, which is how he knows that Uncle will have what he needs to care for his injury beyond. Zuko stays motionless until he feels Sokka finally leaving the edge of his heat sense, unable to move until he knows they’re safely away. Safely for who, he can’t think about.

It takes longer than he expects, and Zuko doesn’t know what to make of that and can’t think about it either even if he did. There’s no time as he throws himself into what needs to be done: tracking down Jasmine—Uncle dropped his travel bag next to her because of course he did—making Uncle comfortable, putting out the fires in what remains of the town, and scouting out a place to go to ground until Uncle is well enough to move.

The work lasts him nearly the entire afternoon, and once it’s done Zuko abruptly runs up against how bad he is at *waiting*, especially when he can’t risk indulging his thoughts right now. He’s hovering, fretting, unable to concentrate but not wanting to take his attention off Uncle, anxious and scared and thrown back far too strongly to how it felt to be helpless by Sokka’s sickbed, which is its own risk to think about right now.
