“What,” Zuke snaps, jerking around to scowl at Uncle.

“Why are you glaring at the Shens?”

“I’m *not*,” Zuko growls. He was just glaring at the wall. The one the Shens happen to be seated in front of.

“They come in every day,” Uncle sighs. “They order the same thing. They give you exact change.” In other words, Zuko’s favorite customers. “Is something bothering you?”

“This entire fucking shop,” Zuko mutters. He can’t believe Uncle even has to ask.

“Something new,” Uncle clarifies patiently, and Zuko only glowers at the prying and goes to find a new pencil, stalking back onto the floor and ignoring the coworker who has to dance around him to avoid slamming into Zuko and dropping his tray.

&#45;-

They finally give up and shove Zuko into the back—thank Agni—to brew tea. Which wouldn't have been Zuko’s first choice, but it’s not the worst move since at least he won’t be scaring off any more customers.

Except maybe Zuko has a knack for that, even off the floor, because somehow all the tea he brews is ending up burnt and bitter. Even though he’s using the same stovetop and the same timers as everyone else. Almost as if Zuko’s water is getting hotter.

”*Nephew*,” Uncle whisper-shouts. Zuko flinches at the bite in it, instinctively responding with a startled glare. “When one plays pai sho, the pattern of tiles may seem random. The actions of your opponent may seem opaque. But one can always discern some truth about an opponent’s mindset in the pieces, and reveal truths about yourself, in turn.”

“…What.” Zuko rarely has a head for untangling Uncle’s oblique brand of advice, and he has even less attention for it today.

“Whatever it is that’s going on—and you don’t need to tell me what it is—take a deep breath. And pull back your fire.”

“I’m not—”

“That water is boiling nicely, Nephew.”

“It’s *tea*—”

“The stove is off.”

Zuko stares. Then he leans back to check that—yup, the stove isn’t even lit underneath his cheerfully bubbling teapot. Zuko pulls on a scowl as he yanks his heat sense back toward his core, knowing that he looks like a petulant child but unable to stop himself. Fuck. *Fuck.* He hasn’t slipped in a way that Uncle would notice in a long time.

“Do you need a break to mediate?” Uncle asks seriously, eyes searching Zuko’s face in open concern.

“I need a break from being here ever again,” Zuko snaps, the words automatic as he squirms away from acknowledging the vulnerability, the loss of control that Uncle plainly sees.

“Take deep breaths,” Uncle suggests, settling in like he’s going to stay here until Zuko starts demonstrating that he knows how to breathe.

“I don’t need to meditate,” Zuko hisses, prickling under the sensation of being overly seen. Zuko is fine, his fire sense is fine, everything is fine. His inner flame is just shoving against the edges of his skin, eager to stretch out and reach for the shape of Sokka, and it’s taking far more concentration than it should to hold it back. It’s *fine.*

&#45;-

Uncle drags Zuko away from the stovetops when their boss starts fiddling with the timers, trying to understand how they could all suddenly be malfunctioning. He shoves Zuko into the back corner at the sinks on dishwashing duty, which is where Zuko’s wanted to be from the moment he started his first shift in this place anyway.

Except Zuko isn’t in a state right now to do anything but resent the way it's taking too much of his focus to keep the water from steaming, but not enough attention to keep his mind occupied. Zuko’s thoughts are racing, racing, racing between possibilities and worries, between things he won’t let himself hope for and the memory of Sokka against his tongue, between the terrifying feeling that he has something fragile within his reach and the sticky fear that he has no idea how to grab onto it without breaking it.

“Zuko.”

He jerks in surprise to hear his name spoken here, eyes darting up around the kitchen to find them alone.

“You can always talk to me,” Uncle says, voice low and grave. “If something is bothering you.”

Zuko grunts and turns back to the sink, carefully pulling back the temperature of the water now that Uncle is at his shoulder, busying his hands with scrubbing the last bit of charcoal from beneath his fingernails.

“I know this is hard for you—”

“I don’t want to talk about it,” Zuko cuts in, making the words firm and sharp. He doesn’t want to hear it, not when Zuko knows for a fact that Uncle has no idea what it is that Zuko’s so tied up about.

“You are not yourself, today,” Uncle sighs. “I just want to help, if I can.”

Zuko takes a deep breath, then just shakes his head, refusing to turn around. He focuses on scrubbing the charcoal from his hands and listens for the sound of Uncle’s footsteps finally retreating back onto the shop floor. He can’t give Uncle what he wants right now. Not when Zuko has been more *himself* today than he’s been in…weeks.

Uncle wants him to be a Good Nephew and Zuko has been trying, he *has.* But he can’t hold himself into that shape right now. Not when he’s nearly crawling out of his own skin from needing to keep everything inside himself from showing. Zuko can’t focus on doing the things he’s supposed to do when it’s taking so much to hold his inner flame in check. All he can think about is the slow passage of Agni across the sky, a lodestone he can feel in his veins, marking each degree closer to nightfall.

&#45;-

Zuko’s shift is done early, which is a relief for everyone involved. He reflexively reaches for Agni’s position in the sky as he hangs up his apron and abruptly grinds to a stop, fingers twisted in the fabric. It’s not quite night yet but it’s close, and now that it’s a matter of minutes and not hours, Zuko’s anticipation is turning to fear. What if Sokka isn’t there? What if Zuko waits and has nothing to show for it but the cold company of the moon? What if Sokka *is* there, but just to tell Zuko—what, to go? To get out of Ba Sing Se? That he’s turning them into the Dai Li?

Zuko unlocks his white-knuckled grip on his apron one finger at a time, ignoring the side-eyed glances from the kitchen staff and stalking for the door. He hesitates as he exits the shop, letting his eyes adjust to the late afternoon sun after the dim kitchen lighting. It will be time soon. Shit, should he try to clean up? He just worked a full day, and he was taking orders so there’s probably charcoal on his face again. Should he change? What would he even wear, though, all he has are works clothes in shitty Earth Kingdom colors…

Movement in his periphery has Zuko shifting instinctively to take in the threat on his left. Except it's not a threat, or a random person on the street. It’s Sokka, already by the mouth of the alley, watching him, and Zuko’s brain goes completely blank. Zuko can only stare, motionless and barely breathing until a distant shout from inside the shop has him jerking back into motion away from the possibility of being called back inside.

He crosses over to Sokka, yanking his inner fire back as it dances and coils in on itself in a combination of nervous anticipation and delight. Sokka stays against the wall, watching Zuko approach, and since that’s apparently what they’re doing Zuko takes the opportunity to look at Sokka, too, like he didn't wholly get to this afternoon. The wolf tail and undercut are familiar, the forced casualness of his slouch against the wall less so. Sokka’s fingers pick at the edge of his wrist wraps and Zuko latches onto the motion, following the expanse of bare skin up Sokka’s arms, eyes jumping to the triangle of chest revealed by his loose summer-weight tunic. Zuko wants to press his mouth to that spot. Zuko wants—his breath hitches as he gets close enough to see what might be the upper edge of reddened fingerprints on the edge of that triangle, just visible if you look closely enough.

“Hey,” Sokka breathes, voice husky.

“Hi.”

They stare for Zuko doesn’t know how long. Some part of him is sure they look ridiculous, gazing at each other like this unmoving from only a pace apart. But Zuko is content for now to just look into those blue eyes and let himself realize over and over, with a jolt of amazement each time, that he isn’t dreaming. That Sokka is actually here.

“How was the rest of your shift?” Sokka finally asks, stirring from his slouch to stand upright.

“Terrible,” Zuko says absently, focusing on the way late afternoon sunlight is now streaking Sokka’s hair.

“Oh.” Sokka blinks. “I’m sorry to—”

“It’s always terrible.”

“Oh.” There’s something like laughter in Sokka’s voice. Zuko doesn’t quite know why, but something in his chest flutters all the same at making it happen.

Sokka clears his throat. “Did you have a place in mind to…talk?” That thing in his chest does a little flip at the extra hesitation it took for Sokka to be able to make the question sound neutral. Oh, Zuko’s inner fire wants to *burn.*

“Yeah.” Zuko takes a few steps into the street before pausing, uncertain if he’s supposed to take Sokka’s hand, or usher him along, or…something. He briefly and intensely panics before just pivoting and walking away, and fuck, that’s probably the worst option of all of them. Agni’s tits, Zuko is so *bad* at this.

Except Sokka falls easily into step beside him, and something about that makes the thing in Zuko’s chest feel tight and light at the same time. It makes Zuko want more. He wants to hold Sokka’s hand. He remembers how it felt in that other lifetime, to walk with Sokka’s fingers laced between his own, marking Sokka as his and Zuko as taken in turn. He barely let himself think about it after, but Zuko’s skin and subconscious and fire remembered.

But Zuko doesn’t reach out even though his palms itch for it more and more with every step they take. Sokka has an air of careful, forced casualness about him, and his face is a mix of concentration and worry whenever Zuko sneaks a sideways glance. Zuko doesn’t think he should try to breach Sokka’s tension with touch, just yet.

Besides, Zuko isn’t positive that he could touch Sokka right now and still talk, and not…*talk*.

Zuko brings them to one of the secluded little squares that Jin had shown him, a bit out of the way and rundown, with high walls built up around it instead of nice views. It’s not the prettiest place in the city, but it’s always been private whenever Zuko has come here with and without her, windowless walls and open space and straggling plants that are surviving even though no one seems to be caring for them anymore.

Sokka takes it in with a quick glance and Zuko pretends he isn’t anxiously trying to read Sokka’s reaction. Fuck, he’s acting like this is some special place, which it isn’t, it’s just a spot he knows. But bringing Sokka here…Zuko wants him to be relaxed, happy, pleased. Wants Sokka to be comfortable wherever Zuko brings him, wherever Sokka is.

Sokka gives him a quick, unreadable glance before making his way to the lone bench, sitting down with a sigh. Zuko wants to sit next to him, to share that space with him. But he knows he needs to see Sokka’s face more, for this, so he sits on the edge of the stone planter instead, crossing his legs awkwardly in the almost-lotus style he is trying to get used to so Jin will stop teasing him about how he sits. Once he's settled, though, Zuko suddenly finds the prospect of looking into Sokka’s eyes too overwhelming. He stares down at his own bouncing knee, at where he is fidgeting with his cuffs, at where Sokka is picking at his wrist wraps again. Fuck, Zuko can't seem to force himself to sit still but he's unwilling to get up and pace as his eyes finally settle on the heartbeat at the hollow of Sokka’s throat.

Agni’s balls, he feels like he’s going to combust on the spot before they even say anything.

Sokka breaks the silence first, because he’s always been the brave one. “So…what did you want to talk about?”

“Um. I don’t…know?” Zuko definitely can’t look Sokka in the eyes now, but he can still see his pulse jump.

“...What?”

“I…didn’t want to see you leave. Not when…I didn’t know if you were coming back.” The words are painfully honest and Zuko swallows his discomfort over being so bare. Honesty might be all he has to give Sokka, as much of it as is his to offer.

Sokka doesn’t react for a long moment, during which Zuko dies a thousand times, before he suddenly seems to deflate, letting out a sigh and running a hand through his hair. “We should still talk, though.”

Zuko nods, biting his lip as his inner fire spikes with anxiety. He knows that they need to, that this is the whole reason they’re here. He is painfully aware that there are too many raw edges and bleeding wounds between them to proceed blindly like they did before. But, “I’m…not sure where to start.” All of Zuko’s emotions are crowding into his throat, messy and tangled and ready to spill out.

“How about with why you’re here?”

Zuko glances around the square.

“I mean in Ba Sing Se.”

“Oh. Um. Okay.” Zuko can feel himself flushing and that just makes him flush more. “Uncle and I came here as refugees.” He only hitches a little over the word. He’s had a long time to get used to it, especially in Ba Sing Se when it’s all that he is to most people. “It was hard being fugitives, outside the walls. He wants to start over, and…” Zuko shrugs. “A teashop is his dream, so…here we are.”

Sokka is staring at him in a blank, uncomprehending way that makes Zuko want to keep talking even though he has no idea what he would say. “Fugitives,” Sokka finally repeats, careful, like he’s testing a new word.

“Yeah.” Zuko looks at his own feet now, needing the brief respite of hiding from Sokka’s reaction, because *that* word is as fresh and painful as it’s ever been. “I’m…not really a Prince anymore. I guess.”

Which should be a good thing, because isn’t that what Sokka has always wanted? For Zuko to not be Fire Prince? But Sokka is frowning, brow twisted, so maybe Zuko read that wrong, too, along with everything else. “How long…”

“Since the North.”

Sokka's jaw briefly tightens as he gives a slow nod, face flickering in a way Zuko can’t quite parse. Is Sokka remembering? Because Zuko is, and...maybe it’s as hard for him as it is for Zuko. Is Sokka locked in his own memories of that time? Or are they both thinking about and flinching away from the same things: Katara unconscious on the ground—Zuko’s heart had stopped, when she dropped. Zuko plunging into a snowstorm with nothing but some rope and the Avatar on his back. Of that all-too-short moment of warmth in each other’s arms at the edge of the ice.

When Sokka finally speaks his words are careful, face opaque, voice tense with...something. “Does that mean that you’re…done?”

“With what?”

“With your…quest. For your…honor.” So, so careful. Like Sokka knows exactly what kind of bomb he’s skirting around.

Zuko closes his eyes. It still hurts to remember what he used to have. What he forced himself to leave behind. It makes him feel dangerously adrift to remember that he has no honor anymore, no place outside of the space Uncle makes for him. “I don’t…I just want Uncle to be happy. I can’t—that’s all I…all I can want.”

Zuko hears Sokka’s breathing stutter and his eyes snap open, but not fast enough to catch the expression leaving Sokka’s face as he nods in understanding and stares down at his wrist wraps, brow furrowed. Zuko wants to smooth that indent away, fingertips tingling with the need. He wants to understand what about his words just hit home.

Zuko exhales, controlled and deliberate, and spools his fire back toward his center. His fingertips are tingling from that, too. “What about you?”

“Hm?”

“Why are you here?” Sokka had said things this afternoon, but Zuko hadn’t exactly been focused on them once he had enough information to realize that Sokka was alone, wasn’t trying to hunt them down, and that the Avatar wouldn’t be showing up in the immediate future.

Sokka hesitates, searching his face, before he finally says, “There are some things I can’t tell you. We aren’t really telling anyone yet who doesn’t need to know,” Sokka hurries to add when Zuko can't suppress his wince. "It’s not because I don’t trust you”

“You *shouldn’t* trust me.”

“…Why not?”

Zuko frowns at Sokka’s genuine-sounding curiosity, his eyes flickering up to meet Sokka's in his surprise. “Why would you?”

Sokka tugs on his wolf tail, expression going thoughtful, which...is not what Zuko expected. “Are you lying to me?”

“No.” Even if he wanted to, Zuko’s pretty sure there's no way he could get away with it with Sokka. He can't even get away with it with total strangers.

“So why wouldn’t I trust you?”

“I’m not…” Zuko flounders, wondering if they’re sharing the same reality. “I’m your enemy.”

“But you aren’t doing that anymore,” Sokka challenges softly, eyes staying intent on Zuko’s face even as Zuko blinks, stutters, gapes back at him.

Agni’s balls, Zuko is utterly speechless at the reminder of all the things he doesn’t have anymore, delivered so gently. But also from the sudden realization, looking at Sokka, of what it could *mean* to not have those things anymore. It isn’t something Zuko lets himself think about often. Or ever, really. He always burns it away into his inner fire the minute those thoughts try to rise in him, because there’s no point in wasting his energy on useless wondering about things Zuko can’t have and choice Zuko can’t undo.

Except Sokka is sitting in front of him, right now. Here. Guarded, but listening. So maybe there is a choice here, one Zuko never thought he would have again.

“If you don’t give me a reason not to trust you then there won’t be a problem,” Sokka shrugs, a quiet order, like it’s that simple and easy. And maybe to Sokka it is. Maybe to him it’s always been that plain, and that’s why it seemed hurt him so deeply when Zuko couldn’t see it the same way.

“…Okay,” Zuko agrees when he can finally find his voice again, dizzy with the idea that his word alone might be enough for Sokka. That Zuko could say something like that and Sokka —suspicious, smart, observant, brilliant Sokka—would believe him.

“Good.” Sokka takes a deep breath, fingers picking at his wrist wraps again, and—did he used to do that so much? “Okay, so. We’re here for one reason. Well, two, I guess.” Zuko scrambles to remember his original question. “We need to meet the Earth King. Partly for Avatar stuff.”

Zuko flinches slightly and Sokka hesitates, but Zuko just shakes his head because he doesn’t want to explain, he just wants to shrug off the unsteadiness of his pulse and the smell of blasting jelly that he *knows* isn’t actually there.

Sokka looks uncertain, pressing his lips together and giving Zuko a close look before finally continuing. “Right now, we’re mostly here because we’re looking for Appa.”

“How did you lose a sky bison,” Zuko wonders. The specifics hadn’t been particularly important this afternoon, but now Zuko can’t help but remember the *size* of the thing. Multiple tons of muscle and fur and legs. Not exactly a creature made for stealth.

“Technically he was stolen,” Sokka mutters, looking some mixture of worried and put out by the fact.

“Ah. Yeah, that would work,” Zuko frowns, cataloging all the logistics that would need to go into something like that with the efficiency of years of experience.

“Huh?”

Zuko glances up from calculating how much rope you would need to source to make a big enough net and freezes under confused blue eyes. Fuck. This isn’t what Zuko does anymore. He needs to remember that. “…Nothing.”

“No, what did you mean,” Sokka presses, curious.

Zuko…should probably try to get out of this question. It would be smart to find a way around this. But it’s been a long day, and Zuko isn’t good at lying to start with, and it’s not like Sokka isn’t more than acquainted with this part of him. “I thought of that. At one point. But it was going to be too complicated. So. I didn’t bother with it.”

“…You thought about stealing Appa?”

Zuko shrugs, even though the answer is yes, studiously avoiding Sokka’s eyes. “If you want to capture the Avatar, taking his companion is a pretty good way to make him come to you. His spirit companion,” he adds after a moment. They both know that Aang never came for Sokka, and Zuko wonders if his inner fire will ever stop flaring, tight and angry, at that fact.

Sokka’s mouth works silently for a moment, expressions flickering too fast for Zuko to catch in the fading light before finally settling somewhere between incredulous and bemused as he lets out a little half-laugh. “Of course. Of course, you thought about that. You thought about everything."

“I…”

“I don’t think Appa got taken for that reason, though,” Sokka says over whatever nothing Zuko was about to offer up. “We don’t know where he is, so if they’re trying to lure Aang somewhere they’re not doing a good job of it.”

That…isn’t entirely true. “You know the sky bison is in Ba Sing Se,” Zuko points out carefully.

“Yeah, but it’s a gigantic city.”

And for some people, it’s probably enough to have the Avatar grounded and in one generally known location, especially one as full of eyes as Ba Sing Se. Taking away the mobility the sky bison affords is huge. But Sokka already looks worried and anxious enough, so Zuko tries to shift into some moderately helpful mode instead of pilling on more bad-news hypotheticals. “Can you get help from the government?” Zuko finds it hard to believe that the administrative network here isn’t fully aware of every single thing that crosses the city walls.

“The people in charge have not exactly been forthcoming,” Sokka mutters, scowling.

“No,” Zuko snorts. “They wouldn’t be.” He doesn’t like the idea of Sokka encountering any of the power brokers in this city, quickly glances over Sokka for injury even though Zuko had him mostly naked a few hours ago and intellectually knows he’s fine. “Be careful.”

“Why? Do you know something?”

Zuko shrugs. He knows lots of things, most of them useless. Sokka is going to need to be more specific than that.

“What about—have you heard of the Do Lai?”

“Dai Li.”

“Yeah, them. What’s their deal? No one will give us a straight answer.”

Zuko likes the idea of Sokka trying to talk to the people in charge even less than he did thirty seconds ago. “They’re a secret police force made entirely of earthbenders.”

Sokka frowns, and Zuko can practically see his brain shuffling and rearranging pieces of the puzzle. “It can’t be very secret if you know about it.”

“Sometimes the most effective secret police are the ones that everyone knows about.” Then they don’t even have to be present for their presence to be felt.

Zuko watches Sokka digest that, his eyes flicking between Sokka’s face and the restless way he is still fiddling with the edge of his wrist wraps. Zuko is almost certain that Sokka never did that on the *Wani.* “What’s their deal, then? Who do they report into?”

Zuko *really* doesn’t want Sokka to go digging into the Dai Li. “Technically, the Earth King.”

“And actually?”

Zuko shrugs. “They have power without accountability and they’re beholden only to themselves. You don’t want to mess with them.”

“No,” Sokka agrees after a moment, but there’s inexplicably a little smile on his lips, like something Zuko said relaxed him instead of making him more cautious. Which…doesn’t make any sense, and is mildly concerning even if Zuko does like to see the tension leaving the set of Sokka’s shoulders.

They lapse into silence and Zuko’s thoughts bubble up, automatic and unwelcome. The sky bison has been missing for weeks, it sounds like, and the Avatar has been in Ba Sing Se at same time as Zuko for who knows how long. There’s an instinctive urgency that wants to rise in him, a shot of adrenaline and burst of misaligned purpose that has Zuko tensing against the need to move and take action. It would be easy, to find the Avatar like this. But Zuko also remembers how it felt back in that no-name town, fighting because he needed the Avatar without being entirely certain what for, feeling like he somehow had a single goal that could spin him down so many different paths.

Sitting in front of Sokka, staring into clear blue eyes, Zuko finds it’s easy enough—practiced enough—to focus on what’s in front of him and shove back down the remnants of who he used to be. Though Sokka is studying his face rather closely, and Zuko is suddenly nervous over what his expression might have been showing. What if this is some sort of test? Agni, is this Zuko’s one chance to somehow convince Sokka to come back again tomorrow? Only this time Zuko has nothing but his own words to work with, which he’s never been any good at.

It’s Sokka who breaks the silence again, cutting through the growing clamor in Zuko’s head. “So. What do you want?”

Zuko goes motionless against a bolt of completely ungrounded anxiety that Sokka could somehow see into his thoughts, somehow knows that Zuko still wavers. “…What do you mean?”

“Zuko…” He tries to ignore the shiver that comes with hearing his name on Sokka’s lips. “If we’re both here. In Ba Sing Se. And if you’ve…left certain things behind. What does that mean?” Sokka wets his lips. “What do you want?”

“Oh.” Relief and disbelief and something like giddiness make Zuko feel briefly disconnected from his own body. “Oh. Yes. Okay. Yes.” He can barely think through the way his inner fire is turning backflips in his stomach.

“…That’s not an answer,” Sokka points out, but with reluctant laughter in his voice more than annoyance, so it's probably fine.

“Right. Sorry.” Zuko musters his courage and holds his breath but then he can’t speak, so he slowly reaches for Sokka’s hand, giving him plenty of time to pull back if he doesn’t want this, if Zuko is misreading everything. Agni, Zuko feels Sokka’s cool skin beneath his fingers like a bell tolling through his entire body. “Sorry,” he says again, blankly. “I’m not…good with words.”

Sokka exhales hard, shaky. “You are very good with words, Zuko,” he says, voice hoarse in a way that has Zuko wanting to wrap all his limbs around him. “Trust me.”

Zuko looks into Sokka’s eyes, dark blue with emotion, remembering all the sentences they spilled onto page after page for each other, burned into his brain even if they were lost to the ocean like everything else. The bare brush of Sokka’s skin against his finger could set him on fire. “Not at saying them out loud, then.”

Sokka takes a deep breath and then slowly turns his hand to press palm to palm against Zuko’s, not lacing their fingers together but pressing his fingertips against the underside of Zuko’s wrist instead. “Okay. Does that mean you want to…try? This, I mean, whatever this…”

Zuko nods, eyes fixed on their hands. He doesn’t know what to call what’s between them either, but he wants to reach for it so badly. And with Sokka’s hand trembling under his, it feels like Zuko might actually be able to hold onto whatever it is if he can just try hard enough.

“Okay,” Sokka exhales, laughing slightly, fingertips pressing almost imperceptibly harder and Zuko’s inner fire is spinning, spinning, spinning around the sensation. “Good. That’s…good. But first I…I need to have a talk.”

Zuko glances up in confusion. What, exactly, does Sokka call what they’ve just been doing?

“With the others,” Sokka clarifies.

Zuko can’t hold back a flinch at that. Everything in him pulls away from the idea of someone as sharp and cutting as Katara, or as dangerous and unpredictable as the Avatar, being even distantly exposed to the soft, vulnerable parts of him. “Can’t we just…”

“No,” Sokka cuts in, gentle but immovable. “We can’t do this if it’s a secret, Zuko. *I* can’t do that. Not again.” Zuko winces again, this time at the edge of not-so-old pain in Sokka’s voice. Proof of how much Zuko managed to hurt him without even trying. Of how much they hurt each other, really, because Zuko can still feel the echo of terror and hurt in his own chest if he ever lets himself go quiet for long enough to hear it.

“Okay,” Zuko finally sighs. “That…makes sense.” And it’s not like Sokka is asking for his permission. Not if Zuko wants to see him again. “But do…do I need to tell Uncle?”

“Only if you want to.” The words are a relief, because that means ‘no,’ which means Zuko can continue pretending for at least a little while longer that he's the person Uncle wants him to be.

Silence drifts down again, less fraught this time, less full of hectic, chaotic thoughts. They sit with their hands pressed together in the dark, both of them staring down at that point of contact. Zuko marvels at the coolness of Sokka’s skin when he’s so blazing bright against Zuko’s heat sense. He admires the shape of Sokka’s callused, tan hands, all broad fingers and blunt nails next to Zuko’s pale skin.

“What now?” Zuko whispers, finally giving in to the urge to brush his thumb along the edge of Sokka’s palm.

“I need to go talk to the others.”

“Tonight?” Zuko doesn’t want Sokka to go. Is aware that Sokka probably needs to. The longer they stay here, the more they do first, the harder Sokka’s conversation is going to be.

“Yeah. And then…I’ll come back. Either way, I’ll come back and let you know.”

“When?” Zuko feels like he’s drowning under the fact that there are two ways that this could go, and one of them is the very real possibility that the next time Zuko sees Sokka could be the last time. His fingers spasm against the urge to tighten around Sokka’s wrist and never let go.

“The day after tomorrow? That’s the soonest I have time to come back down here…”

It’s so far away. Endlessly far away. But Zuko beats back the part of himself that wants to protest, to demand more, to cling. He knows that Sokka has his own life, his own thing. His own purpose that goes beyond showing up at a teahouse every day to make someone else happy. “Okay. I’ll…be waiting.”

Zuko glances up when Sokka’s fingers twitch and is caught off guard by the expression of pure delight that flashes over Sokka’s face. Zuko doesn’t understand why Sokka looks quite so pleased by…whatever Zuko just said or did. But once again, Zuko is more than happy to be the cause of it.

&#45;-

It’s full dark by the time Sokka makes it back to the Upper Ring. The wide streets are empty except for occasional servants hurrying about, their downturned faces and averted eyes still sitting uncomfortably despite how long Sokka’s been in Ba Sing Se already. He doesn’t like it and doesn’t particularly need more discomfort on top of what he’s already carrying and walking toward. His head is spinning, body exhausted from a day of walking in the sun, emotions thin and taut after swinging between passion and fear and worry and now a dangerously enticing hope. Sokka can’t quite bring himself to shove it down just yet even though he learned months ago to push that kind of thing away.

A not insignificant part of him is still convinced that the whole day is going to turn out to be some overly elaborate dream, that any second now he will wake up alone in his ridiculously large bedroom. The larger part of him won’t stop shouting that this is real, that it actually happened and is still actually happening. That’s the voice that getting louder and more insistent, clamoring to be heard over churning nerves and fragments of anxiety with every step Sokka takes toward their house.

Zuko is in Ba Sing Se.

Zuko is here, and circumstances have changed, and suddenly there’s a choice in front of both of them again, a crossroads that Sokka is acutely aware that they're standing between. Sokka wants to see Zuko. He wants to finally have the chance to explore what’s between them, even if it just ends up being physical attraction and lust and a whole lot of projection. But Sokka knows he can’t make that decision for himself without talking to the others, not again, and he can’t put it off any longer than he already has.

But Spirits, this is going to suck. And Sokka doesn’t know what he’s going to do if they ask him not to go back to the Lower Ring.

“Sokka!” Toph shouts before he’s even halfway across the broad porch. “You missed dinner.”

“It’s fine,” Sokka calls back, trying to figure out where in the sprawling house she’s yelling from. Spirits, he could fit Zuko’s apartment into this place ten times over and still have room to spare. Nothing makes sense anymore.

“What do you mean, ‘it’s fine?’” Katara pops out from one of the three—*three—*living rooms, brow furrowed. “You never miss food. Are you sick? What’s going on?”

Sokka takes deep, steadying breaths as he makes his way over, relieved to see that the whole group is gathered together, even Momo. “I have something to share. Not about Appa,” he hastily adds when Aang perks up from his spot on the windowsill. “Or, well, not directly. It might be upsetting, but just…hear me out?” That opening really didn’t end as confidently as Sokka would have liked.

Aang twists around to look at him as Katara slowly resumes her place on a plush chaise, face concerned and fingers marking her place between the pages of a book. Toph has her head cocked as she reclines back on a pile of cushions pulled off the couches. She slowly sets the foot she had crossed over her knee flat to the floor. Fuck, Sokka can only imagine what his heartbeat is doing right now.

“What’ve you got for us, Snoozles?” Toph prompts.

Sokka takes a moment to ground himself in the familiarity of her affected indifference before turning to Katara and plunging in. “So. Remember that time I told you that Zuko was in Agna Qel’a, and you got all upset because you thought I was hiding it, even though I wasn’t, it just took me a long time to find you and then I was distracted because I thought you were dead?”

“Excuse me, what?” Toph props herself up on her elbow, digging at her ear with a finger. “What was all that?”

Sokka doesn’t repeat himself, though, because Aang is staring with wide eyes like he can already see where this is ending, and Katara’s face is shifting toward slowly dawning horror. “Sokka, what the f—”

Sokka doesn’t wait for her to finish. “So, turns out Zuko’s in Ba Sing Se.”

The silence is a tangible, suffocating thing. Aang and Sokka both stare at Katara, waiting for her reaction as she slowly sets her book onto the floor. Like she needs both hands free, which does *not* make Sokka feel any better about the rest of what he wants to say.

“Uh, who’s Zuko?”

“The Fire Nation is in Ba Sing Se?” Aang asks on top of Toph, his fingers curling around the edge of the windowsill and Sokka doesn’t know if it’s from fear or anger or something else. Probably anger, these days.

“No,” Sokka shakes his head, firm and immediate before taking a moment to actually consider the question.

“Guys, who is Zuko?”

“Well, I guess technically.” Sokka allows. “But not like…officially. *Zuko* is in the city.”

“What’s the difference,” Katara asks, deliberate and only a little bit sharp. Sokka can tell that she’s doing her best to resist her old hostility—he appreciates the effort even if he can always tell that it’s still there—but he can see automatic anger and not-even-flight-all-fight in the slow tightening of her fists.

“And again, *who is Zuko*?”

“The Crown Prince of the Fire Nation,” Katara finally grumbles, as Aang absently says, “Sokka’s old boyfriend.” Sokka chokes on air.

”*That* Zuko?” Toph shoots upright, something terrifyingly close to glee on her face. “Sokka was getting busy with the *Banished Prince*?”

“No, he isn’t—we weren’t—Aang!”

Aang just raises his eyebrows, plainly asking what else Sokka would call it.

“So, he wasn’t your boyfriend, he was just your—"

“Ew, Toph, don’t *say* that, I don’t want to think about my brother—”

“You were all just talking about it!”

“Not about *that*!”

“Well, where do you think this is going, Sweetness, if—”

“It doesn’t matter,” Sokka shouts, burying his face in his hands. “It doesn’t matter and that’s *not the point*.”

“What is the point, then?” Aang asks, valiantly focused as Toph collapses back in a fit of… something between a cackle and a giggle.

“The *point* is that Zuko is *here*,” Sokka repeats, wondering how they aren’t as blown away by that fact as he is. “In Ba Sing Se. In the Lower Ring. Working in a teashop.”

Katara’s mouth snaps shut, Aang’s eyebrows shooting up again in surprise as Toph finally chokes herself off. Sokka feels vaguely satisfied, if only for a moment. *That* managed to silence them all, at least for a second.

“Some kind of deep cover?” Katara finally asks, clearly struggling to wrap her mind around the dual concepts of ‘Zuko’ and ‘working.’

“No. That’s what I thought too at first,” Sokka admits. “But…he’s working in a teashop.”

“Trying to get intel?”

“No, like…actually working in a teashop. He does the register. He has an apron.”

Toph sits back up again, looking awestruck. “The Crown Prince of the Fire Nation has an *apron*.” She puts enough emphasis on it that Sokka is once again cursing the fact that she can sense heartbeats. Tui and La, please don’t let her ask for an explanation.

“Zuko told you that?” Aang says slowly, clearly also struggling with the overall idea of Zuko doing anything other than slinging fire.

“And I saw him there.”

“And…you believe him?” Aang cuts right to the heart of Sokka’s anxiety, his words part statement, because he can clearly already tell, and part question, because he clearly needs to hear it.

“Yeah,” Sokka admits, tugging at his wolf tail and contemplating his wrist wraps. Things are about to get hard. “I do.”

“Sokka…” Katara sighs, heavy with disappointment.

“I *know*. I know, okay? I do.” And he doesn’t need to hear her say it, not when he’s been saying it to himself all afternoon. They all know Sokka has believed Zuko in the past and been burned by it. “But it’s—It’s not like that, okay? It’s not the same this time.”

Katara doesn’t look convinced and Sokka shifts uncomfortably as she flicks her eyes over to Aang, a silent conversation full hesitancy and concern flashing between them. Fuck, how often have they talked about this between themselves to be able to do that?

“Like ‘that’?” Toph repeats, clearly looking for an explanation. Sokka searches for the words but finally just ends up shaking his head. He doesn’t know how to explain ‘that’ to her and not sound completely crazy for wanting to do it all over again.

“Look,” Sokka sighs, pressing the heels of his hands to his eyes. “I don’t know how to say it. It’s just…it’s not the same, okay? I believe him. He’s…different.” In ways Sokka can’t quite put his finger on, because he’s still so overwhelmed by the idea of Zuko *being there*. But definitely different. “We had a talk.”

“What if he lied?” Toph asks, her foot tapping the floor in emphasis.

“Zuko…isn’t good at lying,” Sokka says, wincing at her quiet snort of disbelief because even he can hear how weak that sounds. Being a bad liar would be a perfect cover for someone trying to deceive. But Sokka’s already worked himself through that particular tangle and came to terms with it, enough to be comfortable with the truth of it applied to Zuko. If he's wrong about that then...well, then he'd really be wrong about everything.

“Wait.” Katara’s spine goes stiff. “How long ago did you find all this out, again?”

“…Today.”

“When, exactly, today.”

“…This afternoon?”

“Sokka,” Katara says slowly, like she needs to say it out loud to make sure, like he *must* have a good explanation if she gives him the chance to provide one. “It’s past dinner.”

*Shit.*

“Yeah, so I saw him at work in the afternoon,” Sokka says, aware that he’s speaking just a bit too fast. Fuck, fuck, fuck. “And we talked this evening after his shift, and—"

“What did you do with the afternoon?” Toph jumps in, delight in kicking up trouble back in her voice.

“—and we had a talk, and it was very open, and he answered all my questions, and I believe him.” Sokka is speaking even louder and faster and absolutely dying inside because it’s not doing a bit of good. He can feel the blush rising up his neck and hear the nervous edge to his words, and Toph is cackling which is really all the confirmation that anyone needs. Fuck everything.

“Sokka, come on, really? You were supposed to be putting up posters!”

“I did put up posters! I put up all my posters!”

“What, all in one teashop in the Lower Ring?” Katara snarks.

“No!” The streets all around it, mostly. “I’ll have you know—”

“Why did you tell us,” Aang cuts in before Sokka and Katara’s squabble can really grow legs.

“What?” Sokka frowns, trying to tear himself away from the familiar rhythm of bickering with his little sister.

“Why are you telling us about Zuko?” Aang’s eyes are sharp, searching, and Sokka shifts uncomfortably under the Avatar’s probing gaze. “Was it just to tell us? Just so we know that he’s around so we can keep away?”

Sokka licks suddenly dry lips. “I didn’t want there to be secrets again.”

It’s not quite an answer, but Katara hears Sokka’s response anyway, dropping her face into her hands. “You’re starting it back up.”

“I—Yeah,” Sokka admits, folding his arms and contemplating the ceiling instead of needing to meet anyone’s eyes. “I want to.”

“Tui and *La*, Sokka, did you forget what happened last time?”

“And remind me, what did happen last time, again?” Toph jumps in.

“Of course I didn’t forget last time,” Sokka bites out, glaring at Katara’s tight scowl. Katara *knows* that he didn’t. That he never could.

“Then why—”

“He wants to try, and I want to try, and—”

“And you both tried last time and you still got hurt!”

Sokka snaps his mouth shut, mute in the face of Katara’s sudden rage.

“Sokka, I don’t want to see that happen to you again. I don’t—” Her voice cracks, a tendril of fear slipping out. “I don’t know if you remember what you were like, after the North, but—”

“That was *not* all because of Zuko,” Sokka protests, even though so much of that time immediately after is a haze that Sokka tries not to think about, tries not to remember.

“No,” Katara agrees quietly, seriously. “But a lot of it was.”

Sokka finds that he has nothing to say to that. She isn’t wrong. Yue’s death had hit deep—still hits deep—but it took him down as hard as it did because Zuko had left, too, and because Sokka hadn't been able to stopping himself from wanting too much. Katara knows it.

“Sokka,” Aang says tentatively into the tense silence. “No one wants anyone to get hurt.”

“I don’t want to get hurt either, guys,” Sokka laughs without humor. “I promise, I really don’t.”

“But you still want to try again.”

“Yeah. And I know it might not work out, I get that. But I can’t not see if it *could*.” Sokka can’t meet their eyes again, suddenly feeling so overly exposed and vulnerable. They talk about this stuff more than they used to—mostly teasing, which is fine—but Spirits, Sokka is laying himself say open right now. And he’s so scared that it won’t work.

“I don’t want to see you get hurt again,” Katara finally says, discontent and frustrated. “And I don’t see how you won’t.”

“I get that,” Sokka sighs. “But—is it my choice to make?”

Katara’s eyes shoot to his in surprise as Aang makes a soft ‘oh.’ Sokka can see understanding finally dawning of what this whole conversation has been for, what Sokka is actually trying to talk about. Starting something up with Zuko is a risk, one that Sokka would be taking for more than just himself. He can’t do it again if Katara is against it. If any of them are.

“Do you trust me?” Sokka finally asks, putting out plainly what he’s been too afraid to give voice to in the past.

“I trust *you*,” Katara huffs. “I don’t trust Zuko.”

Sokka snorts at the familiarity of that particular sentiment. “Do you trust me to be careful? To keep putting this—” he gestures to indicate the four of them, their mission, their purpose “— first?”

“Yes,” Katara sighs, slumping in defeat. Aang nods and Toph just shrugs like it doesn’t matter to her either way, which means yes because she wouldn’t be shy about it if the answer was no.

Sokka sags in relief, nearly staggering under the sudden realization that all three of them aren’t going to say ‘no,’ that they aren’t going to ask him not to go back. Sokka genuinely hadn’t known what to expect of this conversation, or what he would do at the end of it, and the weight of what he’s going to try to do is suddenly overwhelming without nervous anxiety and stress holding him up.

“I can’t believe we’re doing this again,” Katara mutters, reaching for her book. She doesn’t sound…actively angry about it?

Sokka eyes her, trying to read how upset she really is. “You know…Zuko said the same thing about you, back when we last saw him.” He can see her flash of outrage at doing anything that Zuko would do. “That he trusted me, not you. And you were upset about it.”

“Shut up,” Katara grumbles, and Sokka grins as she throws her bookmark at him, rolling her eyes. Not too upset, then.

“Wait.” Toph jolts upright, both hands slapping to the floor, eyes wide beneath her bangs. “Back in—Crown Prince Zuko is *Sparrowkeet*?”

&#45;-

Sokka leaves his door open when he finally calls it a night and starts to get ready for bed. The conversation moved on surprisingly quickly from his little revelation, like everyone was eager to find the familiar rhythms of teasing and storytelling. But Sokka knows it isn’t completely over and sure enough, it’s only a few minutes before he hears Katara’s steps coming down the hall, her gentle knock against the doorframe.

“I brought you some dinner,” she says, holding out a bowl that they both know is part peace offering, part signal of non-hostile engagement. Sokka appreciates the effort as he takes the food with murmured thanks. He hates that he and Katara aren’t always sure how they fit together these days. Sokka is bursting with pride at how much she’s grown in only a few short months, but it’s also unsettling that Katara is needing him less and less as a coach and more and more for just…support. The same way he thinks he wants her to support him. It’s strange, and new, to think of her as an equal as well as his little sister. Sokka thinks he likes it, or that he will with enough time, even though it’s not entirely comfortable for either of them yet.

They settle down in the sitting area in the corner—his bedroom is big enough to have its own sitting area. Ba Sing Se is *ridiculous*—and Katara curls up in a cushioned chair, wrapping her arms around her knees, face pensive. Sokka just eats, waiting for her to work around to whatever she wants to say, content to just sit with her if that’s what she needs.

“Are you sure about this?” The question is genuine, not trying to talk him out of anything just…needing to hear an affirmation.

“No,” Sokka snorts, because he has no idea where this is going to go, no plans, nothing. Just a persistent, impossible-to-ignore-now-that-he’s-looked-at-it desire to feel Zuko pressed against him again.

“But you thought about it?”

“For hours,” Sokka admits. Longer, maybe, if you count useless daydreams and silent, furious rehashing of the choices Zuko had already made and things that couldn’t be taken back no matter how many regrets there were now.

“And you want something with him. It’s not just…” She starts blushing. “A—a *physical* thing, or—"

“Spirits, please stop.” Sokka can feel his own face lighting up. “I do *not* want to talk about that with my sister.” He also isn’t sure that he can tell her ‘no,’ if she really presses. Sokka’s body wants Zuko in so many ways he can barely understand them all. He doesn’t know if he will ever wholly work it out of his system, but Sokka also isn’t sure that they can be more than something physical to each other anymore. So much has changed, since the letters.

“Sorry,” Katara mutters, cutting him a sideways glance that says she noticed his non-answer. “You know I just want you to be happy.”

“I know.” And Sokka always appreciates the reminder that it’s still true.

“There are other ways for you to be happy,” she says, more careful now.

“I know,” Sokka sighs, avoiding her eyes and fiddling with his chopsticks. “I…Katara, I don’t *need* to have anything with Zuko. But I *want* to.” And he hopes that he can remember to keep ‘need’ and ‘want’ separate, this time. And maybe over time ‘need’ will fade with exposure, and ‘want’ will go along with it, and everything will be easier. Maybe.

“I thought you were going to take time to figure stuff out, though.”

“Huh?”

“After Serpent’s Pass. That’s what you said. After Suki.”

“Oh.” That.

“You said that you didn’t want to start something with someone until you got yourself worked out,” Katara presses, like Sokka hadn’t been part of that awkward, fumbling conversation where he felt like he was somehow letting Suki and Katara and himself all down the further he got into it. “You said that you didn’t want to use anyone as a rebound.”

“Yeah, that—that’s true,” he finally says, because she’s looking at him expectantly like he’s supposed to see where she’s taking this.

“Doesn’t that apply anymore?”

…It does, except, “I’m pretty sure you can’t rebound with the same person.”

She waves that off, which is probably what he deserves for another non-answer. “That’s not the point. I just want to make sure that you’re…giving yourself space. You said you needed it for a reason, Sokka. Make sure you aren’t just…”

“Falling back into old habits?” Sokka finishes quietly.

“Something like that,” she sighs.

Sokka doesn’t really know what to say. He isn’t exactly *not* worried about that, too. “Katara…I’ve thought about this. A *lot*. More than just today.”

“And someone like Suki wouldn’t make you happy?” Katara’s question just misses neutrality, a little bit too plaintive and frustrated, and Sokka slumps back in his chair.

“Suki isn’t here.”

“And what, it's whoever’s closest?” Sokka winces, because he walked right into that one by trying to be evasive. Spirits, like he isn’t aware that it *would* be so much easier if it could be Suki, easier in so many ways. But…

“Someone like Suki would be nice,” Sokka finally says, waiting for Katara to look at him, needing to see if she understands. “But…would you want to settle for just nice? If you could have something that was…” He struggles for words that he can share with his sister. “That felt like maybe every piece of it could be perfect?”

“*Could*, though.”

“Nothing is certain,” Sokka shrugs, poking at his empty bowl because his answer was easy, almost flip, like Katara isn’t right. This particular ‘could’ is huge. Bigger and more fragile than Sokka can ever describe to her.

“It’s a big risk, Sokka.”

“I know. But I’m not going in blind this time. I promise.” He flicks his eyes up to make sure she believes him. “I’m not just…jumping in and seeing what happens.” Not this time. Hoping to be caught is more than Sokka can think about right now when just the knowledge that Zuko also wants to try is enough to make his pulse pound. Even though he knows that trying and actually succeeding can be worlds apart. Sokka more than learned that all the effort in the world doesn’t guarantee that things will turn out the way you want them to.

But Sokka isn’t going to just hope to be caught, this time. He’s going to be careful, because all his non-answers are spelling out—as if he didn’t already know—that Katara isn’t entirely wrong to be worried. Sokka isn’t used to being so driven by wanting when he likes to think of himself as a rational, logical individual. And he doesn’t know what it would do to him, how he would pick himself back up, if he takes another leap and hits the ground again.

&#45;-

Sokka stares up into the darkness, unsure how late it is. Usually, the pure luxury of his bed carries him immediately to sleep. Every once in a while, though, his brain can’t quiet down without the sound of the others’ breathing. Some nights Sokka can time his breaths to the sound of Toph’s snores, and that’s enough to settle him. Other nights he needs to get up and slip down the hallways, hovering outside each door until he can hear signs of them at rest inside.

Tonight, though, it’s not misplaced, engrained protectiveness keeping him awake. Its nerves, and anticipation, and too many what-ifs to even begin to sort through. It’s the bundle on his chest, pulled from the depths of his bag for the first time in months. Worn paper still wrapped in singed, dirty linen. Still so familiar under his hands as Sokka runs his thumb carefully over the soft edges.

Sokka can barely think over the rhythm his heart has set, over trying to ignore the steady beat of *hope* and *maybe* and *Zuko* that Sokka’s too scared to give conscious thought quite yet. The letters sit heavy on his chest, proof of the lie Sokka keeps telling himself, like maybe he can actually get fully behind the idea if only he says that it’s just physical to himself enough times.

## Chapter 14: Making Time

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Warnings for sexual content in this one

### Text

Zuko feels like he’s going to burst out of his skin when Agni’s light starts to shimmer through his veins and he abruptly realizes that ‘the day after tomorrow’ could mean any moment from now until Zuko tries to fall back asleep again. He has no idea when Sokka will show up. If Sokka will show up.

Fuck.

It's not a calming thought, his inner fire fretful and tight in his chest. Meditation goes about as well as could be expected, which is to say not well at all. But Zuko manages to get out the door without lighting anything except his own socks on fire, and they’re only a bit singed, and Uncle didn’t say anything about it. So maybe it's fine and Zuko can call it a win.

It’s going to be a fucking divine miracle if Zuko doesn’t burn the teashop to the ground today.

&#45;-

Zuko is still on dishwashing duty, which is a relief for everyone involved seeing as he hasn’t managed to become a more functional human being over the last day of waiting for Sokka. It's best for him to only have to deal with cups and cookware and not customers. His boss had taken one look at his bloodshot eyes and clenched jaw and refused to let him even step onto the shop floor, which showed that the man wasn't a complete idiot. That, and the very prosperous teashop.

Zuko is clearing out the last of the teapots from the morning rush, moving onto cookware and trying to burn away his anxiety and only seeming to end up short-tempered, when the familiar shape of Sokka’s not-flame crosses into the range of his fire sense. Everything in Zuko goes motionless, for a heartbeat, and then the world restarts in a rush of noise. The muffin pan falls from his hands into the sink, clattering and crashing and adding to the clamor of his heart pounding in his good ear as Zuko darts toward the door.

“Lee!” One of the other servers, Sung-min, fumbles his empty tray as Zuko barrels toward him. “What’s going on?”

“Break,” Zuko snaps, rocking to a stop to dry his hands on his apron, thankfully remembering not to heat them dry this time.

“What?”

“I’m going on break,” Zuko glares. Sung-min is *in his way*.

Sung-min shifts in confusion, turning to look back over his shoulder at the sand-clock on the shop floor. “But we don’t get break for—"

“Great, bye!” Zuko dashes for the opening, worming through the half-open doorway and ignoring Sung-min’s startled yelp as Zuko shoots onto the floor just as Sokka steps into the teashop.

Zuko’s breath skips at the sight of him, *here*, so familiar and so out of place in the mundanity of the shop. It skips again when blue eyes find him on the crowded floor and Sokka’s face relaxes into something that could almost be a shy smile. Agni. Zuko’s inner fire is spiraling out in his chest in nervous, giddy sparks as he stares into that expression. He wants to burn it into his memory so that he never forgets the shape of it, what it does to Sokka’s face, the way it makes his eyes seem endless and bright.

*Keep it together*.

Sung-min’s approaching grumbling jolts Zuko back into motion. He strides forward before anyone thinks to call him back, trying not to read too much into the shifting of Sokka’s weight, into the way his eyes go half-lidded and his mouth curves into a lopsided smile as Zuko comes up to him.

“Not here,” Zuko mutters before Sokka can say anything, grabbing Sokka’s wrist and hauling him outside. Which is probably rude, and presumptuous, and the wrong thing to do. But Zuko needs to be Lee at the teashop, and he can’t hold onto any bit of that with Sokka in front of him. Sokka doesn’t seem to care, thankfully, just giving a quick half-laugh and Agni, Zuko could die on the spot right now and be fine with it, except that he wouldn’t get to hear Sokka laugh again.

“Your room then?” Sokka asks as Zuko pulls him into the alley. The question is a little breathless with suppressed laughter, or maybe something else, and Zuko is so busy thinking about it that he almost doesn’t notice the curl of heat trying to wrap itself up Sokka’s arm before Zuko yanks it back. It’s harder than it should be, with Zuko and his fire both hungry for anything they can get of Sokka.

“Yes,” Zuko replies, belated, and he can hear the tightness in his own tone as he tries to keep his desire from leaking into the word. He can’t cut that loose yet. There are two ways Sokka’s conversation could have gone, which means there are even odds that he’s here to tell Zuko to fuck off forever. And regardless of the outcome, Zuko knows he’s going to need privacy for however he reacts to what Sokka has to say.

But they’re going to a place that’s private and close and Agni’s tits, Zuko can’t stop his mind from spinning out hopes even though he knows he shouldn’t. He’s already riding a sharp edge of anticipation because Sokka is *laughing*, and it’s ridiculous to hang so much on so little, but—that means it can’t have gone poorly, right?

Zuko shoulders open the apartment door, feeling like he’s about to vibrate apart from his need to *know*. He stumbles back against the wall a bare second later, Sokka hurtling into his arms before the door even fully closes. Zuko grabs onto Sokka’s shoulders for balance and then keeps his hands there because he likes it, because he can pull Sokka even closer this way. Sokka’s scent—leather and sunshine and metal and him—is all that Zuko can smell. Zuko has never liked the end of summer. In his early years, the sudden end of beach vacations always loomed large and tragic on the horizon, hurtling closer and closer with each day. Then it became the uncomfortable, stilted return to lessons and training and not being good enough and everyone knowing it. Eventually, that changed, too, in favor of the persistent small dread of food and fuel becoming harder to come by, the nagging fear of coming cold threatening already thin budgets, the bitterness of another year passed with no progress. Even as he clung to warmth and long days and sun, Zuko could never not see the end in front of him.

This year, those end-of-summer days are hesitant and awkward and wary, full of stilted conversation and uncertain welcome, and Agni, Zuko thinks he would give anything for them to never end.

Zuko and Sokka are tentative with each other like they’ve never been before in letters or abbeys or festival towns or the top of the world. He thinks they might both be consciously trying to be careful, newly aware of all the ways this can hurt them. It’s more than just caution for Zuko, though. He finds himself continuously needing to adjust to the knowledge that Sokka won’t be gone the next day, or the next. That his words can be met with an immediate response. That he can see Sokka reacting to them. Whenever he sees Sokka he’s quietly stunned all over again by the fact that they’re both still *here*. And he marvels every time they come together at how uninhibited Sokka can be and feels it in stark contrast to the reserve that seems to cling to them both in everything that isn't sex.

Zuko holds like it's a brittle thing the fact that there aren’t war or circumstance or impossible choice pulling them apart yet. He isn’t sure if it’s him or Sokka who is more aware of—more fearful of—that ‘yet.’

“Don’t ask questions,” Sokka suggests, leaning down to press a smiling kiss against Zuko’s lips. “Just appreciate a good thing when it’s put into your hands.”

Zuko looks helplessly down at the apron, then back up at Sokka, who just dodges Zuko’s questions with kisses and laughter until Zuko finally relents and accepts that for some things, he doesn’t need an explanation. Zuko finds he is more than happy to indulge Sokka in anything he wants, even if he doesn’t understand it. Especially something as easy as this.

&#45;-

“Where did you get to this afternoon?” Jin asks, looping her arm through his in her usual fashion. “I’m used to seeing you around all the time these days at the Blooming Petal.”

“I was busy,” Zuko mutters.

“Oh yeah?” Jin knows he has no life in Ba Sing Se. “With what?”

“Um.” Zuko can feel himself blushing, and really he should have been prepared for this, he knows that Jin loves to ask questions about everything.

“Are you—Lee, are you *blushing*?”

“No.”

“You are! What were you doing this afternoon?”

“Nothing!”

“No one?”

“He’s not—” Zuko bites the words off, but Jin is already letting out a delighted peal of laughter. Zuko automatically flinches away from the idea of anyone knowing, but after a moment of nothing but Jin grinning up at him, he manages to unfreeze enough to keep walking at her side. His heart is still beating faster than it should with instinctive alarm. But after a few shaky blocks, he can acknowledge that some part of him feels…good, to be able to share a small bit of his happiness with someone else, even if it’s only with someone who can never know all of it.

&#45;-

“You seem distracted this morning.”

Zuko startles at Uncle’s quiet words in what’s usually the silence of morning meditation. It’s true, Zuko is distracted. He always is on the days when Sokka is coming, starting the day already restless and tight with an anticipation that cuts through the memory of numb cold that tries to follow him out of sleep.

“You have been distracted a lot, lately.”

“Um.” That’s also true.

“Is it something at the Blooming Petal?” Uncle presses gently, and Zuko snorts at the idea that he would let anything there bother him enough to be a distraction. “You seemed to be settling in, there. Pao said good things about your work.”

That is patently ridiculous, that the owner would say anything positive about the terror Zuko was on his best days even before Sokka thoroughly upended his focus. But Uncle seems to be expecting a response, so Zuko finally says, “I don’t know, I guess it could be,” when really he has no idea what to say.

Zuko does know how to do his job at the teashop these days, that’s true. He isn’t sure that’s what Uncle means, though, because Uncle had said *seemed*. As if Zuko were settling in before and now isn’t. When really the only difference is that Zuko had been trying to be Lee, before, trying so hard. And now…

“I had hoped that, as is often the case with a new tea blend, that that which at first seems strange becomes familiar, with time, and then a source of contentment and enjoyment.”

Except now, Zuko is trying for something else, too. *Someone* else.

“You want me to be happy serving tea,” Zuko finally says, flat, staring at the floor because he can at least hold onto some semblance of being a Good Nephew who doesn’t glare at his Uncle first thing in the morning.

“I want you to allow yourself to be happy serving tea,” Uncle corrects gently. “Or whatever you decide to do. I do not want an opportunity for you to discover that happiness disrupted by…”

“By what,” Zuko snaps.

“By trying to hold onto the past,” Uncle finishes sadly, like the weight of watching Zuko go down that path is almost more than he can bear.

“I’m not—” Zuko bites off the rest of his words, suddenly hearing the lie. Sokka *is* part of his past. And Zuko thinks he would do terrifying things, sometimes, to hold on to him, especially on the days when it feels like all that’s left of Zuko, of who he used to be, is trying to keep whatever he can in his grasp.

“I know that your former mission consumed much of your life, Nephew. But it is okay to—”

“It’s not about that,” Zuko growls, tasting smoke on the back of his tongue.

Uncle makes a skeptical noise. “Your…restlessness—” A polite word for disappearing for extended periods of time throughout the week, and general distraction when Zuko’s around. “—has nothing to do with the Avatar?”

“No!” The word hangs uncomfortable in the air. Zuko has never been good at lying, and Sokka has never not been intertwined with the Avatar.

Uncle sighs, managing to inject a lifetime’s worth of disappointment into the sound. “Nephew, you can chart your own course. But I beg of you, please, to be careful. And to consider the life you could build, not just the one that you have left.”

Zuko flinches away from the words and the sadness in them, slamming his eyes shut to pull the shield of meditation back around himself, even if he’s unwilling to reach for the candle flame when the unsteadiness of his inner fire would give him away so clearly.

Fuck.

Zuko knows that he can make Uncle happy if he tries. And he knows that he’s been slipping up more and more at being a Good Nephew, that trying has been something he’s occupied himself with less and less. But Zuko can’t seem to bring himself to care as much about being Lee as he did before, can’t seem to fit himself as easily into that awkward shape now that he’s started being Zuko again in Sokka’s arms.

Not for the first time, Zuko wishes that it weren’t so impossible to have all of the things he wants at the same time. He wants too much, he knows he always has, but it's bitter and harsh that he can’t protect both Sokka and Uncle’s happiness without feeling they are so at odds, that Zuko needs to be two different people torn between them.

If only it didn’t constrain quite so much, to make himself into a Good Nephew. If only he could stop craving being called Zuko by the only person who still does it.
