#### Chapter End Notes

In case anyone was wondering, per the earthquake glossary: A locked fault is a fault that is not slipping because frictional resistance on the fault is greater than the shear stress across the fault (it is stuck). Such faults may store strain for extended periods that is eventually released in an earthquake when frictional resistance is overcome

## Chapter 18: Every Scar a Story

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Warnings for sexual content and references to child abuse in this one

### Text

It feels different to meet Sokka in the evening. Logically it should be the same. But Agni pulls differently at Zuko’s blood at this time of day, and finding the shape of Sokka in long-stretching shadows instead of golden afternoon sunlight drives home the fact that this is something new. Zuko can feel his pulse leaping, eager with anticipation, even as his blood fizzles with anxiety. The steps to their dance feel like they could be changing and Zuko isn’t sure of the tune, even though he’s the one again to change the tempo. But Sokka’s smile at seeing him is exactly the same, and Sokka lets Zuko take his hand easy as always, and the familiar beats of it soothe Zuko’s restless inner flame.

“You brought food,” Zuko glances at the bag in Sokka’s hand, the wisps of steam escaping the top.

“I figured you’d need to eat after work,” Sokka shrugs. “And isn’t that what people do at—at night and all?”

“…Probably,” Zuko shrugs, tugging Sokka a little bit closer to his side. That hitch—is Sokka nervous too? Does Sokka also feel like they’re stepping into some new space together?

They sit on the floor to eat at the low Earth Kingdom style table, Sokka cross-legged as he starts to pull containers from his bag and Zuko kneeling because in the privacy of his own apartment he can sit how he fucking wants and Jin can take her teasing and—

Zuko snaps back to attention as Sokka tosses a pair of cheap chopsticks in his direction, barely managing to bring his hands up in time to avoid being hit in the face and not nearly fast enough to catch them.

“Smooth, buddy,” Sokka grins as he pulls out napkins. “Real smooth.”

“I wasn’t expecting to have to dodge projectiles during dinner,” Zuko mutters, grabbing the chopsticks off the floor and snatching a napkin, embarrassed heat creeping up his face.

“You should expect projectiles at all times with me,” Sokka teases. “I thought you figured that out the first time we met.”

Zuko scowls, one hand rising without permission to touch the spot where the boomerang had hit him from behind. Agni, he’d felt so dumb, so painfully, visibly falling short to be struck like that in front of the entire crew. But Sokka’s easy laughter now—not malicious or barbed, but warm, sharing—does something to take the sting out of the memory.

“I even threw them to your right side,” Sokka adds. “So you have no excuse. Unless you were too busy looking out for these weapons instead, of course.” He flexes his biceps with an exaggerated eyebrow wiggle, laughing again as Zuko ducks his head in mingled embarrassment and shock.

Zuko…didn’t realize that Sokka had noticed the extent of his blurred vision on the left, enough to know to do something like that without Zuko asking. It shouldn’t surprise him as much as it is, Sokka is observant and smart and can put two and two together and come up with four. Just…no one else ever does, or at least never acts like they do. Zuko does his best to make sure of it. And Zuko never expected to hear it referred to so…casually. Like it’s not something dangerous and potentially debilitating if the wrong people find out. Like it’s just another piece of Zuko, no different than his height or his bending or the fact that he hates tea.

Zuko sneaks a glance at Sokka’s face, which is relaxed and casual as Sokka keeps setting out the food, before quickly hiding his own eyes again, conscious that he is running his fingers over his chopsticks beneath the table with the kind of dumbstruck care generally reserved for things made of gold.

Sokka brought rice and pickled vegetables and diced meat to put on top, simple food, and Zuko tries to latch onto the easy normalcy of getting a meal ready even as it all feels simultaneously relaxing and bizarre. Zuko’s done this hundreds of times before, but he’s never done it with Sokka, not here. His mind keeps tripping over that fact, holding Zuko on the trembling edge of hyperawareness as he furiously catalogs each new thing as it happens —the first time Sokka passes him a bowl, the first time Sokka twirls his chopsticks through his fingers, the first time Sokka finishes setting out all the food and glances at Zuko expectantly, ready to serve and asking what he wants.

*You*.

“Uh—whatever—” Zuko clears the huskiness from his throat and tries again. “Whatever you like.”

“Whatever I like, huh?” Sokka’s chopsticks pause above the containers as he considers. “You’re always doing whatever I like.”

“Um.” That isn’t wrong, and Zuko isn’t sure why Sokka sounds so…fondly exasperated by it?

“What if I said I liked something that you didn’t,” Sokka challenges, raising an eyebrow. “What then, Mr. ‘Whatever You Like’?”

“Sokka,” Zuko says slowly, glancing down at the table. Is this some kind of test? “All the food looks good…”

“What if I didn’t want to eat it?”

“That’s…fine.” It’s a lot to bring and not want to eat, but it will all keep. “I can grab something from—”

“What if I didn’t want to eat at all anymore?”

“Okay, I—” Zuko glances up in surprise—when has Sokka ever not wanted to eat—to find Sokka looking at him from beneath his lashes, eyes half-lidded and hot. “…Oh.”

“What would you want then?” Sokka murmurs, and Zuko can only stare as his mind finally untangles from trying to figure out what Sokka wants enough to register his tone and realize what Sokka *wants*.

Sokka’s eyes are deep pools, expectant, and Zuko can feel his inner fire rising hot and hungry in answer. He licks his lips, then deliberately lets his flame bloom in his hands like he rarely does these days. Zuko watches the way it reflects off Sokka’s eyes, the way Sokka’s breath visibly catches when Zuko sends it streaming out to the candles and lamps around the room. “I’d want to be able to see you,” Zuko whispers.

“Good answer.” Sokka shoots to his feet, and before Zuko can even begin to stand Sokka is dropping onto his lap and tugging Zuko into a hot, hungry kiss as if it’s been weeks, months since they’re seen each other and not just the day before.

Zuko automatically wraps an arm around Sokka to tug him closer, bracing himself with his other hand as he sinks back under Sokka’s weight. Sokka’s hands are cool, gentle against Zuko’s face even as his mouth is urgent, demanding. The contrast, the feel of Sokka already half-hard pressed against his stomach, the thought that maybe he's been like that this whole time, *fuck,* has Zuko’s head spinning, his breathing already ragged.

Somehow they stumble to their feet without separating, fumbling toward Zuko’s futon, sloppy and uncoordinated as they try to shed their clothes without taking mouths off skin. They manage to strip off Sokka’s tunic in fits and starts and Sokka shoves Zuko’s shirt up and off as he licks a line from Zuko’s navel to his throat. Zuko shivers and gasps and kicks off his pants, knees buckling when Sokka sucks at the curve of his neck. Zuko gives up on being upright, then, letting himself just fall back onto the bed in front of Sokka.

Zuko’s inner fire blazes as he looks up the length of Sokka’s body to see the hungry, awed expression on his face. He’s totally bare before Sokka’s gaze, laid out, and Zuko finds himself arching up into it, flexing, a ripple running through him as if Sokka’s hands were on him and not just his eyes. Sokka exhales something between a laugh and a groan, openly staring before dragging his eyes up to Zuko’s face, something wicked flashing in them as Sokka drops his hands down to his pants. Zuko catches his breath in anticipation but instead of frantically tearing them off like Zuko expects, Sokka slowly runs his hand over the waistband, half trailing fingers over his own skin, almost casually pulling the fabric taut over his erection and Zuko is going to *die.*

Zuko leans up onto his elbows to see better, breath gusting out of him as Sokka makes another teasing pass. He’s vaguely aware of Sokka smirking, watching his reaction, but Zuko can’t concentrate on anything except the show Sokka is making of stripping off his pants, of pulling off his wrist wraps, of preening and flexing, each inch uncovered lit golden in the candlelight.

Sokka’s hand is cool and relaxed in Zuko’s as Zuko tugs him into the teashop before opening. Toph is the only one at the house when Sokka finally makes his way home that morning, which isn’t entirely unexpected. He’s a bit later coming home than he thought he’d be. “Shut up.” He cannot walk across this room fast enough, but he will *not* break and actually run. She would never let him live it down.

“Don’t worry,” she calls. “It’s all just physical, right?”

“Toph!”

They nap together, now that Zuko has arranged his shifts to give them have more time, now that they’ve slept side by side before. Somehow Zuko is unprepared for how much more intensely annoying his shifts at work have become, especially when he’s returning from one of his overly long afternoon breaks. Zuko has never hated the teashop as much as he does then when he’s coming back to it after lunch. Zuko is entirely unsure of who this guy is, or what he wants, or whether Minji knows him or not. But Zuko is sure that, at the very least, the man is disrupting her focus and this teashop cannot function with both its floor staff in a state of distraction. And Zuko fucking claimed that spot first. Minji is the one who’s always completely collected on the floor, at ease regardless of how difficult or chatty her customers are, smiling and cheerful to a degree that it scrapes across Zuko’s nerves when he has to deal with it for more than an hour at a time.

But today Minji is fumbling her order pad, dropping her pencil, blushing crimson, mixing up sencha and matcha which even Zuko hasn’t done in years. Zuko barely manages to hold back an audible growl as he grabs the tray from her hands. If she can do this right then he will do it for her because he’s *done* with this lack of focus. Sokka is starting to wonder if their naps might be the only time Zuko ever really rests, because Zuko certainly doesn’t seem to sleep without dreams, and the dreams never seem good. Even if it’s just a doze, even if the dream isn’t enough to wake him, even if Zuko doesn’t seem to remember that it happened, Sokka is starting to think that practically every unconscious moment Zuko has is stalked by nightmares.

Zuko flinches in his sleep, an unvoiced noise rumbling through his chest beneath Sokka’s ear. He can’t throw it in here, but he also can’t bring bare fists to what is now, apparently, a knife fight—where did the guy even *pull* that from? Spirits, it is too far past breakfast for this shit.

Sokka has slightly more reach with his boomerang against the man’s knife, and he uses every bit of it to keep the man at bay and try to figure out a strategy. A boomerang isn’t exactly an edged weapon, but it can deal plenty of blunt-force damage. And his opponent is already favoring the leg that Sokka punched. And all the while Sokka keeps his eyes on the man’s center of mass, watching the way he telegraphs his moves, getting used to the way his body shifts ahead of a strike, waiting for his opportunity to—there.

Zuko is basking in the afternoon sunlight, enjoying Agni’s touch along his back before they head into the newly crisp fall air to train. “Mhm,” Sokka hums, lips quirking. “Think about it,” he murmurs. “You could live in luxury. You could be my personal tea server. We’ll get you a nice apron, you can follow me around with melon grapes and a fan and—”

“Shut up,” Zuko huffs, rolling his eyes and shoving Sokka’s shoulder as Sokka laughs. But Zuko lets the brief image of what could only ever be a fantasy settle in his chest, carving out enough space for him to breathe even as the idea of it drives home reality. Zuko can’t just run away from Uncle. Which means Zuko can’t run away from whatever Uncle wants to say.

“For real, though,” Sokka asks, serious. “You’re good?”

“I’m fine,” Zuko sighs, and it sounds a little more real this time. “Thank you. You’ll—you’re still coming back? Tomorrow?”

Sokka's blue eyes study him closely for a moment before Sokka finally gives him a quiet smile. “Always.”

&#45;-

Iroh is waiting for Sokka at the bottom of the stairs, which…isn’t exactly a surprise, really, even if Sokka had secretly hoped to make it out of the apartment without having to look Zuko’s uncle in the face after being caught in bed with his nephew. He’s a large shape in the darkness of the narrow hallway, and Sokka is suddenly distinctly aware of how *solid* Iroh is. Especially when he’s blocking the door.

“Master Sokka.”

“Um.” Sokka is pretty sure that Iroh’s neutral tone is not actually neutral. “Hi.”

“Leaving so soon?” The words are inquisitive, his smile calmly curious, his eyes are sharp in a way that makes Sokka feel like his skin is two sizes too small.

“Ah, yeah…” Not that Sokka necessarily wants to. He isn’t exactly loving Zuko’s emotional state back up there. But there’s a lot, he thinks, that needs to be said between Zuko and Iroh. The kind of things that won’t get said if Sokka’s there.

“Hm.” Iroh’s stare is uncomfortably long and uncomfortably silent. “Then we will talk later.”

Sokka…cannot have heard that right. “What?”

“Tomorrow after my shift, perhaps?” Oh Spirits. He did hear it.

“Um…sure,” Sokka says, fighting back the urge to fidget. He’s pretty sure that he can’t say no.

Iroh smiles, genial, all teeth. “That is four hours after my Nephew’s usual break. In case you were wondering.”

“Ah…yes. Got it. Okay. That…works.” Sokka can…rearrange his whole day tomorrow. That’s fine.

“I look forward to it.”

Sokka nods wordlessly, unable to say that he shares the sentiment as Iroh finally steps back to let him pass. Sokka ducks his head, hurrying by, torn between needing to get out before he’s crushed under his own embarrassment and wanting to stay in case Zuko needs him. Sokka could tell that Zuko was actually considering climbing out the window back there, which is… not great. Something about revealing this to his uncle is driving Zuko shockingly close to what feels like hysteria, and even if Sokka couldn’t pick out any edges of fear beneath Zuko’s panic, Sokka can’t forget any of the stories that Zuko has told him. He can’t forget that Iroh has been one of the people to train Zuko, who carries so many training accidents on his skin.

&#45;-

Zuko is standing, finally dressed, bed made, everything put back together the way he always does to make it look like nothing ever happened in this room. Which is probably futile, now that Uncle has seen that something definitely has. But Zuko needs whatever distance he can get right now from the vulnerability of an unmade bed for two.

Uncle taps quietly on the door and waits a beat before slipping in, which isn’t the same as waiting for permission but is more than he’s ever done before. Maybe, Zuko thinks grimly, Uncle enjoyed walking in on Zuko exactly as much as Zuko enjoyed getting walked in on.

Uncle has fresh water in hand and gestures Zuko to the low table as he sets about making tea. Zuko walks over on barely-solid legs, crossing the room in a few paces and immediately at a loss for what to do. Does he sit with his back to the bed, so he doesn’t have to look at it the whole conversation? But then Uncle will be looking at it, so Zuko should sit facing the bed. But then every time he dodges Uncle’s eyes Zuko will be looking at those sheets and remembering and—

Uncle ends his struggle by pointedly setting down two cups and taking a seat. Back to the bed it is, then. Fuck.

Zuko drops in front of his cup, automatically folding into a formal seiza, hands flat and stiff against his thighs. He watches Uncle go through the motions of heating water and measuring leaves and desperately wishes he still had the weight of armor around him to keep him from vibrating out of his own skin. Everything feels like it’s happening underwater, like it’s distant but far too close at the same time, until Zuko is dizzy from it. The gentle brush of porcelain against wood echoes like ice cracking beneath fire.

“I have questions,” Uncle finally says, clasping his hands and watching the teapot as if he can see the leaves steeping through the ceramic. He flicks his eyes up when Zuko is silent, waiting until Zuko manages to jerk his head into some semblance of a nod.

“I would ask that you answer them,” he continues, implacable, and Zuko forces out another tight nod. “I also have something I would like to say. You will listen.”

Zuko can’t manage to make himself move, even to nod, eyes fixed on the wood of the table, hands white-knuckled around each other in his lap. Zuko’s inner flame is hiding tight along his spine. As if his bones would offer any real protection.

“Will you listen first, or answer first?”

“…Listen,” Zuko rasps out. He can barely say the one word, so he isn’t sure that he could handle speaking quite yet. Not when he feels like everything inside him is about to explode and maybe something other than words is going to claw its way free.

“Very well.” Uncle pours the tea then, motions calm and steady as always and *Agni,* Zuko is going to shatter waiting for the sword to drop. He can already hear the words, the shape they will take, the weight they will carry, the way they will burn as they give form to duty and law and honor and disappointment.

“Zuko.” He twitches, unused anyone but Sokka saying his name anymore. “This does not change how I see you.”

Uncle…already saw him this way? Already…thought Zuko was shameful? Wrong? Irresponsible? Illegal? Zuko might actually pass out. His throat is closed, vision going blurry. Fire needs air and so do firebenders and he can’t breathe, can’t make his chest expand, can’t —

“We both know the laws, in the Fire Nation,” Uncle says quietly, staring into his teacup and Zuko can't respond, can't react, can only think that at least it will only be Uncle watching him break apart, this time. “We are not there. Things are different in the Earth Kingdom. And in the South.”

Zuko…doesn’t understand. He’s already exiled, already hunted, already can’t return home. Fuck, can he be *more* banished?

“Zuko.” He doesn’t flinch this time, even though the sound of Uncle saying his name is just as unexpected. “I have never felt that the laws should have been changed. I have never felt that what Sozin did was right.”

What…that doesn’t...Zuko can’t breathe, can’t think. Nothing Uncle is saying is making sense, it almost sounds like—like—

“Whether you prefer women, men, both, neither—you are my nephew. Your happiness is all that matters to me. I know you did not choose to tell me, but Zuko—This *does not change* *how I see you*.”

Uncle falls silent, taking a long, slow sip of his tea and patiently contemplating the table while Zuko’s world quietly crumbles apart and rebuilds itself beneath him, a not unfamiliar feeling, the ground beneath his feet feeling so fragile and tentative and maybe strong enough to bear his weight, this time. It still isn't any easier to breathe.

“Do you believe me, Nephew?” Uncle finally asks, soft and serious, eyes worried as they rise to Zuko’s face. Zuko stares back, looking for a hint of anything beneath the concern and care. His inner fire flickers a cautious, hesitant pulse through his numb core.

Uncle *can* lie. Zuko knows that. And Zuko isn’t always good at working through motivations, not like Azula is. But hard as he can bring himself to look at this, he can’t figure out a reason why Uncle *would* lie. Not about this. And maybe Zuko just…needs it to be true. Needs, when Zuko is so unsure about everything else, to feel that he can trust in this one thing: that Uncle believes what he's saying is true.

“Yes,” Zuko finally whispers, clearing his throat but failing to add any more strength to his words. “I—yes.”

“Good,” Uncle says, open relief on his face as he closes his eyes. “That is good.”

Uncle lets the silence stretch and Zuko is painfully grateful to be able to just sit, Uncle cupping his tea while Zuko tries to realign all the parts of his life into a shape that makes some kind of sense again. Uncle finally nudges Zuko’s cup toward him and Zuko picks it up without thinking, automatic, not even grimacing against the grassy taste of jasmine.

Uncle watches, and Zuko’s face must be naked and unguarded like it almost never is because the moment he feels a sense of uncertain steadiness, Uncle clears his throat, quietly demanding Zuko’s attention again.

“I do not care the gender of who you decide to—spend time with, Nephew. But—” Zuko feels a spike of pure panic like a knife to the base of his skull. “—I do care *who* you are spending time with.”

Uncle’s eyes are meaningful, expectant, and Zuko can only gaze back, mute and helpless, finally forcing out a tight nod to show that he’s listening. It’s question time, apparently. Fuck. What are the chances of a sudden teashop emergency right about now?

“So.” Uncle sets his cup onto the table, eyes never leaving Zuko’s face. “Master Sokka.”

It’s not a question, technically, so Zuko keeps his head ducked, fiddling with his tea for something to do with his hands and vaguely wishing Uncle were on his left side so Zuko’s face wouldn’t be so easy to read and so Zuko wouldn't have to try so hard to avoid looking at him. Zuko isn’t used to having his shields and walls stripped away like this.

“Are you using him to get to the Avatar?”

“*What*?” Zuko’s head snaps up in horror. “No!” His inner fire wrenches at the thought and his stomach lurches, feeling like the ground is cracking beneath him again. That Uncle thinks he could—that he *would*—

“You have tried to use him before,” Uncle points out, reserved and guarded in a way that has Zuko struggling for air.

“Not like this,” he gasps, ripping his eyes away and barely staying upright against the need to fold around the pain in his gut. “Not—*no!”*

Zuko’s uneven breaths are too fast, too harsh, overly loud in the silence as Uncle studies him, expression grave. Zuko’s inner fire is on the verge of breaking free in its frantic agitation by the time Uncle finally nods, taking a sip of his tea.

“I am sorry that I upset you by asking,” he says. “Forgive an old man his fears. I never want to see you doing things that you will regret, Nephew. And it is hard to see regrets, without the benefit of time.”

Something jagged and sharp that might be a laugh bubbles up, at risk of ripping out of him if his chest weren’t so tight. Zuko’s done nothing his whole life *but* things he will regret. For Uncle to say it about the one thing that Zuko doesn’t…

“Was it always like this?”

“I don’t…what?” Zuko ducks again, uncertain. His mind is going in too many different directions to figure out which track Uncle might be on.

“You have…known…Master Sokka for a number of months now,” Uncle elaborates. “You spent much of that time appearing to be his adversary.” Oh. This question. “You fought with him. Hunted him.”

“I wasn’t hunting *him*.”

“Never?”

Zuko cuts his eyes away and doesn’t respond, which is answer enough for someone who knows him like Uncle does.

“You held him captive, for a time,” Uncle continues when it’s clear that Zuko isn’t going to keep speaking. “You healed him. You set him free.” Zuko stares down at his knotted hands and doesn’t answer, because technically Uncle hasn’t asked a question yet. “You wrote to him?”

“…Yes,” Zuko admits, wondering if he’s admitting to treason in the same breath. Exactly how selective is Uncle with the Fire Nation laws he chooses not to care about?

Uncle hums softly, nodding like certain things are making sense, and if they are then Zuko would like to be let in on it because nothing in his world makes sense anymore. “And then you found him in Ba Sing Se.”

“He found me,” Zuko corrects, watching out of the corner of his eye as Uncle’s brows shoot up in surprise. “He came into the teashop, and…” Zuko shrugs, because he doesn’t really know how to explain what came after, and he’s pretty sure Uncle can figure it out well enough considering what he walked in on.

“I see,” Uncle murmurs, a slight frown twisting his brow. A thinking frown, though, so Zuko only half stops breathing at the sight of it instead of choking up all the way. Uncle purses his lips in thought, looking like he’s trying to figure out how to say something. Wariness slides down Zuko’s back. With all they’re already talking about, Zuko doesn’t see what could possibly be any more difficult than what they’ve already said. “When a young eagle hawk first leaves the nest—”

Agni save him. Is Uncle trying to give him the eagle hawks and the scorpion bees? When Zuko lived on a ship for nearly four years, and is almost *seventeen*?

“—it often has much enthusiasm for flight, but little—”

“Don’t,” Zuko cuts in, voice harsh. He takes a breath, trying to modulate his tone. “Just…say what you mean.”

Uncle hesitates, then nods and takes a bracing breath. “When you are young, and new to passion—” Just end him now. “—there are certain things you need to be careful of. To stay safe. Things I should have considered that you would not have had opportunities to learn. That no one would have felt able to tell you. But things that are important to know.”

“Uncle—you don’t—”

“Things that are *critical* to know if you are a firebender.”

Zuko clamps his mouth shut and reluctantly drags his eyes up to somewhere around the level of Uncle’s shoulders.

“One’s inner flame moves with one’s emotions. It is natural, and nothing to be ashamed of. But it can be dangerous if your partner is not also a firebender. Even if they are, sometimes.”

“I *know*, you don’t—”

“You don’t know,” Uncle interrupts, sharp, startling Zuko into silence. “Not if—” He cuts himself off and takes a steadying breath that does *not* make Zuko feel any steadier about whatever Uncle is trying to say. “Nephew, no one has perfect control all the time. But if you are losing control so much that your partner has as many marks on them as—as I saw—”

They both wince at the reminder and Zuko desperately throws himself into that brief hesitation, trying to head this off before it can go further. “It’s not—I’m not losing control,” he forces out through gritted teeth. “I don’t—it's *fine*.”

“Such things might seem minor, but they can easily—”

“I’m *not*.”

“Zuko,” Uncle sighs. “Now is not the time for pride. This is not a comment on your bending, or your ability. It’s something that all young firebenders need to learn. It is my fault for neglecting—”

“He asks for it,” Zuko blurts out, overly loud, gripping the edge of the table as he goes light-headed with embarrassment*.* Fuck, he can’t believe he said it, but Agni’s *tits*, letting Uncle continue? Getting some kind of *lesson* about control and release and sex? That would be even worse.

“…He…?”

Zuko wonders if throwing himself out the window is still a viable option. “Hewantsmetodoit.”

Uncle is quiet for a long time, tea barely steaming now in front of them while Zuko contemplates whether lighting the apartment on fire is a disproportionate or absolutely reasonable way to end this conversation.

“And this is…something that you know?” Uncle finally asks, voice so carefully neutral that Zuko can’t help but hear the wash of mutual discomfort beneath it. “It’s not just something you—assumed? Based on a…reaction?”

Zuko closes his eyes, tipping his head back in total defeat as he gives up on the last of his pride. “We, um. Talked about it. He was—very clear.”

“That…okay.” Zuko wonders if he should be horrified or vindictively satisfied that the conversation has clearly gone in a direction that Uncle didn’t plan for. Uncle is suddenly sounding a fraction as off-balance as Zuko feels. “That is…obviously not unheard of.” A deep breath. “You still need to be careful though, Nephew.”

“I know,” Zuko tells the ceiling. He would kill for some deep, dark rafters to climb into right about now. Maybe a maintenance hatch.

“Mixing bending with sex, especially firebending, is a fine line to walk,” Uncle cautions, and Zuko wants to just…crawl under the table and never look at Uncle ever again. But he forces himself to keep still and listen instead. Uncle would probably just crawl under after him, anyway. “You do not want to form a habit that you cannot stop.” A beat while he waits for Zuko to dip his head in acknowledgment. “*Can* you stop? If you need to?”

“I—that part of it, yeah,” Zuko says, surprised into an unthinking answer and wincing when he hears his own words. He’s really digging his own grave with enthusiasm, today.

“…'That part’ of it?”

Zuko sighs, finally dropping his eyes back to Uncle, wilting at the utter implacability there. It looks like they’re doing this, then. “I…that part is more…active?” Agni’s tits, they’re never going to be able to look each other in the eye again. “But there’s a more…passive part, I guess, that just kind of…happens..?”

Uncle looks concerned, not his gentle are-you-sure-you-aren’t-going-to-light-something-on-fire expression, more like his I-think-we-should-run-before-the-fire-spreads look. It is not reassuring. “Nephew, I think you are going to have to be more specific.”

Zuko blows out a hard breath, trying to gather his thoughts enough to find a way to provide enough information and not die from mortification before he can get it all out. “Remember when Sokka was sick? On the *Wani*?”

Uncle blinks, clearly taken aback by Zuko’s direction. “Yes…”

“And we needed to keep his fever down.”

“Ah. Yes.”

“And I used bending,” Zuko continues, fiddling anxiously with his mostly-full teacup.

“I remember,” Uncle says cautiously.

“It’s…that.” Zuko glances up and can see that Uncle still doesn’t understand. “I had to…find his inner flame, or whatever, with my fire sense, right? Like the breath of fire, but opposite.” “Yes,” Uncle agrees carefully. “A heat transfer exercise, essentially.”

“He…never left it.” Uncle just looks puzzled. “My fire sense. He…I can still feel him. That way.”

“You are aware that he is there?” Uncle asks slowly. “That isn’t totally unheard of, for someone adept with heat to be able to distinguish the presence of a warm human or animal from—”

“No. Like…it’s not the same as a fire, but it’s close. It…flickers, and changes, and…does the stuff that fire does, mostly. And I can hold it like I can hold a candle.” Agni, Zuko has studied a truly shameful amount of theory to still not have the words for this. “And I can…move it, the same way I can control a candle. Or feed it, or steady it, or…” Lower it, snuff it out, but he doesn’t say that. He doesn’t want to talk about that, doesn’t want to remember it right now.

“That is not something I have familiarity with,” Uncle admits after a heavy pause, brow tight, fingers tapping the table with uncharacteristic restlessness. “It sounds like your bending has somehow become…attuned, in some way, to his chi.”

“Yes.” That’s exactly how it feels. Like Sokka’s chi vibrates on a frequency that matches the tone of Zuko’s inner flame.

“When he was sick…You held onto the heat transfer for far longer than I have ever read of anyone doing before. It is possible that you…” Uncle trails off, thoughtful, absently picking up his tea without drinking. “I will study on this topic, Nephew,” he finally says. “Just because I have never heard of it does not mean it has never happened.”

“There aren’t a lot of firebending scrolls to study in Ba Sing Se,” Zuko points out. The city barely acknowledges that firebenders exist, from what he can tell.

“There are other ways to learn,” Uncle says absently, finally raising his cup and grimacing slightly to find the liquid cool.

Zuko doesn’t have the energy to touch that comment right now, too emotionally drained and exhausted to do more than distantly recognize it as something to be wary of. He just nods in quiet assent, spooling a thread of heat into his own tea and taking a warming sip and letting himself be shakily relieved that even if Uncle doesn’t know what it is that Zuko is doing, he at least isn’t reacting like it’s dangerous. And Agni, at least they aren’t talking about sex anymore.

## Chapter 20: Enter the Dragon

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Brief references to canon-typical child abuse in this one

### Text

Sokka doesn’t know what to do with himself after leaving the apartment, so he blindly lets his body bring him back to the Upper Ring. He stares blankly out of the window of the tram car at the passing houses and districts, navigating tickets and passes and transfers without ever really registering what’s in front of him. Every step of the journey is familiar and every part of it feels completely out of place, a thing that isn’t right to do so early in the day, to do when it involves leaving an anxious, unhappy Zuko behind. Sokka’s feet carry him home even as his thoughts are stuck back in the Lower Ring, knotted around mortification and worry and confusion up until Aang’s startled voice cuts through his distraction.

“Sokka!” The airbender falls out of demonstrating some trick, a handful of marbles scattering on the floor. “What are you doing back so soon?”

“And why’s your heart doing weird things,” Toph frowns, flicking one of Aang’s polished rocks away.

“What happened?” Katara demands, bursting in from the direction of the bedrooms. “Are you okay?”

Sokka blinks, disoriented under the sudden wave of questions, finally registering that he’s back at home, that everyone is there too where of course they would be, it’s the middle of the afternoon, and that Katara...is holding a handful of ice balls?

“…What are you doing?” Is this what they get up to in the afternoons he isn’t around?

“Don’t worry about it,” Katara waves his question away, tossing the ice to Aang with a fluid gesture. Aang nearly fumbles them to the ground along with the marbles. “What’s wrong?” “I’m fine. Nothing’s wrong. Are you—is this a game?” There are books placed over the floor almost like…boundary markers, maybe?

“Lie,” Toph says helpfully, ignoring both his grumble of annoyance and his question.

“There isn’t anything to be upset about,” Sokka tries again, fiddling with his wrist wraps as Toph flicks a marble toward Aang, who halts it mid-roll. “Can I play?

“Also a lie.”

Sokka scowls, crossing his arms and realizing how defensive that looks and immediately uncrossing them and scowling harder. Katara’s eyes flit over him for signs of damage, very much *not* answering his question as she asks, suspicious, “Did Zuko do something?”

“No,” Sokka growls, glaring when Katara glances to Toph for confirmation. “No one did anything. What are the rules?”

“*That* part was a lie.”

“You’re upset,” Katara challenges instead of explaining what the game is, the ice lurching in Aang’s hands toward her until he scrambles to get a hold of it again. Like *Katara* has reason to be worked up when *Sokka* is the one being ignored, here.

“I’m not upset!” Which isn’t a convincing thing to shout, even with Toph staying silent when everyone glances at her for confirmation. But it's true. Sokka is more quietly freaking out, at the moment, than actively upset.

“Why are you back early?” Aang asks, trying a different tact as he guides the marbles of ice back toward him.

“Iroh sent me home,” Sokka grumbles, giving up on finding out about the game. Some stupid bending thing, probably. With water and stone and the Avatar and are those chalk lines drawn on the floor? It probably sucks.

“Iroh?” Katara frowns, some of her ready aggression softening now that he’s answering questions, unlike *some people* in their family today.

“Zuko’s uncle.”

Sokka is wholly unprepared for Toph’s sudden whoop of laughter. “The Dragon of the West *sent you home*?”

“The—the what?” Sokka falters, glancing toward Aang and Katara, but they just shrug, equally lost.

“Didn’t you know?” Toph sounds some mixture of incredulous and thrilled. “The former Crown Prince Iroh, now General Iroh, firstborn of Azulon, descendant of Agni, beloved of the Eternal Flame, Besieger, Destroyer of Walls, the Dragon of the West.”

That…is not a set of titles that makes Sokka feel any better about his pending conversation with the man.

“Your heart is getting weirder,” Toph observes, giving him her full attention, which makes Sokka feel vaguely ill. Or maybe he was already feeling that way and is just noticing.

“Yeah,” Aang says slowly. “Your face is going all…funny.”

“He, um. The Dragon…wants to talk to me? Tomorrow?” Sokka finally says, a fresh wash of anxiety making it come out almost like a question.

“Why?" Katara frowns. "Did you do something?”

“Yeah, Katara, *his nephew*.”

“Not helping, Toph,” Sokka mutters.

“Never said I was trying to, Sokka.”

“Why does Zuko’s uncle want to talk to you,” Aang cuts in, soothing again, with the air of someone who has lots of experience diffusing squabbles between Katara and Toph, which… he probably does, actually.

“Well…” Sokka is pretty sure he’s about to open up a whole new crack in the ice, but he can already tell that between Toph and Katara he isn’t going to be able to wiggle out of it. “Probably because he just found out about me.”

Katara’s eyebrows shoot up in surprise. “He what?”

“Zuko didn’t exactly tell his uncle about me and…him,” Sokka mumbles to the floor, already cringing from whatever opinion Katara is going to have about that fact.

“But he knows now?” Aang clarifies, absently weaving a ball of ice and a ball of stone between his fingers, which…is a new trick? Or at least one Sokka didn’t realize he could do.

“Whoa, *that* was interesting,” Toph says, and Sokka winces at the heart-lurching mortification that’s giving him away right now. “What, did he walk in on you guys doing the dirty?” Sokka’s heart stops and Toph shoots upright. “Wait, *did he?”*

“Uh—”

“Oma and Shu, he *did!”*

“Not like *that,”* Sokka protests uselessly, face on fire as Aang squeaks in startled embarrassment. “We weren’t—”

“What, you just finished up?” Toph cackles, whooping louder when all Sokka can offer is embarrassment-choked silence.

“Toph, *ew*. *Stop*. And Sokka—” Katara looks at him in horrified disbelief and amazement. “Tui and Li, how do you *do* these things to yourself?”

“It wasn’t my fault,” Sokka insists, wanting to just evaporate out of his skin because Spirits, his day has already been full of more than enough unexpected oversharing.

“Don’t you know how to lock a door? You’re sixteen!”

Sokka makes a wordless, aggrieved noise because what if they all *just stopped talking about* *it.* “I don’t know, Katara, it’s not my apartment! I wasn’t locking the door!”

“Seems like no one was,” Toph grins.

Katara throws her hands up, exasperated. “How did you not hear him coming?”

“It’s only one room! There’s no hearing someone coming! You’re in the hall or you’re in the apartment, there isn’t any—” Sokka flails his hands around. “—in between to hear!”

Katara’s stutters, rocking back on her heels. “…They live in one room?”

“It’s the Lower Ring,” Sokka grumbles. “It’s not exactly like this.” He waves at their small mansion.

“Let’s circle back to that later,” Toph suggests pleasantly. “*I* want to hear more about how Crown Prince Zuko told the Dragon of the West about his boyfriend by introducing him bare-assed and—”

“Toph!” Katara shrieks.

“That’s not what happened!”

“Oh, what, because you had a blanket?”

“I—yes!”

“Okay, okay, let’s just—” Aang takes a deep breath, face almost as red as Sokka’s must be. “Let’s just all move on from that.”

“*Please.”*

*“Thank you*.”

Aang gives them space to quiet down, waiting for Toph to settle back with an eyeroll and a get-on-with-it head toss before turning to Sokka. “Why are you worried about talking to Zuko’s uncle?”

“Wait, haven’t you met him already?” Katara frowns. “Is he awful?”

“Yeah, on the ship.” Sokka scrubs his hands over his face. Shit, maybe Toph’s relentless teasing is better than all of them intently focused on this particular topic. “He seemed…nice, I guess.”

“So, what’s bothering you?” Aang prompts when Sokka doesn’t elaborate.

“I don’t know.” Sokka hates having to admit to that in front of all of them, but he feels like he’s treading close to the boundaries of things that aren’t his to share. “I don’t really know what their thing is, but Iroh’s important to Zuko.”

“Ah,” Toph suddenly says, nodding sagely. All three of them regard her warily.

“…What?” Sokka asks, bracing himself for more mockery.

Her factual, level tone is a surprise. “You’re freaking out because you’re meeting the parents.”

“I’m not doing that,” Sokka says, the denial immediate. He is most certainly *not* meeting the Fire Lord. And if he was he would know exactly what to do about it.

“Actually…you kind of are,” Aang says slowly, shrugging in apology when Sokka frowns at him. “Isn’t Zuko’s uncle kind of always with him?”

“Yeah…”

“So, you want Zuko’s uncle to like you because he’s important to the person you’re, you know, with. That’s basically meeting the parents.”

“But it’s not—we’re not…like that,” Sokka protests, sputtering as Aang shoots him a skeptical glance and Katara rolls her eyes and Toph snorts out a quiet “sure” that drips with sarcasm. Sokka stares. *All* *three* of them think that? Spirits, what are the odds that they’re *all* wrong?

…Fuck. *Are* he and Zuko like that? And if they are, how did it happen without Sokka noticing?

“You don’t *have* to talk to him, you know,” Toph points out, breaking Sokka’s visible spiral into hysteria.

“I don’t?” Sokka perks up at the idea of a way out of being grilled by the Dragon of the West, which…might be a tad more of a literal description than Sokka would like.

“Well yeah,” Toph shrugs like it’s obvious. “Just don’t do it.”

Sokka stares, waiting for more, slowly deflating when ‘more’ never comes. “Toph, I can’t just not show up.”

“Why not? Life is too short to do the things you don’t want to,” she says with uncharacteristic seriousness.

“I don’t think it works that way, for this,” Sokka says glumly, chewing on his cheek as fidgety nervousness rolls through him again. It would be great to just never do anything that feels unpleasant, but…Sokka doesn’t see a world where he can avoid doing this and keep doing Zuko.

He winces. Spirits, Toph is rubbing off on him.

“Whatever,” Toph waves a dismissive hand in his general direction as she climbs to her feet. “That’s you’re problem then. But for the record?” She pauses at the edge of the doorway next to him. “I told you so.”

“What?” Sokka frowns, trying to remember what—

“Get carving, Lover Boy.”

Sokka lets out a manly squawk of outrage, then buries his face in his hands as Katara whips toward him in horrified shock.

“Sokka,” Katara says anxiously. “What did she mean? Why is Toph talking about carving? Sokka? Sokka!”

&#45;-

Sokka can’t relax that night. Restless energy from an afternoon not spent training—and that’s the *only reason, Toph*, thank you very much—is twitching through his limbs. He eventually gives up when the others start to wind down for the night, slipping out of the house so as to not be the one to keep them up.

The night air is finally cool enough to be enjoyable, the breeze even prompting a light prickle of raised hair over his skin. Sokka settles on one of the wide porch railings so that he can sit in Yue’s light, head tipped back toward her. Would she be doing that crinkle-eyed, suppressed laugh of hers over the ridiculousness that he’s found himself in? Sokka thinks she would be amused, to see him so flustered and off-balance this way. He thinks she would have enjoyed Toph’s sense of humor, its brashness and boldness.

Or maybe Yue would be envious and resentful of Toph’s refusal to work within the systems that Yue spent so much time learning. Maybe she would be angry that Sokka was hung up on an enemy before, and is even more hung up on him now. Even if Sokka isn’t really sure that Zuko qualifies for that title, anymore. Even if Sokka isn’t really sure what else to call refer to him as. Can there be anything other than allies and enemies, when the whole world is at war?

Sokka isn’t entirely surprised when Aang eventually pads out to join him, jumping easily up onto the railing in a little gust of wind to sit quiet and contemplative next to Sokka.

“You’re going to be fine,” Aang offers, voice confident but quiet enough that Sokka could choose to just let it be a statement and not an opening, if he isn’t in the mood.

He probably shouldn’t be, after earlier, after all the ways he’s still feeling too exposed, but —“Maybe.”

The Avatar gives him a small smile. “You care about Zuko. And so does Iroh, right? The rest will work itself out.”

“I hope so,” Sokka sighs, trying to let the words lift some of the worry off his shoulders.

“You should bring him a gift, or something,” Aang suggests after a moment’s thought.

“What? Why?”

“He’s inviting you over in order to meet you!” Aang exclaims, bright with enthusiasm. “You want to make a good impression, right?”

“…But I’ve already met him. Multiple times.” And between the ship and the abbey and that little room, Iroh has met far more of Sokka than either of them would probably like.

“Sure, but you haven’t met him like this, right?”

“Like what?”

“As Zuko’s—” Aang is momentarily at a loss. “—person.”

Sokka opens his mouth in automatic denial, then slowly closes it because…shit, that is what this meeting is going to be, isn’t it? Fuck. “…What kind of stuff should I bring?”

If Sokka doesn’t want to mess up the tenuous space he and Zuko have carved out for themselves then Sokka needs to actually do this thing and do it right. Which means he needs to figure out what he’s going to say, and how he’s going to act, and how to do it all without upsetting the one person Sokka is entirely positive he could get Zuko to admit to caring about. It's...going to be a long night. Sokka can’t just run from this conversation, for all that he might have fantasized about it with Zuko and entertained a brief moment of hope with Toph, but he has no idea what Iroh is going to want to ask, what Sokka can possibly say.

And he needs to get it right. Sokka needs to go back to the teashop and that little apartment more than he needs to nurse the sting of his embarrassment. Those are the places where Zuko is, and Sokka doesn't want to lose them. Sokka needs to make sure that Zuko is okay, needs to know where things stand between them now that Zuko’s world has changed. And Iroh is important to Zuko, Iroh's opinion matters to Zuko. Which forces Sokka to, reluctantly, admit that he does, in fact, want Iroh to like him.

Fuck.

This could be hard, because Sokka isn’t sure that *he* can like Iroh back. Sokka feels that way about all the adults in Zuko’s life, really, but especially about the sole one who seems to have ever claimed to care for him.

&#45;-

Sokka feels as nervous and jittery walking the familiar route to the Blooming Petal as he did months ago waiting for the first light of dawn to start the invasion of the North. Which isn’t exactly an encouraging thought to have before joining the Dragon of the West for tea. His hands are warm from carrying a tight package of spiced meat buns and evening shadows make the streets seem half-foreign, calling to mind the last time Sokka came here at night. Which is also not a great thought for starting off a chat with Zuko’s uncle, even if it’s a reminder of all the reasons Sokka is enduring the conversation in the first place.

Iroh is waiting outside the Blooming Petal, clearly intending for them to talk there rather than at the apartment. Sharp yellow eyes watch as he approaches. Spirits, how the two of them weren’t immediately pegged as firebenders by Ba Sing Se’s intake agents is one more piece of the city's incompetency than Sokka has the capacity for right now. Iroh’s face is impassive and Sokka feels an unwelcome bolt of fear. Iroh might be doing his best to seem like everyone’s grandfather these days, but Sokka can’t forget that this man was a general before he was ever Zuko’s uncle, especially not after hearing Toph rattle off his list of titles. What does someone need to do, to earn the right to call themselves a Dragon?

“Good evening, Master Sokka,” Iroh says when Sokka slows to a reluctant stop in front of him, the words pleasant and bland.

“Uh, hi. Good—good evening.” Great start. Stellar. Sokka tries to subtly clear the squeakiness from his throat, praying that his next words are remotely close to his usual register.

“I thought we could talk here,” Iroh says, gesturing Sokka through the open door. “I closed tonight, so there should be plenty of privacy.” And no Zuko, which is likely the real reason. Sokka doesn’t think Iroh wants Zuko around for whatever this is going to be, which makes Sokka's pulse flutter with nerves even as it springs to mind a few things of his own that he could say without Zuko present. The man isn’t likely to kick his nephew out of their apartment, and apparently they both know that Zuko wouldn’t be unable to make himself leave.

Sokka silently obeys, trailing Iroh over the shop floor and into the kitchen. He nervously notes every twitch and movement of Iroh’s shoulders, trying to read his mood beneath that veneer of geniality. Iroh is better at concealing his body language than Zuko is, though, and Sokka is struggling to watch as closely as he could. He can’t seem to keep his eyes from bouncing around the kitchen, trying to imagine it bustling with the day’s activities and full of the coworkers he’s heard about, with a hum of customers just on the other side of the door. Sokka doesn’t like that he feels off balance being here instead of the apartment, like Sokka is somehow invading Zuko’s space without him. Or walking onto Iroh’s turf.

There’s already tea steaming on the table, which makes Sokka relieved that he at least managed to show up on time and not make the man wait. Sokka knows enough from Zuko muttering about work that the only thing worse than fresh tea is over-steeped cold tea.

“I ah—here. These are for you,” Sokka blurts out, shoving the package across the table. Spirits, could Sokka be any more awkward?

“Thank you,” Iroh says mildly, reaching to unwrap the package. “There was no need for you to bring…spiced buns?”

“There’s a kind of spiced sauce mixed into the filling,” Sokka mutters, avoiding Iroh’s eyes. He should have done flowers. Aang had suggested flowers. Everyone loves flowers, don’t they? But it seemed like one of those things where there could be lots of odd Fire Nation symbolism for Sokka to mess up.

“I didn’t realize they made this in Ba Sing Se. These are very close to a Fire Nation dish.”

“Yeah. Not as spicy though.”

Sokka risks a glance up when Iroh doesn’t reply, fingers spasming beneath the table when he finds himself the object of a long, considering look. After an endless second Iroh makes a neutral, humming noise—which is itself something of a revelation, to realize where Zuko must have picked up the habit—and starts plating the buns and pouring the tea.

Iroh makes himself comfortable while Sokka fidgets and darts quick looks around the room. He keeps seeking some sign of Zuko in this place, keeps trying to picture Zuko in one of those corners, working at one of the stovetops, wiping down these counters. Keeps failing to make it fit.

“Thank you for coming here,” the General finally speaks, expression even but tone shaded with a formality that lets Sokka know the interrogation is beginning.

“You told me to,” Sokka can’t help pointing out, fiddling with his chopsticks.

“You didn’t have to.”

“Yes. I did.”

That earns Sokka another contemplative look and Sokka’s stomach flips. He can already tell that he’s going to be getting a lot of those looks, and he’s already at the brink of his tolerance for being so obviously studied and picked apart and judged.

“I have already talked with my nephew, and I will say the same to you that I said to him. There are things I will tell you that you will listen to, and there are things I will ask that you will provide answers for.”

“Okay,” Sokka agrees warily. He really wishes he knew what to expect. He really wishes he had seen Zuko first. Zuko doesn’t do well with anything that close to an order, in Sokka’s experience.

Iroh takes a slow sip of his tea, appearing to gather his thoughts which Sokka is pretty sure is a nice piece of performance art. There’s no way the General doesn’t already have everything he wants to say at hand. “I will ask plainly,” he finally says. “What are your intentions toward my nephew?”

Sokka drops one of his chopsticks in surprise. “My—what?”

“Your intentions. You are an ally of the Avatar. You have been a captive of the Fire Nation. You and my nephew fought on opposite sides of the siege of the North.”

“Well, Zuko wasn’t really *on* a—” Sokka bites his tongue when Iroh slowly raises an eyebrow at the interruption.

“You have been enemies in the past,” the General continues. “And just when my nephew is trying to start a new life in a new city, surrounded by those who would hurt him if they knew his history, you find him. So. What are your intentions, Master Sokka?”

“I…” Sokka flounders as Iroh’s words hit like a fist he never saw coming, landing all the harder for the fact that he should have known to look for it.

The General watches him struggle, finally setting down his teacup with a firm knock of porcelain on wood. “Are you trying to use him to advance the Avatar’s agenda?”

“What?” Sokka jerks back, dropping his second chopstick. “No!” Sokka might daydream sometimes—*all the time*, a traitorous voice whispers—about the difference between Zuko being with them instead of just not against them. But Sokka wouldn’t *try* anything. Not on purpose.

“You would not be the first person to attempt to use him for your own aims,” Iroh says, and Sokka doesn’t think he’s imagining the crackle of fire beneath the words. “I will not be any more lenient with you because of your youth than I was with them.”

“I’m not,” Sokka insists, voice climbing a few more octaves than he would like. Sokka can't get hung up on betraying how affected he is, though, not when he's quietly scrambling to slot Iroh’s words into months of hoarded lines from letters and offhand comments about dinner parties and power and influence and being thirteen and wounded and—maybe—alone.

“You tracked my nephew down in Ba Sing Se, when no one knew of our presence in the city.”

“I didn’t know he was here,” Sokka tries to explain, tightly aware that there’s no way he could ever prove it. “It wasn’t on purpose.”

“How…convenient.”

“Yeah. It was,” Sokka glares before snatching up his tea and forcing himself to take a sip and calm down because fuck, he needs Zuko’s uncle to like him. “How much did Zuko tell you?” Iroh purses his lips at Sokka’s daring to ask a question. Or maybe at the hostility in it. Sokka refuses to relent on this, though. “I’m not going to say something to you that he didn’t want you to know. What did he tell you?”

Iroh is expressionless for more heartbeats than Sokka cares to count before finally responding, “He told me that you wrote letters, for a time. That his interest, at least, in something more than letters was prior to the North. That you were the one to find him, here.”

“Okay,” Sokka says slowly, quickly sorting out what that leaves out of bounds. He’s surprised that Zuko let himself get pinned down on even that much, to be honest. But Sokka can work with this. “Okay. You keep asking about my intentions. I don’t…I don’t know what you want me to say. I just want what I’ve always wanted. Just…to spend time with him.”

Iroh makes a neutral-but-doesn’t-think-you’re-telling-the-whole-truth noise, and Sokka feels a flash of annoyance that *that* is the first Fire Nation neutral-but-saying-more-than-it-seems sound that he’s finally able to parse.

“Why is it so hard for you to believe that someone would like him?” Sokka snaps, fidgety and short-tempered to be caught saying these things to Iroh and not Zuko. To be saying them and have them doubted.

“That is not what I struggle with.” Sokka crosses his arms in annoyance, gesturing for Iroh to go on, which might not be the best way to be getting on the man’s good side, but fuck the General’s good side right now. “You and I saw each other, at the North Pole.”

“I remember,” Sokka says curtly. He’ll never forget all that happened at the Oasis, not when he can look to the sky every night and see the results of it. Not when he can close his eyes and see clear as the moment it happened the way Yue looked choking for air that was never going to come.

“I recall that you were very…distraught.”

Sokka’s eyes narrow. “When my friend died?” Because *Sokka* recalls Iroh being the one to help her do it. The one to show her the way, to goad Zhao into striking the fatal blow. Sokka’s anger over the North never truly went away. Might never go away. It just settled, dormant with distance and the urgency of finding Appa. It’s raising its head now, though.

Iroh hesitates, the first break in his confidence Sokka has seen, and maybe the man can sense that he's treading toward dangerous ground. “You seemed quite attached to each other.”

“She was my *friend*.”

“Is Zuko?”

Sokka pulls up short, reaching for an immediate answer and finding less certainty than he would like. He and Zuko have never defined whatever it is they’re doing. Shit, Sokka has actively avoided Toph’s attempts to pin a description onto it, because descriptions always felt like they'd come along with obligations and Sokka isn't sure that Zuko wants any more of those. It’s never really been a problem, before, but now Sokka is cursing himself for not pushing the issue.

But...is it really so uncertain? From the beginning, when it was just letters and nothing more, before they knew each other, Zuko was a friend. Sokka doesn’t think that has stopped, or changed, regardless of what else has.

“Yes,” he finally says, putting every bit of confidence he can into the one word.

Iroh studies Sokka’s face before finally picking up a spiced bun, contemplating it before taking a delicate bite. “There are many kinds of friendship.”

“I know.” Sokka is well aware of the spectrum, from his exasperated affection toward Toph to his easy familiarity with Aang to the quiet closeness he had with Yue to whatever it is that he holds toward Zuko.

“And so we come back to your intentions,” Iroh says quietly, finishing his bun as Sokka sighs. “I will ask a different way, perhaps, since I recall how the—impulsivity, of youth, does not always lend itself to well-considered intent.”

Is that a jab at yesterday? Which was *not* Sokka’s fault, it’s Zuko’s fucking door and the Blooming Petal’s fucking schedule. And Iroh has a key, anyway.

“Master Sokka.” Iroh waits until he has Sokka’s visible attention. “What would you have my nephew be, to you?”

*Mine*. Except Sokka can’t say that, not to Iroh, not when he’s never said it aloud to anyone yet.

“Do you picture a future together? A life where he will join you?”

Maybe his tea was poisoned, because Sokka is suddenly finding it almost impossible to keep his hands from shaking. He tries to hold onto his composure, tries not to give too much away because he still isn’t sure where he stands with Iroh. Nowhere great, based on how it's feeling for Zuko’s uncle to be pushing Sokka toward the kinds of things Sokka hasn’t allowed himself to even glance at. The kind of things that Sokka has leapt for in the past and fractured himself trying to grasp. Suddenly being plunged into thinking about them again after months of purposeful self-denial—Spirits, Sokka feels like he’s burning up in all the possible futures he knows better than to hope for.

Iroh sighs, a flicker of dissatisfaction breaking through his mask of neutral calm before he takes a sip of his tea, the motion pulling the picture of composure back around him. He nods, sitting back in apparent acceptance that Sokka isn’t able to say anything, not to him at least. Sokka is painfully aware that this is not how you make someone like you, especially when that person is already uncertain whether you’re worth keeping around.

“Be careful what you ask of him,” Iroh finally orders, voice quiet, solemn, a little open in its worry. “My nephew will break himself against your expectations if you aren’t.”

“Zuko doesn’t need me asking him for things to do that,” Sokka mutters, fidgeting with his plate and wishing his chopsticks weren’t on the floor because it would be great to hide behind food right now. “He does it all by himself. He already has enough expectations.”

“Hm.” Iroh considers another spiced bun before placing it back down on his plate. “Maybe so. My nephew has always cared too much for others, and not enough for himself. Even as a child, he wanted nothing but to please.”

Sokka forcefully bites his tongue to keep his reply trapped behind his teeth and his glare on his plate. It makes him feel sharp and far too reckless for dealing with someone like Iroh to hear the man so easily acknowledge what Zuko is like and to act like it’s just a little thing, like it's nothing. He wants to rage at the General for never bothering to ask *why* Zuko was so desperate to please. He wants to smash the pot of tea at Iroh not thinking to take a child away from a place that would hurt him until after it was already done.

But Sokka strangles it all back down into his throat. He doesn’t know what Iroh knows, and Sokka will not be the one to reveal Zuko’s secrets.

“He would do much, to please you, I think,” Iroh adds, voice going hard, like maybe he caught some of the resentment Sokka is feeling. There’s a warning and a threat there, but Sokka’s anger is already sparked and lit.

“And you.” It’s satisfying, the way Iroh’s chopsticks stutter, just a little. “Zuko will please you, too. It’s your expectations he’s living for right now.” Sokka doesn’t even try to keep the bitterness from his words.

“We are starting a new life,” Iroh says after a beat, quiet and careful in a way he hasn’t been yet. Good.

“Are you?” Sokka challenges. “The Dragon of the West starting over within the walls of Ba Sing Se.” He doesn’t really know what he’s saying, but judging by Iroh’s reaction he still managed to hit some kind of mark. Sokka really needs to ask Toph about that Dragon thing. “Did you even bother to ask Zuko if he *wanted* to start over?”

Iroh frowns and runs a thumb over his chopsticks and doesn’t say anything, which is answer enough for someone who has spent so much time with Zuko’s barbed silences. But the lack of a reply still makes Sokka even more upset.

“He—you—ugh.” A deep breath that does nothing to calm him. “Zuko is one of the best firebenders I’ve ever seen. He is *amazing* with his dao. He cares so much about everyone around him. He’s so selfless sometimes it’s *stupid*. He knows about politics and trade and— and so many things. And you want him to serve *tea* the rest of his life? Zuko doesn’t even *like* tea!”

“He likes jasmine,” Iroh protests softly, face drawn at the edges.

“Because you do!”

It’s another shot in the dark based on offhand comments and the steaming pot in front of them, but Sokka has that feeling like he gets when he knows his boomerang is going to fly perfectly true before it even leaves his hand. All the pieces are slotting into place without active thought and Sokka isn’t going to question it.

The silence in the wake of his accusation is huge and loud in its emptiness. Sokka forces himself to sit back, actively pulling himself back down from his frustration, taking careful breathes and wondering how much he just fucked everything up. This isn't how you make someone like you.

At least Iroh seems deep in thought rather than actively angry, though he also doesn't look exactly happy to be here right now, which makes two of them. Spirits, Sokka is really going to need to work out how to have civil interactions with the man, assuming Zuko’s uncle doesn’t kick him to the curb after this. Sokka knows Zuko cares about Iroh, would need Sokka to be able to get along with the General because of that. Sokka can manage it if he has to, for Zuko. He knows he can, even if all Sokka can be right now is mad.

Iroh finally stirs, picking up his cup, the act of sipping tea seeming to return some vigor to his face and body. “You have given me much to think about, Master Sokka.” Sokka just grunts in reply. “I thank you for your candor.”

“You’re…welcome?” Sokka feels the last sparks of his anger wisp away in the face of the genuine consideration Iroh seems to be giving his words.

“I would ask one last thing of you, if you would allow it.” Iroh’s tone is less rigidly neutral than before, less tightly protective.

“Okay…” Sokka feels a stab of sympathy for where Iroh must be coming from, the protectiveness and wariness, now that he isn’t on the receiving end of it anymore. Sokka is pretty sure he’s been reacting from the same place.

“I would ask you to be careful, in asking my nephew for what you want.” Iroh drops a pointed glance toward Sokka’s linen-wrapped wrists, and it takes him a moment but then Sokka flushes absolutely crimson as he realizes that Iroh knows what’s beneath them. That he either saw or Zuko told, and Sokka wants to go find the nearest body of water to throw himself into so he can die alone with his humiliation.

But Iroh’s face is grave rather than horrified or disgusted, tone openly concerned in a way that forces Sokka to pay attention despite his embarrassment. “Zuko has been hurt by the touch of fire before. That is no secret, I’m sure, for you. Or for anyone who has seen him. It would break him to hurt someone he cared about in the same way.”

Sokka struggles to find his voice, to set aside his own acute mortification and focus on Zuko, finally clearing his throat enough to get out, “I know.”

“There is nothing wrong with wanting what you want, as long as both parties are consenting.” Sokka wonders if it’s possible to blush so hard that he passes out, because he feels like it might be happening right now. “It is not shameful. You are certainly not the first person to ask for such a thing.”

“Spirits,” Sokka mutters, finally breaking and hiding his face behind his hands.

“But it can be hard, in the midst of passion, to moderate.” Iroh continues. Maybe the new strategy is to drive Sokka away by making it so that Sokka can never risk making eye contact with him ever again. “For you. But especially for a firebender.”

“Zuko won’t hurt me,” Sokka protests into his hands.

“He won’t want to.”

“He won’t.” It’s a correction, not agreement. Sokka feels a potentially disturbing level of confidence in the statement that he should probably force himself to pick apart at some other time. It’s just...Iroh might know firebenders, but Sokka knows he hasn't seen Zuko the way Sokka has*.* That maybe Iroh knows Zuko with fire, but Sokka knows Zuko with heat, has seen how he is with it, has seen him lost in passion with and without it. Sokka feels it in his bones that heat is different for Zuko than fire.

But still. “I’ll be careful.” Because Sokka is suddenly painfully, acutely aware, sitting across from Zuko’s worried Uncle, that Zuko would shatter himself trying to please Sokka, if he were sufficiently motivated enough. That Zuko probably already is bending himself around Sokka, the same way Sokka can see him doing with Iroh, and Sokka's just been too caught up in his own head to realize the extent of it.

“Thank you,” Iroh says, relieved, for a moment looking as exhausted as Sokka feels. “All I want for him is happiness.”

“Me too,” Sokka sighs. Maybe one day he and Iroh will even see the same path there.

## Chapter 21: Without Consent

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

No particular warnings for this one!

### Text

Sokka is anxious to find Zuko when he finally escapes the Blooming Petal, the taste of jasmine tea bright and bitter on his tongue. He doesn’t have to look far. Zuko is hovering next to the alley when Sokka bursts out onto the street, and snaps upright, swaying forward despite planted feet as Sokka stumbles to a surprised stop of his own. Did Iroh tell Zuko to stay away? Or was that just as close as Zuko could manage to bring himself?

“Sokka,” Zuko says, too much in the word for Sokka to parse, relief and nervousness and warmth and tightness, maybe, and so many other things.

“Zuko.” His own voice sounds thin and strung out to his ears. Which is fairly representative of how he feels, actually.

Zuko moves like Sokka saying his name was some kind of permission, striding over and grabbing Sokka’s hand with his usual determined purposefulness. The gesture cuts through some of Sokka's roiling thoughts, giving him a little thrill at the way it always feels like touching Sokka is something special and intentional for Zuko.

Zuko would normally be pulling Sokka to the apartment or their training courtyard by now, but instead he stares down at their loosely clasped hands, his brow tense. Maybe Zuko doesn’t quite know what to do next, either, when they're both so far outside of their usual patterns, when Zuko is such a creature of habit and routine—surpsingly so, for someone who can be so impulsive—and Sokka has become so comfortable in the habits they've built. Or maybe Zuko’s conversation with Iroh left him just as tangled as Sokka’s did—Spirits, Sokka still can’t figure out what he's supposed to feel about the mix of supported and threatened and intensely awkward he just experienced.

“Are you okay,” Sokka finally asks, trying to read anything in Zuko’s downturned face. “I’m fine.”

Sokka can hear that it’s an automatic response—it always is—and that it’s not entirely true— it usually isn’t. But he can also feel the way Zuko threads his fingers more tightly between Sokka’s, and see the relative looseness in his shoulders, so Sokka doesn’t press it, just makes a wordless noise of acknowledgment and squeezes back.

Zuko flicks a quick, nervous glance up, a flash of gold that Sokka might have imagined if he weren’t looking for it so closely. “Are *you* okay?

“I…could be worse,” Sokka says after a moment.

Zuko huffs, a dark, humorless laugh. “Always.” He gives a little tug on Sokka’s hand and Sokka obeys the silent request to move into Zuko’s space, suddenly craving closeness and assurance and to ground himself against the feel and heat of Zuko’s body.

Except…after what Iroh said—

“Actually, can we…go talk somewhere?”

Fuck, Sokka should have phrased that better. Sokka is an *idiot.* He can *see* Zuko's sudden spike of anxiety at the question, the way Zuko's attention snaps to the few inches of space still between them.

“It’s not anything bad,” Sokka rushes to add, really hoping that those words are true. “It’s just…your uncle said some things…”

Zuko's shoulders slowly lower as he glowers at the teashop door, looking somewhere between annoyed and wary, which...Sokka sympathizes with. Zuko's scowl deepends when he pivots in the direction of the apartment, a sharp, annoyed exhale crossing his lips as they both realize that they can’t go to his room like usual, because it's nighttime and Iroh is around so it's not technically Zuko's room anymore. The last thing any of them need is another moment of privacy invaded.

“Here,” Sokka finally says, giving Zuko’s hand a gentle pull. “This way.” He knows where they can go. And he needs to start this conversation sooner rather than later, before he loses his nerve entirely.

&#45;-

Zuko takes comfort in the familiar coolness of Sokka’s fingers against his own as they walk, trying to calm the too-fast beat of his heart at the fact that Sokka would leave a conversation with Uncle and then stop himself from touching Zuko. He concentrates on the slide of their skin together—so not all touching, then, just *initiating* touching, or maybe not-hands kinds of touching, and Zuko isn’t helping himself out here—as their feet follow the well-worn path to the courtyard that Zuko has started thinking of as theirs.

Sokka leads them to the lone bench, a half-step ahead in Zuko’s usual position, sitting with a sigh, settling sideways onto the seat with bent knees and motioning Zuko to join him.

“No,” Sokka says, when Zuko makes to drop his hand and take the edge of space beyond his feet. “Like—”

Sokka touches him then as easy as breathing, thank *everything,* and Zuko lets himself relax a fraction in the darkness as Sokka nudges him and moves him and repositions him until Zuko is sitting to his liking. Zuko ends up between Sokka’s bent knees, his own feet planted on either side of Sokka’s hips, both of them surrounded by and cradling the heat of the other. It’s nice, and the intimacy of it further loosens the tight kernel of unease that’s been lodged beneath Zuko’s ribs since Uncle first walked in on them.

“Are you sure you’re okay?” Sokka asks, voice even and familiar in the darkness. “Did everything with your uncle go alright?”

A difficult question to answer. Zuko hasn’t been cast from what family he has left in shame and dishonor, and he hasn’t been able to look Uncle in the face because Uncle will now never not know far too much about what Zuko does in bed. “It was…better than I expected.”

“You guys are okay, then?”

“…As much as we ever are.” Zuko isn’t sure if ‘okay’ has ever really described their relationship, not the way Sokka probably means it.

“What did he want to talk about?”

Zuko grunts, wishing he could just concentrate on the feel of Sokka’s thighs alongside his body, very much *not* wanting to talk about Uncle right now. “You,” he finally says. “Us, I guess. Other…stuff.” Like safe sex, but Zuko shakes that memory away because it's just—too much, when they’re woven together like this.

Sokka hums, guiding Zuko’s hand to settle over his wrist wraps, the linen carrying the warmth of his body and hiding the already-fading shape of Zuko’s fingers on Sokka’s skin. “Other stuff like this?”

“…Fuck.” Sokka lets out a surprised bark of laughter that Zuko can’t appreciate when he’s feeling too much like Uncle just closed some kind of trap around him. “You too?”

“Probably not quite the same thing. Considering.” The words send Zuko into a small spiral of panic over what Uncle could have said to the…recipient and cause of Zuko’s potential loss of control. Agni's balls, maybe they *should* have jumped out of that window together yesterday. “But he did say some stuff, and…” Zuko goes motionless at the reluctant seriousness in Sokka’s tone. “Zuko, can I ask you something?”

“Okay…” Zuko agrees warily, sneaking a quick glance at Sokka’s face even though he can see little more than shadows in the darkness. Maybe he should light a flame for them. Except Zuko thinks he might want the protection of being unseen, if Sokka’s bracing breath is anything to judge by.

“Zuko, that stuff. The heat stuff. When I ask you to, um, mark me. Like that. You’re…you’re okay with it, right?”

Zuko…doesn’t understand the question, is suddenly hyperaware of his own hand still wrapped loosely around Sokka’s wrist.

“It’s not, ah, something that I—make you do?”

How would Sokka…you can’t *make* someone firebend…

“I want to make sure that it’s…that you want it, too. That it’s, you know.” Sokka’s forearm tenses. “Consensual.”

*That* is an Uncle word, and Zuko can’t stop his hiss of startled anger. “Agni’s tits,” Zuko bites out, furious that Uncle said something to Sokka to make him doubt—whatever it is he’s doubting. “I *told* him—” So much. Too much. Not enough, apparently. “Yes,” he grinds out, trying and failing to moderate his tone. “It’s—yes. It makes you feel good.”

“That’s good,” Sokka says in a careful voice that very much does not match his words. Zuko can feel the tension where Sokka’s body is pressed against his own, knows that his own posture is going rigid. “I want to make sure that you feel good, too, though.”

Zuko gapes, helpless. Has Sokka not been paying attention when they’re together? He’s taken Zuko apart in so many ways. Has Sokka not *noticed*? The idea that anything they’ve done together wouldn’t feel good, that Zuko doesn’t…where is this *coming* from? What did Uncle *say*?

“It won’t make me feel good, if you do things just because I want them,” Sokka explains, which makes no sense. Why would something not feel good just because Sokka wants it? What—what is *happening*?

“But. You like it…” How is Zuko supposed to know what to do, if he can’t do the things Sokka wants? He can feel his breath starting to get too shallow, anxiety digging into his chest. Is he just supposed to just *guess*?

“Zuko.” He cringes from the edge of exasperation in Sokka’s voice. “I don’t ever want you to do more than you’re comfortable with, or more than you want to do, just because I asked for it.”

“I don’t mind this,” Zuko cautiously tries, bracing himself. He isn’t sure what Sokka is after, here, but hearing his own words, Zuko is pretty sure he isn’t saying the right thing.

“I don’t want you to just not mind,” Sokka pushes back and Zuko feels like he’s going to crawl out of his own skin, knowing that he’s putting that undertone of frusration in Sokka’s voice and not knowing *how*, which means he can’t *stop*. “I’m not going to be upset if you don’t want to do something that I suggest. Zuko, it would kill me to find out you were just… pretending to be into something, for me.”

“I’m not, though,” Zuko protests, trying to make his voice strong with conviction when most of him feels small with anxiousness and confusion. Does Sokka…does Sokka want to *stop*? Just the heat? Or—or—

Zuko squeezes his eyes shut, trying to breathe through the hectic pulse of his inner fire. Sokka takes his own seeking-patience breath, so big that Zuko can feel it move through Sokka’s whole body in all the places they’re pressed together. Agni’s balls, Zuko doesn’t know what he’s supposed to *say.*

“Zuko. Do you like what we do?”

“Yes,” Zuko says immediately, latching onto this one thing that makes sense in all that Sokka is saying. He tries to beat down his panic, tries not to get ahead of himself even when part of him is already flinching away from what’s coming. Sokka hasn’t said anything about stopping, not yet, and he’s here and touching Zuko even if he didn’t do it before and why would Sokka have them sitting like this if he were about to—if he didn’t want to—

“And…do you only like it because of me?” Sokka presses. “Or would you want it with someone else?”

Is…is Sokka saying that *he* wants to do these things with someone else? *Is* there a someone else? Zuko had just assumed he was the only…but Agni’s flaming dick, Zuko never actually *asked*. Fuck, *fuck,* Sokka is so amazing who *wouldn’t* want to be with him, and why would he want just Zuko when he could—

“Zuko?”

“No!” Zuko bursts out, all his confused desperation breaking free. “I don’t! I don’t want this with anyone else, Sokka. I only want it with you.” He wraps his fingers over Sokka’s wrist with tight urgency, heat prickling behind his eyes. “Sokka, do you—I can stop. If you don’t want it. I didn’t mean to, if I—lost control, or—I’m sorry, I’m *sorry*, I didn’t—I can *stop,* I promise, just don’t—"

“No, no, Zuko, no,” Sokka says, wrists wrenching out of Zuko’s grip and pulling a small sound of agony past Zuko’s lips before Sokka’s fingers are clasping around Zuko’s forearms and Zuko’s heart is going to *explode*. “You never—everything you do is perfect.
