And in doing so, Zuko would just be throwing himself even faster at the moment he knows will come eventually, the one where he’s going to need to stare down his loyalties, old and new, and decide which of his most important things still have power over him and which he can no longer hold onto. “…No.”

Sokka nods like that’s the answer he expected, and Zuko doesn’t like that he can’t tell if the gesture is disappointed or relieved. “So, okay, what would you do—and imagine in this situation that you don’t have your bending—if you had to—”

“You’re sure that you’re being careful?” Zuko can’t help but cut in, tensing around the quiet, creeping reminder that moments with Sokka might feel like they’re divorced from the rest of the world but that they aren’t, not really.

“Yes,” Sokka waves off his concern. “Now pay attention, you’re surrounded by four enemies here, you can’t be this distracted.”

“Fine,” Zuko sighs, even in his worry unable to look away from the way Sokka grins while teasing. “Where am I, again?”

&#45;-

Sokka began losing the battle to hold onto coherent thought almost the second the apartment door closed this afternoon. He's leaning back against the door, pleasure boiling low in his stomach, barely able to keep his eyes open and simultaneously unable to tear them away from the sight of Zuko on his knees. Zuko is taking his sweet time for all his decisive intent, mouth hot and wet and making Sokka’s voice crack as Zuko drags ragged gasp after choked moan out of him. Fuck, Zuko is going to take Sokka apart just like this, slowly and steady and relentless, and Sokka is *so* here for it.

Zuko starts doing that twisting thing with his tongue, humming in the back of his throat when Sokka jerks in response, and then his fingers—Sokka’s brain goes completely blank, hands scrambling for purchase, for anchor, as sensation and pleasure jump along his limbs, running down his spine. Sokka’s body starts to twitch and shudder and Spirits, he’s so close, so close, and the sight of Zuko like this on top of everything else he is feeling, it’s too much. Sokka's left hand finds a grip on the doorframe, his right hand dropping to cradle Zuko’s face, and— Zuko is across the room before Sokka even registers the loss of him.

Sokka flounders, flailing at the sudden loss of sensation, mind struggling to catch up, offering nothing more useful than disjointed pieces. Zuko's already-pale face completely white, caught between stunned and confused. His chest heaving, shallow and far, far too fast. The air shimmering around his hands, like it's being superheated by flames Zuko can’t let free. Zuko staring back at him, wide-eyed and beseeching.

Sokka doesn’t know what to do, what's going on. He holds his breath and freezes and makes a point of not moving or twitching or doing absolutely anything at all, because Zuko looks like he is teetering on some edge right now that Sokka had no idea they were approaching. Zuko was *right there* and now he’s as far away as he can get and still be in the room, and looking more than halfway to panic, and Sokka doesn’t know *why*, all Sokka did was—

*…Fuck.*

Zuko is the one to move first, licking his lips and rasping out a barely audible, “I’m sorry.”

“No, *I’m* sorry,” Sokka says, distress twisting in his gut in place of pleasure, his right hand burning as if it were—well. “I didn’t think, I didn’t mean to…” Sokka obviously knows about Zuko’s scar, but he’s touched it before, kissed it before, and nothing even close to this has ever happened. That something about what they were doing in particular could have triggered Zuko…Sokka feels like he’s going to be sick.

“I don’t…I’m sorry,” Zuko repeats, shaky and still holding himself like he’s ready to go out the window at any moment. “I don’t know why…why that…”

“Zuko…” Sokka’s voice cracks, uncertainty suddenly making him grateful for the support of the door at his back. “Really?” Sokka slowly closes his right hand into a fist, tucking it behind himself out of sight and hiking his pants up with the other because now is really not the time to be dick-out disheveled.

Zuko stares for a long beat, brow tight, before suddenly blinking in understanding. A moment of wide-eyed surprise, then his whole body jerks in an immediate denial. “It wasn’t—this isn’t—No. This isn't—It’s not like it was like…that…”

"Zuko," Sokka says, fighting to keep his tone even. "It doesn’t have to be exactly the same, for something to bother you. There doesn't need to be a reason.” There’s a quiet but urgent question underneath Sokka’s words, one he needs not to bloom into panic, because if Zuko is bothered by this then Sokka *needs to know*. He would do almost anything—maybe actually anything, and isn’t that terrifying to suddenly realize—to avoid being the one to put that kind of fear in Zuko’s eyes.

Zuko just fidgets his hands together, though, looking tense and distressed in too many ways for Sokka to be able to name, his fingers starting to strangle each other the longer the silence drags. Sokka cautiously pushes off the wall as the quiet grows into a sharp, suffocating thing. He slowly moves toward Zuko’s corner of the room, keeping both hands low and visible and as relaxed as he can make them. Zuko watches his approach with a mixture of wariness and uncertainty and rising stiffness.

“I’m not some animal that’s going to bite you,” Zuko snaps, words covered in that familiar anger that Sokka knows Zuko can always layer over everything he doesn’t want to feel.

“I didn’t say you were,” Sokka replies carefully, feeling even more unsure as he stops within reach but not so close that Zuko can’t get by him, if he wants to. He would normally try to soothe and distract from something like this, but this time he doesn't think he *can.* “Zuko, I don’t…this was an accident. I didn’t mean—”

“It’s fine.”

“No, it’s not *fine*,” Sokka says, immediately stepping back in apology and trying to rein back the vehemence of his words. “If you have—stuff. I need to know. I *want* to know.”

Zuko scowls, shifting restlessly, tone irritated and wary and eyes skating toward the window and Spirits, that sick feeling in Sokka’s gut is getting worse. “…Why.”

Sokka sighs, running his hands through his hair and struggling for calm. He doesn’t wholly trust Zuko to discern between anger at him and on his behalf on a good day, and this most certainly isn't one of those. But fuck, how many different roads can Sokka find to all the ways that Zuko doesn’t seem to care about himself? To all the ways Zuko seems to think he doesn't matter?

When he feels marginally more level—at least on the surface—Sokka slowly reaches out, taking Zuko’s hands in his. He’s relieved to find them warm but not too much, just normal firebender-hot. And he’s relieved enough to make his knees weak that Zuko doesn’t flinch from the contact, that he lets Sokka take his hands even if he looks distinctly uncertain about the whole thing.

“We’ve talked about the stuff that I want, and that I like,” Sokka finally says, trying to find a way to make his point without pressing Zuko so hard when he’s already feeling raw that Zuko closes himself off. “And what I don’t like. Right?”

“Yeah.” Zuko’s voice is still raspier than usual, but it sounds a bit less strangled and tight. Or maybe that's just wishful thinking, on Sokka's part.

“That goes both ways. It’s not just about what I need from you.” Zuko frowns at the words, looking even more unsure. “It’s what you need, too. This is about us feeling good together, Zuko, not you making me feel good.”

“I like making you feel good,” Zuko says immediately, an undeniable fact that Sokka normally deeply appreciates and currently wishes were maybe just a bit less true. Zuko sometimes seems to anchor to it with a single-minded intensity in a way that Sokka has been nagging at his thoughts as...maybe not all that great, actually, even if it always feels good at the time.

“I like it too,” Sokka says, searching Zuko’s eyes for understanding. “And I like doing that for you, too. You know that, right?” He barely holds in a gust of relief when Zuko nods. “But Zuko, it’s not a—a performance, or something. There’s no script to follow.” He tugs gently at Zuko’s hand to keep those gold eyes on him when they try to cut away. “You can stop something whenever you want. You can ask for whatever you want. Or say you don’t want to do something you’ve done before. That’s all *okay.* I won’t be upset, Zuko, I promise. I want to know. I want everything we do to feel as good for you as it does for me.”

Zuko’s vibrating tension slowly bleeds into tentative uncertainty as Sokka speaks, his fingers losing some of their stiffness, not quite intertwined with Sokka’s but not as rigid anymore, either. All good signs, even if when Zuko opens his mouth, searching for words, he eventually glances away without responding. Sokka holds back a sigh. He just...wishes it didn't feel like sometimes Zuko might not say no until it's already too late.

"I know you…that you always put others first,” Sokka finally says, ignoring Zuko’s sudden confusion. Of course he can’t recognize himself in the description. Of course. “But just…will you think about it? About what you want for you? And let me know?”

“I…Yes. Okay. Sure,” Zuko finally says. His fingers slowly wrap around Sokka's, exerting the barest bit of pressure, and the gesture does far more to ease Sokka’s tight anxiety than Zuko’s words do. Sokka studies Zuko’s face. It’s still too white, but it isn’t as tight now as it was before. And his breathing is no longer quite as frantic, even if it still seems too shallow.

“Do you want to lie down? Just to lie down?” Sokka asks. Even if the mood weren't thoroughly dead and buried, Sokka can clearly see Zuko’s lingering discomfort. He isn’t about to immediately test whether Zuko will actually say no when pressed. “We could… cuddle? Or nap? If that’s something you want.”

“I…Yeah. That…sounds nice.” Zuko's words are cautious and slow, but honest. And underselling his own wants, probably, if the way Zuko wraps himself around Sokka’s body is any indication. Zuko buries his face in the crook of Sokka’s neck the second they hit horizontal, cuddling close like he doesn’t ever want to let go. Or maybe that’s just how Sokka feels when his arms are full of volatile, angry, maybe-actually-terrifyingly-fragile firebender.

&#45;-

Zuko manages to drag himself back to his shift feeling marginally more like a human after napping in Sokka’s arms. But he’s still far more shaky and twitchy and just *off* than he ever wants to be in front of anyone, and especially the general public. Zuko hasn’t had an episode like that in…a long time. And the fact that it happened *then*, of all times? With *Sokka*, of all people? Sokka, who Zuko knows down to the core of his fire would never hurt him like that?

Except Zuko’s fucking subconscious hasn’t gotten the picture yet, apparently.

Zuko’s inner fire is restless, his throat thick with a sticky kind of nervousness that has no grounding in reality and no place to be directed. It’s a nauseating mixture that he can feel spinning all too easily into rage, because Zuko is feeling weak and helpless in a way he isn’t used to anymore. In a way that he doesn’t let happen anymore. He refuses to.

Which is all to say that Zuko has absolutely no fucks left to give when he walks back into the teashop to see that *man* smirking at Minji’s back as she hurries toward the kitchen, not even bothering to pick up the pencil that fumbles from her fingers onto the floor behind her.

Zuko hisses—audibly, judging by the flinch from the table by the door—and stalks forward. He snatches Minji’s pencil off the ground without breaking stride, because she will need it, and immediately snaps the cheap charcoal in half when someone shrieks with laughter across the room, because *fuck everything* today.

Minji turns at the sound, face splotchy, eyes darting from the broken pencil in Zuko’s hand to the floor to his face to something over his shoulder that Zuko can only assume is that *fucking* guy.

“What did he order?” Zuko demands, inner fire crawling thick and wild beneath his skin, ignoring the way Uncle straightens in alarm from his station by the tea canisters.

It takes Minji a few tries. “Tea.”

Zuko stomps toward the stove, grabbing a pot of boiling water, throwing in a haphazard handful of his least favorite leaves, and slamming it all onto a tray. He fixes Minji with a glare. “And?”

“…A bun,” she whispers, clearing her throat and darting quick glances toward Sung-Min and Uncle, both frozen in opposite corners and watching Zuko with two very different kinds of wariness.

Zuko grunts. He strides to the baked goods basket, grabs a flaky bun, and hurls it onto the tray. “What else?”

Minji stares at the crushed shape of what used to be a pastry. “A…muffin?”

Zuko grabs a corn squash muffin because *fuck* these corn squash muffins, whoever bakes these makes them so *fucking dry*. He drops it next to the bun in a vaguely muffin-shaped pile of crumbs. “Anything else?”

“N—No.”

“Good,” Zuko snarls, grabbing a to-go bag and the tray before Minji can even think of moving toward it. He storms past Sung-Min, regulars at the teashop already clearing a path before him, as well-trained as the soldiers on the *Wani* by this point to respond to the sound of his boots crashing against the floor. It's wood, instead of metal, but still satisfyingly resonant once Zuko figured out the right way to make his steps really shake the boards.

The *fucking* guy glances up and freezes in a deeply gratifying way.

“Your food,” Zuko spits, slamming down the tray. Crumbs spray over the table and mostly onto the man. “And your tea.” The man scrambles back from the table, anticipating a slosh of boiling water that never comes as Zuko delicately sets the teapot down. It’s one of Uncle’s favorites. “And your to-go bag.”

“I didn’t ask for that,” the man says inanely, stupidly, suicidally considering the hungry pull of Zuko’s inner fire.

“I don’t fucking care,” Zuko growls, swallowing back smoke. “Put your shit in it and leave.”

The guy glances at the pile of crumbs, wrong-footed and helpless. “But how do I take the tea?”

“Pour it on your crumbs*,* shithead*, do I look like I care?*”

Minji is hovering just inside the door, Uncle at her back, when Zuko crashes back into the kitchen, ignoring the stares from the other customers. His inner fire is darkly satisfied to have sent someone running like that in a way that probably isn’t good for Zuko to get used to. But it’s been a while since Zuko has been able to do that, to let this part of himself slip free.

“What?” Zuko snaps, bracing himself to endure a chirping lecture about the customer always being right from Minji and aphorisms about self-control from Uncle.

“Thank you.”

Zuko stutters, rage suddenly slipping with nothing to hold onto. “…For what?”

Minji just gives him a small, barely-there smile and presses another tray into his hands. “This one is for your friend.”

Zuko stares, utterly confused, but she doesn’t say anything more than that and Uncle looks like he’s retreating back to his corner, apparently with nothing to say. Zuko hesitates, finally pivoting back around without a word, his crackling frustration banking somewhat to see Jin watching from her usual table with raised eyebrows. This is what he needs, maybe. A few minutes with someone who expects absolutely nothing from him and has no opinion on who he used to be before or should be now.

“That was impressive,” Jin drawls as he sets her order down.

Zuko grunts in reply, which has never been a problem for Jin.

“Not a fan of his?”

Zuko glares.

“Hm.” She eyes him over the rim of her teacup. “Did he do something?”

“I don’t know,” Zuko shrugs. And he doesn’t fucking care, either.

“…Minji didn’t seem to like him either.”

At least he didn’t chase off a wanted suitor, then. Not that Zuko would have cared if he did.

“Lee.” He pauses, tilting to head to show that he’s listening even as he studies the tabletop. “You need to be careful, with that stuff.”

Zuko can’t stop his scoff of disbelief. Zuko can count on two swords and one raging inner flame why he doesn’t need to be careful when it comes to that asshole.

“I’m serious,” Jin presses. “I know you’re strong, and that you can fight, I saw the whole— sword thing.” Zuko winces at the reminder of Jet. Fuck, as if he needed his day to get any worse. “But it’s not all about physical strength. Not inside the walls.”

Zuko forces himself to take a breath to consider her words, which is a full breath more than he would give anyone except maybe Sokka when he’s feeling like this. “…What’s it about, then?”

“Money,” Jin says succinctly. “You can buy anything in Ba Sing Se with enough of it. And he has more than you.”

“So?” It’s testy and sharp, but Jin hears the genuine question beneath.

“It means if he wants, he can come after you with more resources.”

“I’d like to see him try,” Zuko mutters, some part of him eager for the simplicity of a fight, of just getting to lay someone out and fuck the consequences.

“Would you?” Jin challenges. “What if he comes after the Blooming Petal instead?”

“I don’t care about this place.”.

“But your uncle does.” Zuko scowls. She knows him too well, apparently. “Just…be careful. It’s good that you want to defend your friends and protect them from stuff like that.” She jerks her head toward the empty, crumb-covered seat across the room. “But there are ways to do it without blowing back on yourself.”

“I can handle it.” Except the rules aren’t the same, here. And Zuko can’t quite seem to remember that lately, can't seem to stop getting tangled in all the different rules for all the different parts of his life.

“You aren’t a refugee, anymore, Lee,” Jin says quietly, face soft and gentle in a way that Zuko hates to have directed at him. “You serve tea now.” And that’s all that anyone will see, she means. Lee the tea server. That’s all Zuko is supposed to *be.*

“…You’re right,” Zuko forces out, the words as bitter as the tea she’s sipping as she watches him with eyes far more understanding than he is comfortable with.

“There are other ways, Lee. It’s not like you just have to sit back and take everything. You just need to think a little different than you did before.”

Zuko thinks about a lot of things, that night, though nothing he particularly wants to wrap words around. He feels drawn too tight, like he’s on the verge of exploding out of his own skin. It’s yet another feeling he hasn’t had in a long time, one he would prefer to have left behind him. It's like there's too much of him, which...is a feeling he knows he never left.

Uncle had watched him with quiet concern since this afternoon, but he didn't comment on Zuko’s restlessness because he never does. Which Zuko really appreciates right now, because there’s no way he could possibly explain the origins of this particular mood. Not when Zuko barely understands it himself. Besides, this isn’t something that an uncle should be bothered with, and fuck, Zuko has never felt so painfully aware of the confines of the role he’s been trying to fit himself into as he does right now.

Zuko really has been following a script, hasn’t he? He has hoards and stacks of lines and cues and character notes for being the kind of nephew Uncle deserves, for being just Zuko for Sokka, for being Lee with Jin. And before that, trying to be an honorless refugee, a Crown Prince, a worthy son…Fuck, Zuko has done nothing *but* perform all his life. Sure, some of it has felt more natural than others, some of it fit more cleanly. But Agni, Zuko has tried to carve off so many pieces of himself for other people. He doesn’t know what the actual shape of himself is supposed to be, anymore.

He’s pretty sure this isn’t exactly what Sokka meant for him to think about, but it’s still where Zuko keeps finding himself. Feeling the confines of being Lee. Remembering how he played at being an uncomplicated refugee with Jet. Thinking of the constant craving to just be Zuko in Sokka’s arms, whatever that fuck that means, to be Zuko anymore. Unable to ignore the way he always feels rootless the minute Sokka leaves and there’s one less thing to anchor himself to again.

Zuko lets out a quiet sigh, inaudible even to his own ears beneath the rumbles of Uncle’s snoring. Zuko isn’t going to be able to sleep tonight. He can already tell that it won’t come easy, and that if he does manage to drift off…well, after the day Zuko’s had he doesn’t feel the need to revisit that particular memory in his dreams or to endure whatever his subconscious will twist it into. Zuko’s dreams have never been subtle, and he’s queued up some excellent material for them.

If Zuko were truly the kind of nephew that Uncle deserves he would stay here. Stay under the blankets and just breathe through it. Maybe meditate until Agni’s light starts the day. Maybe not have this problem to be dealing with in the first place, because he would be the simple, uncomplicated, tea-loving person that Uncle wants him to be.

Too bad Zuko has never really been a Good Nephew.

Zuko’s feet are soundless as he rolls to his feet, nothing but the soft rustle of cloth accompanying him as he slips out of bed and pads to his corner of the room. He quickly shucks his sleeping clothes, pulling on something tighter to the skin, darker, the kind of thing he hasn’t had reason to wear in months. Zuko doesn’t let himself think as he fishes a dark cowl from the bottom of his flimsy little chest of possessions. And he doesn’t let himself think as he straps his swords onto his back, and a mask over his face, the one that’s somehow still with him through everything. Zuko would almost think it were a good luck talisman, if he believed in that kind of thing. Or thought his luck would ever be good.

It’s just as easy to climb out the window as he imagined it would be. The hinges are silent because Zuko had some extra time on his hands one day, and some extra oil, and couldn’t think of a reason not to do something productive. And the stone is as rough and easy to find handholds on as he predicted, the alley private and dark at this time of night. Nearly an invitation, really.

Zuko hauls himself up instead of down, focusing on nothing except moving fluid and quiet onto the roof. The Lower Ring stretches out before him when he finally rolls over the edge, the night clear and crisp, stars bright with the kind of clarity that only comes with winter’s approach. The moon is dark, like a blessing, or permission, or maybe an excuse. The lack of light cuts down his vision, but not enough that Zuko can’t easily make the jump to the next roof, then the next, falling easily into old rhythms. His body remembers, even though it’s been months, and he sinks back into motions that feel more natural than serving tea or slipping on his apron ever have.

Zuko sets out into the darkness, no goal in mind other than burning off energy. And if behind a mask on top of the roofline where no one knows he’s there might be the most truly seen Zuko has felt in…a long time, he doesn’t let himself think about that head-on too much. And he very thoroughly ignores the fact that chasing after this particular sensation might mean running away from other important things, things that he wants to hold onto even if he isn't sure how. It’s selfish, he knows. But Zuko still can’t bring himself to stop.

## Chapter 24: Breaking Loose

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Warnings for some sexual content in this one, and depictions of a panic attack

### Text

Sokka kicks a cabbage in frustration, sending it tumbling down the suddenly-empty street as the last two earthbenders who had jumped them disappear literally into the ground, taking their knife-wielding companions with them.

“Why do they keep running away,” Aang complains with something close to a glare, fingers tightening around his glider as Momo chitters in agreement.

“Because then we might know who they were,” Sokka mutters, forcing himself to breathe deep and trying to just—calm down.

“We *know* who they are,” Toph says, crossing her arms, tone daring anyone to disagree with her. “We should just go after them.”

“We need to know for certain,” Sokka says, scrubbing his hands over his face as he repeats himself for the who-knows how many times it’s been now.

“We’re never going to be certain if we don’t chase down the evidence,” Toph says. “And we aren’t having any luck chasing it down this way.”

Sokka winces but can’t fight that point. All his plan to canvas the city has gotten them are suspicions, nervousness, empty leads, and fights, which basically add up to a whole lot of nothing. And even if any of them actually thought Appa was okay out there and just needed to be found, not rescued, Sokka is tightly aware that the time before the eclipse is increasingly finite.

“*Can* we even go after them?” Sokka asks, circling the solid patch of cobblestone the earthbenders closed behind them, the only sign of their passage the slight offset of the pavers.

“I can do whatever I want,” Toph rolls her eyes, but she cracks her knuckles in something like eagerness. “Are we finally going to follow them, then?”

“I mean...We’re all here,” Sokka shrugs, glancing around. “And no one is injured, right?”

“You’re the one hurt, Sokka,” Katara says from where she’s still standing in the wreckage of overturned produce carts. “Will you let me look at it, this time?”

“Why wouldn’t you look at his leg,” Aang frowns. “It’s bleeding.”

“Someone—” as if her tone leaves any room to doubt who. “—was being weird about it, before.”

“I wasn’t being weird about it,” Sokka grumbles, fully aware that he had been weird, as he rolls up the leg of his pants to bare a stinging swathe of road rash to the air. He’d slid under a chunk of flying rock, which let Aang come over top of it to end things, and the move had worked but Spirits was Sokka not wearing the right clothes for it. Sliding on cobblestones is not the same as sliding on snow, *at all*.

“That’s not too bad,” Katara says after eyeing his lower leg, water already beginning to glow blue between her hands.

“It hurts like it is,” Sokka grumbles. Now that he’s paying attention to it, he can feel the raw skin and bruising running up past his knee, stinging with every shift of his weight.

“Stop complaining, Snoozles. It wouldn’t have happened if you were paying attention in the first place.”

“I was paying attention!” Sokka says, nearly dropping his pant leg into Katara’s water orb in his outrage. “Did you not see me in that fight?”

“No.”

“Oh, come on. You know what I—”

“And besides, that was when the fight had already started.”

“That’s when you need to pay attention the most!”

Toph shoots a shard of stone toward him with an annoyed flick. “How about before the fight starts, so it doesn’t get that bad in the first place.”

“I was *totally*…” Sokka trails off with an uncomfortable shrug. Shit. He *had* been distracted, and he is sure Toph knows it from his heartbeat, because she always knows. And Sokka can’t even be mad about it because he asked her to keep an eye on him. Dammit.

“Yeah, that’s what I thought,” Toph says before she dismisses him to begin poking and kicking at the ground.

“You *have* been a bit…out of it, today,” Aang says tentatively, voice quiet and eyes on Katara as she slowly guides water around Sokka’s leg.

“I’m sorry,” Sokka sighs. “I don’t mean to be. I just have a lot on my mind, I guess.”

“We all do,” Aang agrees. A show of understanding, but Sokka can’t help but hear it as a warning, too—Sokka is the only one slipping.

“Is it something we can help you with?” Katara asks, face set in concentration. “Talking out your plans usually helps.”

Sokka actually considers it before slowly shaking his head. “I don’t think so. It’s not really a plans thing. I’m just worried about some stuff with Zuko.” Katara’s eyes shoot up, quick and hard. “Not *about* him, *for* him. He’s just. He’s having a time.”

“You need to focus when we're out like this,” Katara says, avoiding Sokka’s eyes as she guides her water back into her waterskin.

“I know,” Sokka assures her—all of them. “The mission comes first, I haven’t forgotten.” He glances over to Toph. His own reassurance.

“It has to,” Aang says, voice heavy. “For all of us.” He looks momentarily grim, skating near the fact that they’re all well aware of: that they’re slowly but surely approaching a decision point between finding Appa and acting on the eclipse. All the more reason for Sokka to keep his head in the game and make sure that they never have to reach it.

“Are we done with the chit chat?” Toph calls, stomping her foot for emphasis and sending a shiver through the sheet. “Are we ready to chase them now?”

“Yeah,” Sokka says, testing his weight on his healed leg and finding it good as new. “Let’s go.”

&#45;-

Zuko feels like everyone is conspiring against him today. Through malice, or maybe just through incompetence, not that the reason matters when the result is the same. It’s not exactly a new feeling for Zuko, or really even a false one, considering the entirety of the fucking teashop and its clientele. But Zuko hasn’t felt this quite so intensely in a while, to the point where it seems like every person and part of his life is coming together to make it as hard as it can possibly be for Zuko to hold onto the face he needs to present to this particular piece of the world.

Zuko is logy despite Agni’s light when he shows up to his shift, already tight with an irritableness that borders on cranky over the unexpected, chill drizzle that made Zuko just damp enough to be uncomfortable and just noticeably wet enough that he can’t heat himself dry in front of Sung-Min. He is restless and unsettled in the way that usually comes with clinging dreams, even though Zuko barely let himself sleep last night, between slipping onto the roofs again and resolutely ignoring all the things he didn’t want to think about.

It makes his hands itch, as he pulls on his apron, to be grabbing the hilts of his swords instead, an urge that is absolutely useless and does nothing but feed the disgruntled seething of his inner flame, because Sokka isn’t going to be around until the day after tomorrow to train with, and because Zuko is staring down two whole days of working back-to-back opening and closing shifts in order to carve out the time for him. And Zuko doesn’t think he can put off sleeping again tonight to go up onto the roofs, much as he might want to.

The day has not improved since then.

Zuko unboxes the latest tea leaves to find mold in half the order. Sung-Min almost immediately trips over a customer’s child, leading to shattered plates and crying toddlers, both of which grate equally against Zuko’s good ear and set the other one ringing. Minji somehow dumps an entire pot of tea all over all their spare order pads, and the shop’s patrons seem determined to be as difficult as possible, whether through not knowing what to order, or not having the right change, or just not liking what they ended up with. Zuko snaps three charcoal pencils before the lunch rush arrives, when lately he’s been down to only needing three to get through a whole week.

It’s not Zuko’s fault. It’s not like he sets the tone for the entire teashop, or else it would be perpetually pissy and hostile. He isn’t causing whatever mood is infecting everyone else and bleeding through the morning into lunch. But Zuko is marginally self-aware enough of the size of his moods, especially ones like this, to know that his on-the-edge-of-exploding frustration with the whole day isn’t helping.

Zuko is trying not to entirely lose his shit when both Minji and Uncle take their break in what should be the post-lunch lull. It should be completely fine, because Zuko leaves them in this situation all the time. But the cold drizzle seems to be driving people into the shop rather than keeping them home, and Sung-min cut his hand trying to clean up one of the latest broken plates, now they can’t work as fast as usual even without the crowd, and Zuko is feeling ragged and resentful of everyone who walks in the door. And if the tea is coming to a boil faster than usual as a result, it’s still not enough to bleed off his temper or to get them out of the weeds.

Fuck. Everything.

Jin walks through the door right around when Zuko is trying desperately to keep his tray balanced as some woman ‘helpfully’ decides to grab her teapot off the edge before he’s ready. It should be a relief to see her, one moment of sanity in this awful day, except the first thing out of her mouth is, “Did you hear the Avatar was in the Lower Ring yesterday?”

Zuko barely manages to turn a scream of frustrated *everything* into a grunt, scowling at the table as he unloads the last of his tray. He will *not* care about whatever the Avatar is doing in the city. He won’t. He won’t think about it at all. Not about where the Avatar might have been, or where he might be going. Not about whether Sokka was with him. And not about how much better Zuko knows these twisting Lower Ring alleys than the Avatar probably does. Especially not about how easy it would be to lead someone already hunting onto the wrong path.

Zuko isn’t in luck today, though—when is he ever—because one of the shop’s intermittent regulars is in a chatty mood, the woman twisting fully around on her bench to jump into the conversation. “Did you hear there was a fight, too?” She sounds scandalized, in a particularly eager way.

“Yes! Can you believe it?” Jin exclaims, somehow managing to address both Zuko and the woman and it’s not like he can just outright walk away because he needs to clean off this other table. “Who would attack the *Avatar*?”

Zuko…studiously readjusts the teapots on his tray before reaching for another dirty dish.

The woman hums in agreement, then leans back to whisper-shout in a way that is not at all clandestine, so what’s the fucking point. “Rumor I’ve heard is that the Avatar and his band ran afoul of some rules.”

Jin and Zuko share a quick, automatic glance that means ‘careful.’

The teapot-grabbing-trying-to-be-helpful woman jumps in at that. “No one is above the rules,” she says, face wrinkled in distaste. “Why, I heard they ripped up a whole street! Vendors, stalls, produce—all destroyed!” Which…sounds like something the Avatar would do, to be honest.

“But it’s the *Avatar*,” Jin practically glows. “Can you imagine, Lee?”

“I wouldn’t want any fights in here, though,” the first woman frowns, glancing around the teashop as if someone is about to start flipping tables at any moment. As if the person most likely to do that isn’t Zuko.

“But wouldn’t it be amazing to meet him?” Jin sighs. “What do you think he’s like, Lee?”

“Useless,” Zuko bites out, stalking away in the sudden surprised silence to deal with another table and ignoring other words like ‘powerful’ and ‘melancholy’ and ‘young’ and ‘terrifying’ swirling in his head. But no matter what table he is at, Zuko can still hear Jin and the women speaking, phrases and half-sentences carrying over the chatter of the busy shop.

And they’re *still* talking about it when Zuko comes back with Jin’s usual order, and of course she turns to fold him back into the conversation as if he never left. “What would you do if you met the Avatar, Lee?”

Zuko nearly drops her muffin, inner fire spiking in panic as his mind scrambles to catch up. “…What?”

Zuko desperately hopes he heard her wrong, that he’s just having a bad day and projecting, because Agni’s *balls*, that’s the kind of shit Zuko purposefully never lets himself think about. If he thinks about that, then he has to think about all the things he’s supposed to want, and all the things he actually does want, and the only place that ends is with Zuko taking an actual look at whatever the fuck he’s doing with his life, and when has that ever been worth the pain and effort?

“What if he walked into the shop right now?” Jin continues blithely. “Can you *imagine*?”

All too well, Zuko realizes, as a tight band locks around his chest and his inner flame goes thready and jagged. Zuko’s eyes dart toward the door like the Avatar might walk in at any moment, straight out of his nightmares. Would Sokka bring him? No, Sokka wouldn’t. He wouldn’t. Not that it would matter, with the Avatar’s eyes glowing for the vengeance that Zuko fled months ago, that he’s been running from ever since, that he never deserved to escape in the first place.

Later, Zuko will realize that Sung-min tried to do too much with his injured hand.

There’s a choked shout—Sung-min, stumbling—and the sound of waves breaking against steel—or multiple teapots, sloshing over—and then ships rending on claws and ice—dishes, shattering—and Zuko’s throat feels harsh with acrid smoke and too-cold air and his lungs can’t inflate against the weight of the water and he’s going to die here, and Uncle is too, and there’s nothing Zuko can do to stop it, no matter how far he reaches or how tight he holds, nothing he does will be enough, it’s already too, he’s failing—

”*Lee*.”

Hands on his forearms and Zuko reacts, pure instinct and terror and rage, which are all the same thing for him. He twists the blades of his hands inward in the space of half a too-fast-heartbeat, snapping them out to break the hold on his arms and flowing immediately into a bind, fingers digging into his opponent’s arms, fire rising under his skin. Zuko will *not* let himself be pulled away, or pulled under, not into the—

Jin’s sharp gasp cuts through the ringing of exploding blasting jelly in his ear and Zuko’s fingers go suddenly numb. With cold or horror, he isn’t entirely sure. Either way, he needs to look down to make sure that he’s actually let her go, needs to stare too long to realize that the redness on her skin is from the pressure of his grip and not fire. Nausea rises hard and thick in his throat.

“Sorry,” Zuko gasps, barely a word, too thin and high and weak. “Sorry. I’m sorry. I didn’t —” His eyes bounce around the room, entire body teetering on the need for flight. His head spins and he lurches, feeling entirely disconnected from reality when he realizes that somehow *no one is looking*. They’re all too distracted by the mess Sung-min is standing in the middle of, as if Zuko weren’t a half-breath away from drowning and pulling them all down with him.

“Are you okay?” Jin asks, yanking his gaze back to front. Her big eyes are filled with worry, hands hovering like she wants to reach for him again. She doesn’t, which Zuko is painfully grateful for. The idea of making his skin temperature tolerable to touch, right now, to seem like a normal person—he can’t.

“I’m sorry,” Zuko whispers, taking a half-step back. “I didn’t mean—I—Sorry. Sorry. Sorry.” He’s breathing too fast and he knows it, but Zuko can’t make it stop. Now that he’s coming back from the edge of panicked fear, all that’s left is a buzzing terror that makes his hands tremble, makes it hard to hear, hard to think beyond the fact that *fuck*, Zuko could have just hurt a lot of people. Could have hurt *Jin*. And not just hurt her, as if that wouldn’t be bad enough, but outed himself in front of an entire shop in the process, with Uncle not here to know or to protect him from it.

Oh Agni, Zuko fucked up. So bad, just like he always fucks up, with absolutely *everything*, he can’t do *anything* right, not even—

“Lee, can you help me with this?” Sung-min’s voice is overly loud and too close and Zuko flinches as a tray of broken pottery is shoved into his hands. He stares at it, numb, unsure, until Jin gives him a little push in the back and Sung-min jerks his head in a ‘come-along’ command and somehow Zuko is moving on heavy legs, Jin behind and Sung-min leading, shielding him from the customers.

Zuko makes it into the kitchen without further incident, with is another distant shock. The tray is pulled from his hands and a chair is set down behind him and a cup of something *way* more bracing than tea is shoved into his hands.

“What—” Zuko sputters, coughing as fire crawls down his throat in the opposite direction it usually travels, the sharp sensation snapping the world back into focus.

“Are you back with us, now?” Sung-min asks, and Zuko looks up to find the other man leaning back against the counter in front of him, arms crossed, face grave.

“I—what?”

Sung-min just nods, like Zuko gave an actual answer. “Does this happen often?”

Zuke’s shoulders tighten with sudden wariness. He glances around, wishing for Uncle or fuck, even Sokka, not that he wants Sokka to see him this way. He isn’t exactly panicking again, but he itches with the need to set his back, his left side, against something solid, because if he doesn’t then the blow could come from any direction and not just right in front of him. But no—there’s no one else suddenly in the kitchen. Just Sung-min and Jin, and they wouldn’t—won’t—Zuko could—

“Do you need help?” It takes Zuko too long to realize that Jin isn’t addressing him. “It’s not that long until the lunch breaks end. I’ve done food service before, I can help hold down the front.”

“That would be good.” Sung-min glances back to the raucous sound of the teashop floor. “And when Lee is feeling up to it, he can make the tea.”

“I can—”

“Sit,” Sung-min finishes, giving Zuko a glance that suddenly reminds Zuko that this is a man who has children. Zuko sits.

“But—”

“Take a minute,” Sung-min says, face gentling again when Zuko doesn’t fight the order. “It’s fine.”

“But…”

“Lee.” He waits for Zuko to drag his eyes up to Sung-min’s face, something the other man usually tries to avoid. “You aren’t the only one who came to Ba Sing Se as a refugee. It’s fine. Take your time.”

“I…”

Jin ignores his barely audible protest as thoroughly as Sung-min, which…Zuko isn’t used to. Normally it’s much more *pointed*, when someone makes a show of acting like they don’t care that he’s there. But Jin just briskly tugs the order pad out of his apron pocket, hair already thrown up into a messy bun, charcoal pencil behind her ear and already lightly smudged over her cheekbone.

“Think of it as a favor, how about,” she says, nudging his foot with her own. “You sit here and drink your tea—” Which is basically all whisky, and they all know it. “—and eat something, and when you stop looking like you’re about to keel over in a stiff wind, then you owe me a dance when we go out tomorrow night.”

“…Okay,” Zuko finally mutters, aware that neither of them needs his agreement but feeling vaguely like he should offer it anyway.

Agni, he is…disgustingly grateful, watching her slip onto the floor in his place. The more he sits the more he’s aware of and flustered and overwhelmed by the fact that he just let Zuko bleed into Lee. Crown Prince Zuko, at that. He can’t help bracing himself, waiting for the other shoe to drop, except…no one seems to care, which he doesn’t know what to do with, and nothing is on fire, which is genuinely shocking considering how erratic his inner flame feels.

So Zuko just stays in his chair, and watches Jin zip out onto the floor, and drinks his whisky until the burn of it stokes and coaxes his inner flame back to some semblance of its normal state. Except instead of putting himself back together, Zuko turns himself into endless tangles, wondering what is so wrong with him that he can’t just keep these kinds of things locked down tight where they’re supposed to be.

&#45;-

Sokka is leaning against a little piece of wall by the alley that he’s starting to think of as his, eyes closed and face tipped back toward the sun. He can feel his heart beating just on the edge of fast, like it always does when he’s standing here. His skin prickles, his blood feeling like it's fizzling with anticipation for working up a sweat in the chill air with Zuko, and then getting sweaty in other ways. Sokka is invited over for dinner again tonight—a concept that will never not be weird—which means Iroh is closing the Blooming Petal. Which means that they know exactly where Iroh is going to be until evening and can take advantage.

The sound of the teashop door slamming has Sokka already smiling before he even opens his eyes. He blinks against the light to see Zuko stalking away from the shop, looking tense and wound up and with a bit of a familiar stomp to his step. Sokka’s stomach flips in recognition, the anticipation in his gut beginning to simmer in a way that is going to make training hard to focus on.

Sokka watches Zuko’s stride hitch, pause, and then Zuko turns unerringly toward him. Sokka smiles wider as a bit of looseness enters Zuko’s posture and a spark of warmth softens the hard gold of his eyes. Spirits, but Sokka likes being able to do that to him. For him.

“Ready to train?” Sokka calls, staying leaned against the wall mostly so he can enjoy the sight of Zuko moving toward him. With that lingering moodiness and barely-restrained tension, Sokka feels like he could almost be pinned in place as Zuko prowls toward him, like he might be thrown back in time. It’s…a feeling to save for later.

Sokka clears his throat, trying to drag his mind back to training. That needs to come first if it's going to happen at all, with the way the days are getting shorter. And they need something to be able to tell Iroh they got up to with the afternoon when he inevitably asks, because Sokka might be able to skip around the details but Zuko definitely can’t.

“You just need to grab the swords," Sokka says as Zuko draws closer. "I’ve got lots of snacks today.” As if Zuko doesn’t know that already, since Sokka still can’t manage to come to dinner without bearing gifts. It’s reflexive at this point, and more revealing of his lingering nervousness than he would care to admit, and also maybe more territorial than Sokka is necessarily proud of.

Zuko hums, eyes dragging down Sokka’s body in a way that does *not* make it easier for Sokka to put a pin in that whole feeling-caught thought for later. “There’s no time.”

“What?” Sokka blinks. Can Zuko read his mind?

“We won't have time to train," Zuko says, flicking a quick look upward. So not reading Sokka's mind, then. "There’s a storm coming."

Sokka follows his gaze up to the clear blue sky, broken only with gentle fluffy clouds. “… What?”

“From…” Zuko cocks his head like he’s listening for something that Sokka can’t hear. “There.” He tugs Sokka close, turning him around and pointing over his shoulder. “See?”

“How do you know that?” Sokka wonders as he follows the line of Zuko’s arm. There’s barely a smudge on the horizon, and Sokka knows his eyes are better than Zuko’s.

Sokka feels Zuko’s shrug against his back. “There’s lightning.”

“So?”

“So, I can feel it.”

“…Oh.” Azula was quite the fan of lightning, Sokka remembers. He supposes he should have realized that was a firebender thing, not just a terrifying-Princess thing. It’s vaguely unsettling that something Sokka so strongly associates with near-death experiences could be so casual for Zuko. “What does it feel like?”

Sokka glances over his shoulder when Zuko doesn’t reply, then does a double-take at Zuko’s half-lidded eyes and parted lips and the slow heat suddenly rolling off him.

“…Wow. That good, huh?” Zuko doesn’t look like *that* very often out in public, and Sokka turns to fully appreciate it.

“I—yeah? Kind of? I...don’t know. If it's supposed to feel like...that” Zuko says, eyes pinned to the base of Sokka’s throat as if that will hide the fact that his pupils are still blown wide.

“Don’t you live with a master firbender?” Sokka asks, admiring the flush of red working its way over Zuko’s cheek.

“Yeah, and I’m not going to ask *Uncle* if it's normal every time there’s a lightning storm to get—” Zuko stops with a glare, finally realizing that Sokka is teasing.

“No, I suppose not,” Sokka grins, that simmering anticipation he’d been feeling beginning to spark as the words ‘every time’ and ‘lightning storm’ register with the fact that Zuko said one is coming right now. “So…you can feel it, then? Now?”

“Yeah.”

Sokka gives Zuko a thorough once-over somewhere between curious and lascivious. “And it feels…?”

“Agni’s dick, Sokka,” Zuko huffs, not-quite-laughing as his cheek goes redder. “It’s not…it’s still far away. So it’s just kind of…jittery for now. Like extra energy.”

“And as it gets closer?” Sokka feverishly tries to remember if Toph ever said anything about the prevalence of cold-weather storms in the Earth Kingdom. Maybe they’re entering lightning season?

Zuko hesitates, peeking at Sokka from beneath his lashes in that way he has, the one that’s part shy, part wicked, that hits Sokka with a punch of desire of every time he’s on the receiving end of it. “I…can show you. If you want.”

“Yes,” Sokka says before Zuko even finishes speaking. “I want.”

Zuko bites his lips against something that might be a smile—and just kill Sokka dead right now, he’s never going to make it to dinner—glancing up again in the direction of the storm. Then he grabs Sokka’s hand and tugs him along, a little less careful and a little more urgent than usual—not that Sokka’s complaining—something like excitement in the line of his shoulders.

“How good are you at climbing?” Zuko asks, weaving through the streets, eyes pinned to the sky.

“What?” Sokka is saying that a lot today, apparently.

“It’s better to be up high. For lightning.”

Sokka looks up reflexively, realizing that they’re between two tall, crowded-together apartment buildings. A rickety-looking fire escape is wandering up the edge of one, more vertical than horizontal and not making it all the way to the top. Above it are windows, and what could be termed balconies if Sokka is feeling generous, and laundry lines…and the stone can’t be *that* smooth…

“You up for it?”

Sokka’s attention snaps back to Zuko at his unexpected tone. It’s challenging, teasing, and Zuko’s eyes are already molten and intent, his body vibrating with an energy that’s almost… playful?

“Yeah,” Sokka says, clearing his throat. “Yeah.” It comes out a little more solid, the second time. He’s up for anything, really, that makes Zuko look like that.

Zuko gestures for Sokka to lead the way up, immediately moving behind him. And maybe it’s because Sokka's already been thinking about that old hunter-prey dynamic, or because he’s been indulging the kinds of thoughts more suited for fantasies of being behind cell bars, but Sokka can’t help feeling that it’s reminiscent of his escape from Zuko’s ship. This time, though, there’s a lot less breathlessness over Zuko’s proximity and a lot more choked-off gasping over Zuko’s wandering hands. The way Zuko deliberately crowds up against Sokka’s body, his breath against Sokka’s neck, the husky murmur of his voice describing the route up, it’s all very…*supportive*, as they get ready to climb.

It’s also unexpected, a side of Zuko that Sokka doesn’t see often, and he can’t help but wrack his brain to remember if the few times he’s seen it before were close to bad weather. Regardless, Sokka is wholly on board with Zuko’s unspoken demands, breathlessly aware of Zuko’s extra height and the muscle that Zuko has finally started to put back on his frame. Sokka can almost feel the hard edge of armor against his skin when Zuko presses in close, his knees going unhelpfully weak when Zuko gives Sokka an easy boost off the last landing toward the nearest handhold. Sokka doesn’t necessarily need the help, but Spirits, being *manhandled* this way, so effortlessly—Sokka needs to focus or else he isn’t going to make it up this wall.

The climb is a relatively straightforward one, though challenging enough to require focus. Though not so much that Sokka doesn’t notice how remarkably at ease Zuko is with the whole thing. Sokka can’t help but wonder how Zuko even knew this path to the rooftops was here in the first place.

Zuko’s grin is fierce when he pulls himself onto the roof after Sokka, all teeth and snapping eyes as he looks into the suddenly gusting wind. When Sokka drags his attention away to follow Zuko’s stare he can finally see that yes, that is a bank of clouds rolling in now, coming fast and deep, casting darkness over the ground beneath it and whipping the wind out ahead of its arrival.

“You good?” Sokka asks quietly, almost afraid to move in case he disrupts whatever mood it is that Zuko is in.

“Yeah,” Zuko breathes, eyes fixed on the storm, looking half-anticipatory and half-entranced. Sokka feels almost like he’s witnessing something private, and just as the feeling of seeing something not meant for prying eyes starts to get overwhelming, Zuko cuts him a hot-eyed look and beckons. Sokka scrambles over the clay roof tiles before his brain has a chance to catch up with his limbs, everything in him wanting to get as close to this side of Zuko as possible before it disappears along with the storm.

Sokka doesn’t stay close for long, though. Zuko sets him up by a chimney with a distracted, “Best not to be too close. The lightning rod will take anything that doesn’t go for me,” which is not the most reassuring statement he’s ever made. Sokka tries not to think too much about it as Zuko settles a body length away, kneeling like he’s about to meditate, face tipped toward the storm in welcome the way Zuko always seems to open himself to the sun.

“It’s a fast one,” Sokka observes, tucking himself against the warmth of the chimney as the wind kicks up again, thick and wet and cold.

“Yes. It’s…excited.”

“It’s not the only thing,” Sokka mutters to himself, eyeing Zuko. Sokka thought he was the only one who could put a flush like that high on Zuko’s cheek**.** Zuko just grins in response, looking wild and *happy* and like he’s inviting Sokka to share, and Sokka can’t help but smile back, even as the wind whips tears from his eyes and a distant rumble of thunder sounds and he suddenly realizes he has absolutely no idea what to expect.

The storm comes in fast, rolling over the city and through Zuko. That’s the only way Sokka can find to describe it. At first Sokka thinks he’s imagining the light around Zuko, the extra bit of glow. Then he realizes that there are motes dancing in the air, not embers like he thinks at first, but little bits of electricity jumping toward Zuko’s skin and away again.

Sokka keeps waiting for Zuko to flinch, or startle, but it never comes. Zuko just closes his eyes and tips his head back, his whole posture relaxed in a way that Sokka usually has to actively work to make happen. Sokka is the one to jolt in surprise when foxfire begins to limn Zuko’s frame, ghostly over his skin and clothes, not burning, just…there. It stretches out like it’s reaching for that halo of sparks, and the sparks dance like they’re reaching back, and for a moment Sokka thinks that’s all there will be: this teasing, bright little interplay between the storm and Zuko’s fire—is this his inner flame? Is that why it looks so different than the fires Zuko usually manifests?—with Zuko close-eyed and quietly enjoying it.

Then the lightning comes.

The brightness arrives a heartbeat before the deep rumble of thunder, a jagged flash of white that streaks down as Zuko’s fire lances up. Sokka frantically blinks the burned echo of too-bright too-close from his vision, just managing through the bright spots to see Zuko’s body arch at the strike, fire and electricity twining. Zuko holds a long, tight breath, body bent back, releasing it on a *laugh*. Sokka can see how he breathes deep, chest opening and arms stretching out as little bolts of lightning arc across his skin, fire chasing behind and wrapping around him in strips and strands like nothing Sokka has ever seen before but that his body viscerally recognizes from the times Zuko seems determined to wrap him in heat.

Zuko seems unhurt, so Sokka settles back against the chimney, ignoring the cold rain and blinking the last ghost of lightning from his vision. Zuko’s fire dances with the storm and the storm seems to nearly dance back, light and bright and almost teasing, somehow, which isn’t something Sokka ever thought he would use to describe chains of lightning crashing down until the air is thick with the smell of ozone.

Sokka dashes rainwater from his eyes as Zuko’s body shudders, Sokka's own body tensing as his firebender gasps with nothing like pain. Sokka has the sense that Zuko is alone with his fire and the storm right now, the constant restraint Zuko holds himself under gone in a shower of playful sparks. And Sokka can’t tear his eyes away as he realizes that, maybe for the first time, he is seeing Zuko wholly uninhibited and unrestrained.

It’s beautiful, enough to steal Sokka’s breath and make him never want to forget the sight of it. Enough to make his heart clench, aching at the knowledge that it will end as the storm does. Will he ever see Zuko like this again, in his element in the truest sense of the phrase? Will Zuko ever give him permission to see it?

Sokka hungrily tries to burn every second and breath and twitch and spark of fire into his memory, every moment of seeing Zuko so free, even as a corner of him how long Zuko can possibly go before he burns down the city or himself, trying to hold all of this back that’s inside him.

&#45;-

Afterward, Zuko is still…Sokka doesn’t even know how to describe it. Frisky? Playful? Unchained? He’s laying on his back, breathing heavily, the echo of a smile on his face as the storm finally clears the city. He’s completely soaked through, like Sokka, and totally uncaring, unlike Sokka. Wisps are rising up off Zuko that might be steam or might be fabric finally giving way to the dual onslaught of fire and lightning. Sokka shifts against the heat of the chimney, trying to ignore the creeping chill now that he doesn’t have Zuko to completely distract him.

Before Sokka can even begin to try to vocalize a thought about what happens now, Zuko flips over onto his stomach, golden eyes intent beneath strands of wet hair. Sokka startles as he realizes that Zuko’s hair is getting long. Then he forgets about hair entirely as he registers that the expression on Zuko’s face is—oh boy. Oooh boy. Whatever high Zuko was riding in the storm is clearly still working through him, and Sokka is more than a little bit intimidated by it, and a whole lot turned on.

Sokka freezes, pinned by Zuko’s full focus as Zuko prowls forward on hands and knees, which—*Spirits.* Sokka doesn’t know the rules to this particular game, but he’s eager to play it. For all that he knows Zuko, for all that he’s pretty sure Zuko has let Sokka see more of him than maybe anyone else, Sokka hasn’t known this wild, playful, confident part of him before. And Sokka wants to, fiercely.

When Zuko kisses him it's hard and deep and fucking *electricity* jumps from his tongue to Sokka’s, which should fucking hurt but instead is ticklish and feels like bubbles sliding down his throat. Sokka gasps in surprise and Zuko swallows the noise, laughing, an actual laugh not just the breath of one. The sound vibrates against Sokka’s lips and through his whole body as Zuko pulls him in close and oh, *oh* fuck yes, Sokka loves storms.

But—they’re on a roof. And the city will be coming back alive now that the storm has passed. And Zuko might be throwing off heat like an oven, but that doesn’t entirely distract from the fact that Toph’s long-promised cold weather is finally here, and they’re both *wet.*

“How fast can you climb down?” Sokka gasps out, proud of his coherency as Zuko licks along his jaw and begins kissing down his neck.

Sokka shivers, when Zuko’s next exhalation comes with sparks and a knowing smirk.

By some miracle, they make it back to the apartment without Zuko talking Sokka into some side alley, which seemed like a better and better idea every time Zuko mentioned it. And if Zuko is a bit more fumbling and sloppy this afternoon, a bit more awkward and uncoordinated, it’s all the more amazing for it. Because Zuko intent on executing a plan is overwhelming in the best kind of way, but Zuko lost in a moment and acting on instinct and just *reacting?* That's unforgettable. That's Zuko still in his element, without expectation or responsibility, shining bright and blazing hot and Sokka feels drunk by association, contact-high and happy to burn in the fire of him.

Sokka can barely keep up, breathless, panting and something dangerously close to a whine catching in the back of his throat at the knowing smirk on Zuko’s lips as Zuko sets his hands on Sokka’s chest and lets them heat and begins to ride. Spirits, Zuko is unconsciously demanding and confident and utterly beautiful seeking his pleasure. “You know,” Sokka says after, resting his chin on Zuko’s chest and running a light finger around the hollow of his throat. “We might not be able to train, but we can still work on the whole chi bending stuff.”

Zuko cracks open an eye, and Sokka’s heart pounds hard and sudden as the fading afternoon light flashes through the gold of it like a single shard of lightning. “Bad idea, today.”

“…Right,” Sokka says faintly, more than a little dizzy as he tries to imagine what the intense-enough-to-be-overwhelming on a normal day feeling of Zuko moving his chi would be like edged with that kind of energy.
