“We can,” Sokka agrees quietly. “But it will be harder, and bloodier, and take longer.” And after the North…Sokka doesn’t want to be responsible for another body cleanup like that, not if he has the chance to end things quick and clean and now.

“Sokka is right,” Aang says, stirring for the first time, his face still pressed against Appa’s nose. “We can’t let the Dai Li get away with it.” His voice is dark, hand fisted in Appa’s dirty coat, the anger still there. Sokka knows that something like that doesn’t die easily.

Toph and Katara share a long silence, then Katara sighs. “Fine. How are we doing this, then? It’s not like they’re going to welcome us back and give us our house again.”

“We’re going to do it how we should have done it in the first place,” Toph says, cracking her knuckles. “Let’s go break some skulls.”

## Chapter 30: Crucible

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

No particular warnings for this one!

### Text

Zuko is nominally sorting the latest stock order, replenishing tea canisters and mixing the blends that Uncle is starting to become famous for. Mostly, though, Zuko is anxiously tracking Agni’s ascent across the sky, degree by degree, unable to stop wondering whether Sokka will show up this morning. He’s supposed to, but that was before the messenger, and the missed afternoon, and everything else.

Zuko tries, reflexively and uselessly, to tug his inner fire down from its rapid, scattered flickering. Its unsteadiness is mixing with nerves to leave him vaguely ill and shaky. Nothing Zuko does to relax makes an impact, though. He’s been filled with pent-up energy, his heart beating a persistent, frantic ‘*what now’* until Zuko feels like he’s going to burst apart from it.

It’s almost like he never made it out of Lake Laogai, like his body still thinks it’s struggling for open air even as Zuko doesn’t think if he will ever forget the moment of dragging himself from the water to collapse at Uncle’s feet. Zuko could have hated Uncle, then, sprawled on the ground in front of him. But Zuko’s lungs had been aching and his throat raw and his whole body shaking from cold and exertion. Hatred had required more than he had, for once in his life, so Zuko hadn’t fought away the hand reaching down for him. He’d just let it happen, let himself be bundled away, every part of his body heavy as Uncle guided him up and forward. Stumbling back toward the Inner Rings—Zuko really isn’t sure how they made it, he didn’t even have *boots—*the whole way back uncomfortably hazy and grey with exhaustion as he desperately tried to believe that Uncle’s quiet words of praise and his assurances that Zuko had done the right thing actually made anything better.

The next morning dawned as if nothing had changed at the Jasmine Dragon, in his life, and Zuko had stared at his apron for so long he was almost late for his shift, had fumbles to tie it while clawing for calm and wondering if he would ever feel anchored and sure of the ground beneath his feet again.

Zuko is still focused on calm a day later, the kind of way you focus on something unattainable that you know you’re supposed to want. The kind of way you focus on a place at your sister’s right hand and your father’s left, on seeing contentment and approval in your uncle’s eyes. Zuko is so focused on staying calm and feeling exactly, minutely, precisely nothing beyond where the sun is in the sky, his entire being braced for another messenger, that the kitchen door bursting open takes him completely by surprise.

“Zuko!”

Zuko fumbles the tin of leaves, fingers suddenly unresponsive, fresh basil mint scattering across the countertop as his attempts at catching the container only cause more mess because he can’t look at anything but Sokka.

“We did it!”

Sokka sounds…maybe happier than Zuko's ever heard him. And looks like he’s been hit in the face with how dark the circles under his eyes are. He’s rimmed by morning sunlight as he stands in the doorway, streaked with dirt and grinning ear to ear and Zuko doesn’t know if he’s ever seen anything better.

“We did it,” Sokka says again, striding forward and grabbing Zuko up into a bone-crushing, all-too-brief hug that lifts Zuko clear off his feet. Zuko yelps, throwing his arms out for balance, then going total still when Sokka tucks his face forward against Zuko's chest, inhaling deep and long and slow before suddenly dropping Zuko back onto his feet just as abruptly as he picked him up in the first place.

Zuko stumbles, Sokka already on the move again around the kitchen by the time he finds his balance. He watches, bemused and rubbing absently at the center of his chest as Sokka darts around with the kind of jittery energy that comes with too little sleep and too much excitement, like he’s transcended the point where tiredness can reach him.

Zuko's reached that point before. He usually starts tripping over things. “Sokka," Zuko says, abandoning the tea leaves and giving the rather manic Water Tribesman his full attention, ready to lunge forward to catch him if needed. “What did you do?”

Sokka whirls to face Zuko full-on, expression caught between disbelief and joy. He lets out a little laugh, like maybe he can’t quite believe what he’s about to say, hands clutching at his disheveled wolf tail. “We found Appa!”

For a moment Zuko’s entire world goes blank, mind tripping as it tries to take in Sokka’s words and the dirt ground into his tunic and come up with anything other than ‘Sokka was there too.’ It can’t be for more than a handful of heartbeats, but by the time Zuko regains his ability to process the world around him, Sokka is lapping the room again, words tumbling out of him so fast they run together and chase on top of each other, his hands flying through the air as the story bursts out in fits and starts and circles backward because he forgot and then leaps forward because this is only relevant if Zuko knows that eventually—

It’s taking all Zuko’s attention to try to keep up. Which could be a comment on Sokka’s state of sleep deprivation but is probably more a reflection of Zuko’s. Sokka found an old friend, and then Appa—which Zuko just needs to think about later, because he can’t sort out his feelings about his own actions while simultaneously crashing into the reality of them— except, maybe finding the friend and finding Appa are the same thing? And also, the Dai Li were there, who aren’t friends even if at one point maybe they were? And multiple fights, or one really long one, and maybe that bruising isn’t just sleeplessness. Zuko should check, if he can get Sokka to stand still, which doesn't look like something that will happen anytime soon because Sokka's back to acting out something that could be flying or combat, or both, and Zuko isn’t sure if he’s hearing descriptions of even more fights or of the same one, just with new details.

And when, exactly, did they break into the Earth King’s palace? Did Sokka…lead a coup? Did Zuko somehow *cause* a coup?

“Sokka,” Zuko finally cuts in, snagging Sokka's tunic and spinning him to a halt when his next lap takes him within grabbing distance again. “When was the last time you slept?”

Sokka waves the question away, bouncing on his toes and fidgeting but obligingly staying within Zuko’s reach. “I napped a few hours ago.”

Sure he did. And Zuko didn’t have a nightmare last night. “When, exactly.”

“I don’t know, it’s so dark in the palace. After lunch, I guess?”

“Sokka,” Zuko says slowly, with another tug on his tunic to hold Sokka’s attention. “It’s past breakfast.”

“…Oh. Huh.” Sokka twists to frown out the window like somehow he’s been personally betrayed by the passage of time before shrugging it off and giving Zuko a bright grin. “Well. Want to eat?”

“I…Okay.”

There are a million things they should probably do instead, starting with ‘talk about that Appa thing’ and ending with ‘sleep for at least four consecutive hours.’ But Zuko shoves all that aside and snags Sokka’s hand, ignoring the rest of the tea that needs stocking as he pulls Sokka into the sunshine. Uncle will be fine on his own for the rest of the morning. Probably. Getting Sokka to one of the less painfully pretentious spots for food around here is about all Zuko’s tired mind can care about right now, so best not to fight it by trying to worry about anything else.

Sokka has enough energy for the both of them, at least, overflowing with chatter and enthusiasm like there’s so much excitement inside him that Sokka can’t help but let it burst out. It’s nice, to be near that much happiness. And Zuko should say something about Appa. It might make Sokka even happier. Maybe. If Zuko can find the right words.

Though listening to another disjointed, circular story, Zuko thinks he needs to convince Sokka to at least take another nap, first. Zuko’s news can wait for when Sokka is awake enough to hear it. And maybe Zuko will have it figured out in his own head, by then, even if he hasn't been able to untangle a single bit of it before now.

&#45;-

That night Zuko dreams of familiar waters, lit by gouts of blasting jelly and claws of blue. The colors warp and waver as Zuko looks at them from beneath the surface, until he can’t tell where the sky is anymore, where the Ocean is, where he needs to go.

Zuko can feel panic rising in his throat, and that’s familiar, too, like the way the water presses at his lips, trying to get in, like the way his armor weighs on him, trying to pull him down. Sokka is there, though, at his side, looking unconcerned at their distance from the surface, at the fact that they don’t even know where the surface is. Zuko reaches for his hand, clinging, holding tight, a spot of warmth in the sucking cold and for a moment Sokka squeezes back with the kind of calm reassurance that somehow quiets Zuko’s frantic heart.

Then Sokka’s hand is ripped away. Not just slipping out of reach like usual, but sucked away from Zuko by some current that only seems to hold Sokka, that Zuko can’t throw himself into no matter how hard he tries, until the panic finally breaks free and the water comes rushing into to replace it.

Zuko wakes with a strangled scream, tense against the burning surge of water flooding his lungs that never comes. His body shudders, chest heaving as he finally realizes that he can take in air. He stares at the ceiling, taking far too many beats of his far too rapid heart to ground himself in the fact that he’s on land, on earth, far from the water. His throat feels raw, like he's been screaming. Maybe he has been. Uncle learned years ago to give Zuko the illusion of privacy when it comes to dreams.

Zuko’s knees are shaky when he finally brings himself to move, body creaky and sore from too little rest as he hauls himself up to meditate over a flame. He knows that he isn’t going to sleep tonight, not after that. And he can’t go out anymore, and he can’t train in the Upper Ring without being heard or seen and remarked on this late at night, and he has nothing to read, and no thoughts he cares to think. So meditation will have to be enough to make him functional again by morning, because it’s all that Zuko has left to rely on anymore when Sokka isn’t here.

&#45;-

Sokka is bubbling over with energy again when he shows up to train the next afternoon. He’s full of smiles, which Zuko loves to see, and chatter, which Zuko enjoys even when Sokka’s talkativeness means they can’t push that hard because Sokka is barely taking pauses for air. Zuko paces his own breathing to the rhythm of Sokka’s words, something about plans and finally having resources and it being so exciting to get traction…Sokka isn’t really saying enough for Zuko to fully follow, and Zuko doesn’t really feel like pressing. The mere idea of trying to pin down Sokka’s wild energy into some semblance of order is enough to make Zuko feel lethargic, let alone actually attempting to do it.

Besides, Sokka is in fine form today. He’s imitating people Zuko has never met, trying to use his own body to describe what a bear is, rolling his eyes at the idea of Aang receiving instructions in a dream as if Sokka hadn’t once visited a Spirit library run by a snake owl in the middle of a desert—which Zuko is still only half convinced that a real event and not a cactus juice induced hallucination. Either way, Sokka gets into enough Spiritual shit that Zuko finds it distinctly amusing that he refuses to take the Avatar’s Spiritual connection seriously. Zuko likes getting to see Sokka like this too much to interrupt to point that out, though, like's to see him sarcastic and fond and without that edge of cynicism that Ba Sing Se had started to wear into him.

Zuko tries to soak in some of Sokka’s joy, tries to let his lightness lift up Zuko too. It’s easier to do when Sokka is here and infectious in his happiness than it is to hold on to the feeling when he’s gone. And it’s not until Sokka leaves to get ready for some political soiree thing that Zuko realizes he forgot to mention Appa again, that he let himself get completely carried away by the tide of Sokka's enthusiasm. He thinks of chasing after Sokka—he can still feel Sokka with his fire sense, he knows where to go. But the thought of trying to shove himself past the time Sokka has carved out for them, even into just the fringe of that other part of Sokka’s life…Zuko slumps back against the courtyard wall, already exhausted by the idea of it.

&#45;-

Zuko doesn’t dream that night because he doesn’t sleep. He lays in the darkness, staring up at the silver-white moonlight stretching across his ceiling. He refuses to look at the window and the full moon outside, refuses to acknowledge to himself the way he’s huddled in the thin pocket of shadow between the edge of his bed and the wall, refuses to think about how he still feels overexposed. His body prickles with a low current of danger that has no place here but that he still can’t ignore.

Zuko has a lot of time to think, as he lays there, which isn’t something he generally likes to do, but his attention is too shot for meditation. He tries to imagine telling Sokka about Appa. What would Zuko even say, at this point? How would he even start? Sokka is so happy to have Appa back that he’s still mentioning it, and Zuko doesn’t know how to insert himself into the narrative. He still doesn’t fully understand it, for one thing, Sokka has yet to get a clear story out, but the more pressing issue is that Zuko doesn't know how to make his role visible without explaining a lot of things that he doesn’t have explanations for. Things that Sokka will immediately want to know. Things like ‘why.’

Zuko is afraid of seeing the way Sokka’s face might change when Zuko doesn't have answers for him. Or when the only answers that come out are the ones that Zuko himself flinches away from. The ones that reveal that he isn’t the person Sokka thinks he is or wants him to be. The idea makes his chest feel tight, his breaths too shallow, like maybe he’s frozen, or drowning, or bleeding out, after all.

&#45;-

Sokka is admiring the casual grace with which Zuko balances bowl and chopsticks and jars as he mixes more chili oil into his noodles. They managed to snatch a quick, early dinner just for themselves and Sokka is stupidly grateful that he can still carve out these moments that let him catalog the small, everyday little things that Zuko does. Even after just a few days of dealing with the Earth King, it's becoming clear that this kind of time is getting harder and harder for Sokka to defend. For the first time in years Sokka doesn’t have full control over his own schedule. Suddenly he’s running between committee meetings and strategy sessions and counsels and lunches, and Sokka is feeling the strain on his time between balancing all he already had to juggle with trying to muster resources and organize an invasion and teach the Earth King to be a functional human being.

Some resentful part of Sokka protests that finding Appa and having the Earth King’s support was supposed to mean that he would finally have space to *breathe.* That he would be able to stop feeling like the world is going to crash down on top of them if they pause. Instead, things are running faster than ever and the quiet moments with Zuko have started to feel crowded, loud, with everything demanding Sokka’s attention.

Sokka is determined to be as focused on Zuko as he can possibly be in the moments they do have together, though. He doesn’t want the distraction of pai sho games and cooking and conversation with Iroh. Instead, they’re in Zuko’s room with takeout Sokka brought on bowls Zuko stole from the teashop. It’s oddly nostalgic, reminiscent of being back in the Lower Ring, or maybe even Zuko's ship, and it’s the first moment of real quiet that Sokka’s had with Zuko since they revealed Long Feng’s plots to King Kuei. Sokka is basking in it even as he’s slowly noticing—registering?—that Zuko seems…dulled, around the edges. More so than usual.

And doesn’t that just do something low and uncomfortable in Sokka’s gut, to realize that he’s become so accustomed to this subdued version of Zuko compared to the Fire Prince that chased them around the world that he’s only registering a slide into ‘worse.’

“You seem quiet,” Sokka finally says, wondering how much he wants to rock the boat of what little time they have for each other lately by probing at things he knows Zuko doesn’t like to have probed.

Zuko shrugs, glancing up, a barely-there flicker of gold before he bends back to the last of his noodles. His hair is long enough to shadow his eyes, now, and Sokka wants to run his hands through it, both to feel the soft strands and feel the way Zuko always leans into his touch, and to get a clear look at Zuko's eyes.

“You okay?” Sokka needs to see how firm of a line Zuko is feeling like drawing today before he pushes too hard against it.

Zuko’s eyes linger longer this time when they flick up. “I’m fine.”

Sokka raises his eyebrows at the deliberateness of the pause before Zuko’s usual automatic answer, at the tiredness in his eyes before they drop away again. A very firm line, then. Sokka…can work around that. If they aren’t going to touch Zuko’s particular mood, then Sokka can do what he can to lift it.

Sokka makes a show of humming thoughtfully, catching Zuko’s attention again before giving him a slow, careful once-over that has Zuko stilling. “You’re fine?” Sokka grins as Zuko slowly sets aside his bowl, a bit of interest sparking in his eyes. “Better check.”

Sokka reaches across the space between them, gently grabbing Zuko’s wrists and tugging him forward off his knees and closer until he can catch Zuko’s soft sigh with his lips. He runs his hands down Zuko’s back, enjoying the taste of spice on his tongue and the way Zuko melts again him, obligingly bearing Sokka to the floor, all heat and want and lean hardness.

It’s something of a relief that this, at least, is as sharp and intense as it’s always been. Being the sole object of Zuko’s attention, and the wonder of being able to touch and hold him back. This hasn’t changed even if Sokka is flinching from the feeling that everything around them is starting to, and that means Sokka can still cling to the reverence in Zuko’s touch with everything he has, can still chase that feeling and let it settle in his chest warm and fierce and burning.

Sokka lets his thoughts drift afterward in the minutes they have left. His mind wanders around the shape of Zuko, the smoke and spice scent of him. The feel of him underneath Sokka as Sokka lies draped across his back. The contented hum that vibrates through him as Sokka presses his lips to the back of his neck. The familiar always-so-fast beat of his heart. Sokka presses his face close between Zuko's shoulderblades, squeezing his eyes shut and trying to memorize the sound of it until the rhythm of Zuko’s heart is the only thing in his head other than the steady countdown to the moment Sokka needs to tear himself away.

&#45;-

Zuko watches Sokka get dressed through slitted eyes, still sprawled on the floor. He feels like he’s saving up memories again, and he doesn't know what to do about it. He hasn’t felt the urge to do this in a while, to imprint moments that can be pulled out later when he needs to feel like Sokka is close. The automatic way Sokka pulls his hair up, the way he always hops a little to settle his pants back around his hips, the softness around his eyes as he pulls a blanket off the bed and gently tucks it around Zuko like he isn't entirely sure that Zuko is awake.

Zuko closes his eyes at the last moment, though, so he doesn’t actually have to see Sokka leaving. He spins out his fire sense, following Sokka’s progress until he can’t hold onto the not-fire of him anymore, letting it go before he has to feel it forcefully pulled away by the limits of Zuko’s reach.

Zuko rolls over onto his back, knowing that he should clean up what’s left of dinner. He should get dressed, clean himself up, maybe make an appearance with Uncle. He can’t seem to make himself move, though, even to get up onto the bed, clutching the blanket Sokka wrapped around him and feeling so acutely alone that it’s an almost physical thing beside him. Even though Zuko is always alone, really, and always has been, and so it shouldn’t be anything remarkable, shouldn’t still be paralyzing to feel this way.

Zuko sighs, looking at the neat stack of takeout containers that Sokka left him, the fire pepper paste that he stole from the palace because he knows that Zuko misses it. Zuko presses a finger to the spot on his collarbone that he’s pretty sure is going to turn into a hickey, silently cataloging all the little traces of Sokka left behind in displaced objects and the evidence of touch. Wishing there were more of them.

A quiet, persistent, painful voice in the corner of his mind won’t stop pointing out that Sokka’s life is accelerating these past few days. That is started with finding Appa and now the world is really passing Zuko by, time slipping away faster than Zuko can even notice. That Sokka is already gone and just hasn’t realized it yet. A slow, gradual, aching separation, rather than a single sharp severing.

Sokka is on his way back to the palace, to walk the halls of power. Something everyone would agree is more important than staying here with Zuko, no matter how much Zuko wants him to. Zuko tries to picture Sokka at a table with nobles and finery and aristocratic double-speak, and Sokka in his favorite blue tunic and wolf tail and well-worn wrist wraps, all notes and maps and scattered brilliance. It makes Zuko smile, briefly. But it’s far too easy for his hazy, tired thoughts to slide toward other halls of power, other tables full of important men, other sets of maps.

Zuko used to walk in the heart of power, too, like that. Now it's Azula’s turn. And Sokka’s. And the Avatar’s. Now it is their time to take that seat at the table and put forth ideas and demand respect.

Zuko rolls onto his side and hitches the blanket over his shoulders and hopes it works out better for all of them than it ever did for him.

&#45;-

Sokka sends another messenger, late in the morning, that he can’t make it for their training session that afternoon. There’s another ministry meeting, suddenly, because there are so many ministries, and they all have so many meetings, Ba Sing Se, Zuko knows how it is—Zuko wants to raze this city to the ground—but breakfast tomorrow, for sure?

Zuko handles the last-minute change of plans much more calmly this time, merely letting the paper turn to ash in his fist as he walks off the floor instead of evaporating every single fucking pot of tea in this place like he wants to.

Zuko watches the ash flutter to the ground once he’s out of sight, numb. It’s the first time Zuko has willingly destroyed words that Sokka has given him. Another thing that Zuko gives away without even realizing it until it's done. Add it to the fucking list.

Zuko hauls himself to his room, because he has nowhere else to go, and lays down, letting exhaustion finally drag his eyes shut even though Agni is high in the sky. He should be working, but he just…can’t. The idea of it is overwhelming, the mere concept of pretending that every breath doesn’t feel a little bit like uncalled-for fire in his chest, his throat.

Zuko just wants to *sleep*, for once, but he can’t stop fretting, can’t stop thinking of Sokka without him, of Sokka in a ministry meeting alone even though Zuko knows, he *knows*, that Sokka has his sister and his friends with him. That Sokka has done this before and come out fine. But his mind won’t stop poking at the idea Sokka surrounded by the powerful without any idea of how power *works*, not with only a few months exposure to it, the place and the players shifting and sliding until it’s Sokka at a table with Azula, surrounded by fire, and Zuko still not there to help.

They’re anxious, slippery thoughts, almost images, until Zuko realizes that he’s nearly dreaming and claws himself awake out of the water, simultaneously numb with cold and feeling like he’s being scalded from the inside out. He wants to get up, to not go back there, but he feels his fatigue like a physical thing pressing down on his chest, smothering him back into darkness. He tries to lash out, to find something to cling to, something to haul himself up with. But the more he fights, the more Zuko feels like pieces of him are wiggling free, drifting away, cut loose by his writhing, the struggle to hold on only making him unspool faster.

When Zuko finally forces himself to stillness he feels like there’s nothing left of him, just a hollow, fragile shell that can’t bear up against the weight pressing against it. He crumbles under the pressure of cold lightning and silent judgment and quiet expectation, and there should be fire, should be heat to shore him up and press back, but it’s leaking out through the cracks, spinning away, leaving nothing behind but the guttering cold.

&#45;-

When Sokka shows up for breakfast the next day it’s Zuko who can’t be there. Sokka can’t manage to wrap his mind around it, even as Iroh patiently repeats himself over and over— Zuko hates repeating himself, it's clearly not a family trait—and gently turns Sokka away with a to-go bag of pastries and jumble of words that don’t make any sense.

Zuko needs rest, needs quiet, needs space. Sokka needs to let him be, not disturb him, because Zuko is sick, feverish, not well.

All Sokka can think as he stumbles back to get ready for the meeting he guesses he’s going to now is that when Sokka was sick, Zuko never left his side. It sits hard and misshapen in his chest, to cave to Iroh’s insistence and walk away when he knows that Zuko has never caved for anything in his life.

Sokka leaves the pastries for Toph. He doesn’t think he can stomach them.

&#45;-

Zuko is back in the Fire Nation, which doesn’t make sense because he hasn’t seen more than the fleeting edge of it in years. He isn’t allowed to be here, now more than ever, but he’s back in Caldera, in the *palace*, and Zuko knows it’s a death sentence. But instead of being in chains, he’s in fine robes, feeling strangely light in tropical-weight fabrics. His hair is long again, in a top knot which Zuko hasn’t been allowed since he was thirteen. It pulls oddly at his scalp, tension and weight where he isn’t used to feeling anything at all. There’s a headpiece pinned into his topknot, too, one that's heavier than Zuko would have any right to.

His feet seem to know where to go even if the rest of Zuko doesn’t, even if the wide, dark corridors are strangely empty, even for the palace, until finally, Zuko finds himself staring at the a throne. It sits empty on the far side of a wall of fire that seems to be getting along just fine without a Fire Lord to tend it.

It is not, Zuko thinks, supposed to be that way.

Zuko eventually realizes, slow and trickling and without surprise, that he isn’t alone. Azula is here, too. He should have expected it, that she would be waiting for him. Like his conscious acknowledgment was all she needed, Azula is suddenly on his left side, at his shoulder, just beyond the field of vision in his scarred eye. Her voice is familiar, strange, urging him to rest. She will take care of it, she is strong where he is weak. All he has to do is step aside. He knows how to do that, right? She doesn’t call him ‘Brother,’ or ‘Zuzu’, or even ‘Zuko’, and he feels ungrounded, on edge, waiting for something that never comes, some signal that he doesn’t know how to act without.

The fire in front of him trembles as Zuko considers her words, flames wavering in time with his resolve. And like that was its own signal, Uncle is suddenly there, too, on Zuko’s right, behind his shoulder but close enough to speak directly into Zuko’s ear. Urging him to listen, to hold on to what he was, to get out while he still can because this place is not for him. All he has to do is leave. He can do that, right?

Zuko stares at the unsteady flames until his eyes dry out from the heat, immobile, unable to move even when there’s low, angry hissing behind him, the rumbling of lightning, the crackling of furious fire. The throne room shatters around him and still Zuko can’t move, the Fire Lord’s headpiece tumbling to the floor, warped by heat but shining bright as ever until all Zuko can see is fire-licked gold, until he's falling in it, drowning it in, burning in it.

&#45;-

Sokka finally manages to get some answers from Iroh through sheer obstinate refusal to leave. It’s nighttime, so the teashop is closed, and Sokka has sent Toph as his proxy to the latest council meeting because all Sokka needs to accomplish there is to get idiots to shut up, and Toph is an effective bludgeon for that as anything. Which means that Sokka is free until morning and the Water Tribe thrives under the moon or something like htat, and he is fully willing and able to play this game all night long.

Iroh has played enough pai sho against Sokka by now to tell when he isn’t bluffing. The answers don’t make sense, though, as Iroh ushers Sokka into the kitchen with just an edge of put-upon hospitality and sets about making tea, a familiar routine that feels alien without Zuko’s silent, attention-demanding presence. Iroh can describe Zuko’s condition perfectly well in terms that Sokka can understand like fever, dry cough, sleeping—which sounds dangerously close to unconscious, the way Iroh says it. But the General keeps saying things like ‘spiritual metamorphosis’ and ‘actions in conflict with core values’ and ‘inner battle’ which is just…such a sack of shit.

“He doesn’t need spiritual guidance,” Sokka finally snaps when he can’t take it anymore, knuckles turning white around his teacup as he struggles to keep his volume down. “He needs medicine.”

Iroh frowns at the interruption, an open displeasure he doesn’t usually allow himself when Zuko is around. “My nephew’s illness may be affecting his body, but it is a fight being waged in his mind.”

“You don’t psychosomatic yourself into a fever so bad you can’t wake up!” Sokka loses the battle over his volume, because it’s been a long fucking day of making himself palatable for the people nominally in charge of the Earth Kingdom and his patience ran dry hours ago.

“Zuko has pushed himself hard,” Iroh says after a deliberate pause for tea, and Sokka can’t exactly refute that statement. “And he has been forced to finally contend with things that he has put off for far longer than is healthy.” That…sounds like Zuko, too.

“So he’s worn down from lack of sleep and working too hard,” Sokka paraphrases, scowling. “Which means he needs rest, and fluids, and—and herbs, or medicine, or—”

“There is only so much we can do for him, Master Sokka.” Iroh’s voice is understanding in a way that Sokka hates, and it’s hard to hide the reaction without Zuko here to remind him of why he should.

“We can help him,” Sokka insists, reminding himself that taking a swing at the Dragon of the West fixes nothing. It simmers low and ugly in the back of his throat, the way Iroh can look the other way while telling himself that he isn’t.

“There is only so much we can do,” Iroh repeats, even gentler now. The sympathy and empathy and lack of *action* make Sokka want to smash his teacup and shove the table, and he clamps his lips shut over whatever words might come out, bowing his head to hide his eyes, wondering how Zuko does this all the time with Iroh without screaming. Belatedly remembering that Zuko does scream, usually.

From the corner of his eye Sokka can see the General watching him, thoughtful and careful, before finally setting his cup down, leaning forward in his life-advice pose. “I know it is hard, when a loved one is suffering, and you cannot do anything to help.” Sokka’s hand spasms around the edge of the table, wanting to push away…he doesn’t know what, exactly. It's suddenly hard to meet Iroh’s eyes. “I learned a long time ago that my nephew is not someone who accepts help easily. Loving him requires an ability to stand back and let him make his choices, regardless of what they are, and be there when he is finally ready to ask for help. It is not an easy thing to do.”

“*No*,” Sokka snaps, shoving to his feet so abruptly that his chair topples over behind him, something like fury boiling through him. “It requires not letting him suffer in the first place.” Sokka is *done* with this. Being there for Zuko doesn’t mean letting him *hurt*, it means finding ways to *help.*

“Where are you going?” Iroh asks, mild curiosity over a layer of gratifying wariness as Sokka slams his chair back onto its feet and stalks toward the door.

“To get some fucking medicine,” Sokka growls, glaring whatever Iroh is about to say into silence. “I don’t care if it’s a spirit fever—if it’s affecting his physical body then medicine can affect it back.”

Sokka doesn’t wait for permission, or a reply, or anything from Iroh, just stalking out of the kitchen, the door slamming behind him—Spirits, he feels like Zuko right now—and stomping up the street toward their house. Katara will be there if he’s remembering everyone’s schedules right, which he is. Zuko would never want Katara in his space when he’s unconscious and vulnerable, but that doesn’t mean she can’t help Sokka sort through the depths of their pre-stocked, lavishly engraved medicine chest for anything that might help with fever.

&#45;-

Zuko is in the water again, in that state of cold where you’re so far past numbness that it feels like burning. The sounds of battle vibrate the air as he furiously treads, trying to keep his head from going under with the weight of his armor dragging him down.

He is distantly aware that there wasn’t armor when it actually happened, not that that’s ever mattered.

Zuko can hear Sokka’s voice, calling out, but no matter how frantically he turns, Zuko can’t see him in the wavering light of blasting jelly, in the silver of the moon. He can hear Uncle, too, but can’t find him either. And then Azula, and she shouldn’t be here, she shouldn’t, she’s supposed to be home, why is she *here—*

Zuko goes under, struggling in vain to shed layers and forcing his way back to the surface before he sinks so far that he will never get back. He knows how this works by now. The air is cold, full of smoke, like knives on the back of his throat, an attack from within as it hits his lungs, trying to make him cough, trying to fracture his focus.

Everything is dark and fire lit, but there’s no blue yet, no cascade of screams even though it will come because it always does, it just isn’t here yet. Which means that Zuko still has time*,* *he still* *has time*. If he can figure out where to go then he can figure out what to do when he gets there to try to stop it. Maybe this time he can finally be something other than useless.

Zuko just needs to figure out where to go. In the darkness, with sound echoing around him and his unscarred ear muffled and buzzing. He just needs to figure out where to go, if only he could see, could hear, could keep his head above water. He just needs to figure out where to go, if only the voices calling his name weren’t coming from all around him.

&#45;-

It takes Zuko a long, long, long moment to realize that he’s awake. Probably. He can’t entirely focus still, which suggests maybe dreaming. Uncle is here, speaking quiet, soothing words, which could mean either wakefulness or sleep. But Zuko doesn’t get sick, ever, so he acutely remembers what it felt like when he was thirteen to be in the grip of fever. This feels like those first days on the *Wani*, the same haze, the same sliding sense of reality.

Things change on you, he remembers through his muddled thoughts, if the fever gets bad enough. They shift and warp. You close your eyes one way and open them again to something different. Like the world has been bent by the heat of illness into a new shape, one that you didn’t choose, one that you just have to live with now.

Uncle is saying something, maybe something about the new form the world is going to take, the way he tried last time to explain over and over until Zuko finally understood how things were going to be now. Something about going through a spiritual transformation because releasing Appa was in direct conflict with his self-image. Telling Zuko that he will emerge on the far side of this pain as the Prince he was meant to be. As if Zuko needs to be told. As if Zuko’s earliest lessons weren’t in all the ways pain can teach, if you can just learn to listen.

Zuko manages to pry his unscarred eye open, taking too long to find Uncle hovering by his side, to register the belief and gentleness and quiet concern there. The effort is almost as exhausting as the expression on Uncle’s face. Zuko lets his eye close, lets himself release his grip on awareness. The world slides away again in bits and pieces, not quickly enough, for once. Has Uncle ever been able to see him? Or has Uncle only ever interacted with who he thinks Zuko is trying to be, instead of the Zuko actually before him.

Too many Zukos, in that thought. There should only be one of him. There should only be none of him, really, if things had gone the way they were supposed to go three years ago. Zuko doesn’t know if he has the strength anymore to keep track of all the versions of himself floating out there, to keep rejecting all the other parts clamoring for attention.

It’s fine, that no one sees all of him, not even himself, because Zuko hates the feeling of been seen. Sokka maybe does it, sometimes. But then Sokka doesn’t want all of what Zuko is, even if he sees it. Just the parts of him that are comfortable to hold, which is impossible. Zuko knows that he’s a jagged, sharp, burning thing. And Sokka isn’t here, he distantly realizes as the darkness finally sweeps back in. So maybe Sokka is finally starting to notice.

&#45;-

Zuko is thirteen again, burning, burned, worse than any lesson that’s come before. Someone is pressing a blade into his hands—a healer? Uncle? Azula? Father?—whispering words that don’t make sense, urging, telling, demanding. The burn is too bad, the flesh is dead, useless now. Cut away the pieces that can’t live anymore. It’s the only way to give the rest a chance to survive.

The blade is familiar in his hands. Good Earth Kingdom make. His fingers wrap around it like they were born for the hilt, and he can’t make them let go no matter how much he pleads and screams and cries and tries to make them understand. He is burning but the flesh is still alive, *he* is still alive, don’t, please, *please*.

Zuko shouts until his voice is raw and bloody, the taste of copper thick, but still they insist, they demand, they urge—it’s the only way. They press the blade into his hands and guide it toward his face and order him to do it, do it, before it’s too late, before too much burns away, cut away the parts that won’t survive, that cannot be allowed to live.

&#45;-

Sokka is leaving soon and he feels like he’s going to puke. He can’t not go, not without throwing off all the other timing that he’s been fighting and demanding these Earth Kingdom Generals pay attention to and respect. He can’t abandon this now and expect to be taken seriously ever again, no matter how compelling his plans are. And part of Sokka desperately wants to finally see his dad, like he can’t truly believe that Hakoda is still alive until Sokka sees him with his own eyes.

But Zuko is sick, still, feverish, still, and Sokka is struggling to think of anything except that. Even with Katara’s assurances that fevers are normal, that none of the symptoms Sokka has described seem particularly unique or alarming, Sokka can’t find a way to rest easy at the idea of leaving Zuko in Iroh’s care. It makes his chest tight, to know he won’t be able to swing by the teashop to check in and make sure that Zuko hasn’t gotten worse and that Iroh is actually giving Zuko the medicine Katara found. Which Sokka shouldn’t *need* to check because Iroh has never *not* given it—it’s in the form of tea, after all—but Sokka just needs to do *something*, needs to be here.

Except he won’t be, soon. Not without compromising the mission.

Sokka is at Zuko’s side for now, at least. He holds Zuko’s dry hand, gently dripping water between his parched lips and trading out cool washcloths against his forehead and the back of his neck. It will be okay. Sokka knows that. Zuko might be delirious, asleep in a way that isn’t restful, hot in a way that doesn’t feel right, bending erratic enough that Sokka is noticing the weird way the candles move even through whatever Iroh must be doing to keep it contained. But he’s anchored to Sokka’s hand like he never wants to let go and that’s normal, and steady, and sure, so it’s going to be fine.

“Please be okay,” Sokka whispers, pressing his lips to the hot, hot, skin on the back of Zuko’s hand. “I need you to be okay, alright? I know you’re strong. I know you’ll be fine, because you’re always fine.” Sokka takes a deep, steadying breath. “So I know you’ll be okay. And I’m going to have so much to tell you when I get back. So you better be ready to hear all about it.”

Zuko mumbles something, unclear, head turning restlessly against his pillow. It’s probably not meant for Sokka, but he waits for Zuko to settle just in case.

“I’m going to see my dad, you know,” Sokka murmurs, massaging the tense muscles of Zuko’s hand the way he knows Zuko enjoys when he’s awake, even if he would never admit it. “I haven’t seen him in a long time. I’m really excited. But I’m also scared, you know? I’m not a kid anymore.”

Sokka glances up, like Zuko might actually answer. Would Sokka even be able to say these things, if he thought Zuko were actually listening? He hopes the answer is yes. He wants it to be. “I was thinking of telling him about you, actually. Get it all out there and whatnot. I know it’s not really your style, though, so I’ll wait until you can decide you want me to do that.” Which will be soon, because Sokka refuses to let it be any other way. “So I really need you to be better when I get back so we can talk about it, okay? And you can tell me what you think. I miss you.”

Sokka sighs into the silence, heart twisting at not even having Zuko’s familiar, loud body language in reply. He gets fresh water, fresh washcloths, busying his hands until there’s nothing left to do, until he can’t pretend anymore that he doesn’t see the way the light is shifting to late morning.

Sokka leans over to brush a light kiss against Zuko’s lips, eyes prickling at the passivity of them, so anathema to how Zuko *is*. It feels like Sokka is rubbing his own heart raw to gently work his hand out of Zuko’s death grip. Zuko’s fingers clutch convulsively, a choked, dry noise of protest dragging itself out of his chest as Sokka pulls away.

Sokka swallows back an answering sound, suddenly traitorously wishing that they’d never found Appa, had never shone light on the Dai Li, that none of the reins of power had ever been placed into his hands. For all the ability Sokka now has to do good, to make a real difference in the war, he hates that it’s forcing him to walk away right now. Sokka feels ragged as he stumbles down the stairs to the street, thanking the Spirits every step that he manages to avoid Iroh’s too-seeing gaze and wondering if this is what it feels like to be compromised, or just to finally get the things you thought you wanted.

&#45;-

Zuko is prone, immobile, trapped in something soft and heavy and clinging until he could be suffocated under the weight of it, strangled by it, and no one would ever know. His eyes strain into the darkness, everything in him going still like a caught rabbaroo when a figure leans over him.

It’s Azula, as she used to be, round-faced and big-eyed. No, that was just a trick of the dim light. It’s Azula as she is now, fierce and sharp. No, it’s Azula as she will be, worn to a blade and hard-eyed. No—it’s not Azula, it’s their *mom*, sad and resolute. Except no, the hand on his shoulder is too heavy for that, feels more like Uncle’s broad hold.

“Never forget who you are, my love,” Ursa’s voice echoes from memories.

“Forget,” Uncle’s voice echoes from shadows.

Azula’s eyes are cold, inquisitive as she leans over him. “Have you already forgotten?”

&#45;-

Zuko is back in that forge, in that town, in that other life, in that other time, when all he had to care about was working to earn food for Jasmine and maybe himself. It’s a clear, clean thought, a clear, clean purpose, one that Zuko feels like he can breathe around, up until an ingot of raw metal is pressed into his hands.

Zuko knows, with the surety of dreams, that he needs to transform this raw ore into whatever it’s supposed to be. But the smith is walking away before Zuko realizes that he doesn’t know what the final form is supposed to look like. Zuko calls out but the man doesn’t turn. He tries to follow, but he can’t move, feet welded to the floor. All he can do is look down, helpless, at all the tools arrayed before him, each with their specific purpose and design and no idea what intent he’s supposed to bend them toward even if he knew how to use them in the first place.

The metal requires both hands to hold. It’s ugly, jagged, raw. No one will ever want it like this, and Zuko needs to make something someone will want if he wants to earn what he came for, if he wants to be able to demand what he’s worth. But Zuko doesn’t *know,* not any of it. With a roar of frustration, he sweeps the tools off the table, watching with savage satisfaction as they fall to the floor, out of sight, out of reach.

Zuko doesn’t need them, doesn’t want them, can do it all on his own without them. He doesn’t need to be constrained by these Earth Kingdom ways, or anyone’s ways or expectations. With a snarl he lets fire and heat pour into his hands, concentrating the force of it instead of letting it flow away. The metal turns red, then white, becoming soft under his grip until Zuko can use his fingers to shape it, his skin miraculously untouched by the heat of it. Zuko has no idea what will come out the other side, but his fire is loosed now and that’s as good a guide as any.

&#45;-

Zuko is falling, which is a new sensation, crashing through water, which is not. He struggles to the surface, catching one ragged breath of air before he is falling again, into a sheet of flame, burning on all sides, the fire angry and hungry until Zuko manages to get his breath control and force the flames away from his skin. Falling again, then, into the earth this time, buried alive, clawing his way free only to somehow still be falling, falling, falling no matter how many times he fights to get back up again.

Maybe he’s supposed to stop fighting. Maybe he’s supposed to just close his eyes and breathe out and let himself slip under. Except Zuko has never known how to stop struggling, to just stay down, even when it was good for him. Especially then.

Zuko falls for years, and eventually notices that every time he does, something changes. He’s wearing robes he hasn’t worn since childhood, confining because they haven’t grown but he has, until he tears his way free. Then armor, the weight of it dragging him down until he can wiggle out of it. His Blue Spirit guise, unable to see. Tattered Earth Kingdom rags, exposed. A teashop apron, vulnerable. Water Tribe blues. A Fire Sage’s headdress. Yuyan facepaint. The Fire Lord’s crown. A monk’s robes.

Zuko crashes down with a gasp into a room, instead of an element, eyes snapping open, back arching as he tries to throw himself upright before realizing that he isn’t in freefall anymore, isn’t being suffocated or drowned or erased. He scrambles to his feet, because getting off the ground is the one thing he never needed to be taught, limbs loose and sloppy as he stumbles toward the door. His door. His room.

Zuko freezes at the jarring familiarity, then at the sight of himself in the mirror—when did he put a mirror there? Does it matter? He barely recognizes what he sees. Fire Nation reds, his scar stark and angry, dao hilts framing his head, Sokka’s bite marks visible along his collarbone.

Oh, he thinks, like a gong ringing inside his chest, shattering the dream around him back into blackness. Yes. This.

&#45;-

Zuko opens his eyes to Agni’s gentle touch, a soft sigh passing his lips. His breath feels easy in his lungs, his body sore but not actively aching, and Zuko slowly realizes that he’s awake, alive, okay. No longer ill, his fever broken, as true a sleep a firebender can get in the daylight crawling up over him for the first time in weeks as his chest quietly resounds with *yes, yes,* *this is right, yes, this can be the way.*
