And Agni, apparently the one ‘could’ that Zuko is willing to gamble on, the one he'd already decided to risk, is the one where Sokka could be okay, at the end of all this.

“*Go!”*

Zuko’s voice cracks, pleading, and finally, *finally* Uncle moves. He’s visibly distressed to do it, but he bows to Zuko’s wishes, because when push comes to shove Uncle always does when Zuko truly digs his heels in. Or maybe because Iroh is still too much of a General to waste any more time in the midst of battle, to risk his escape route closing over with nothing to gain for it, and Zuko can’t be anything but grateful for it right now.

Zuko doesn’t watch Uncle go, not with a much more immediate concern at hand. He turns his back on Uncle’s retreat to face the imminent explosion that hasn’t moved since it first entered the room, trying to be relieved that none of the Dai Li move to follow Uncle even as part of him shudders that it can't be good, for the Dai Li to not care about the Dragon of the West.

Azula looks like she’s on the verge of laughter. “You’re going to hold me off, Zuzu? Really?”

Zuko doesn’t waste breath on a reply, just falls into an offensive stance, some part of him straining to rip free and fight even as a thread of his inner flame feels cold and thin at the idea of throwing fire at his sister. He breathes through the feeling, knowing she'll have no similar qualms if she's feeling properly motivated, forcing himself to watch her eyes, her torso, her stance, waiting for the flicker of an opening that will come before an attack.

Which is a mistake, to get so focused on just one thing. It always is. Azula knows better than to reveal anything that way, especially when someone expects it. She catches his eye, a slight smirk on her lips, gaze as tawny gold as he remembers, as piercing as he remembers, Fire Nation through and through, enough for Zuko to forget that her clothes say Dai Li.

Azula barely twitches a finger and Zuko is hit from all side by cuffs of stone, bands of rock, clouds of grit, the flames he tries to throw snuffed, his arms pinned, his wrists pulled to the floor, his shoes sunk into liquid stone. Zuko can’t back in a shout, a near-animal panic clawing at him as he heaves against his restraints. He feels wild with adrenaline, nearly frantic with it in the few desperate breaths it takes him to fight himself to tense stillness, his chest heaving as he battles against a lifetime of instincts that scream to get up, get up, *get up*, *getup.*

Azula waits for him to master himself before she walks over, the clack of her boots a crisp metronome that Zuko could set his heartbeat to. “That was foolish, Zuzu,” she observes, and she doesn’t have to say it for Zuko to be sure she means everything that led him to this moment, not just his attempt to fight.

She crouches down, robes pooling elegantly around her, and he sucks in a shuddering breath at being so trapped and having her so close. She cocks her head, eyes curious as she studies his face, his clothing, his hair, before finally reaching out to trace the edge of his scar with one red-painted fingernail, thoroughly ignoring his glare. “You never do learn, do you,” she murmurs.

“I don’t need lessons from you,” Zuko rasps, jerking away from her touch as far as he can before he hits the edge of his restraints. He glowers at her, watching her cool amusement and toying with spitting fire into her face. It would be emotionally satisfying and dumb as shit when he can’t do anything else.

“No?” She sounds genuinely curious. “And yet all you do is find new ways to hurt yourself when you’re on your own.” She reaches forward until he would need to fold himself away and around his restraints to try to evade her touch, pressing at the ridge of scar below his eye, the spot where it’s deepest, where he feels it least. “You never did like to be protected.”

Zuko shakes her hand off again, sharp, and she pulls back with a smirk. “I don’t need protection.”

Azula cocks her head. “But you think your little peasant does? Sending the Dragon of the West away to go check up on him when dear Uncle Iroh could have gotten you both out of here?” Zuko stiffens at the suggestion of knowledge in her words, at the suggestion that maybe Sokka isn't the one she has, if he can trust any suggestions she makes. Her lips curl, the hint of a smile. “But I suppose you know that I would have just followed. Don't you want me to meet him properly? Don't you want to introduce us?”

Zuko glowers, trying and probably failing to hide how desperately he wants the topic to change. He should know better than to react to a vulnerable spot, but Agni, he can’t even find words around how deeply he doesn’t want Azula's attention on Sokka in any way. Zuko is willing to do…a lot of things, actually, to shift her focus somewhere else.

She pouts when he doesn’t reply, theatrical and exaggerated. “That hurts, Zuzu. You have no need to worry, it’s not like he’s to *my* tastes, Brother. Though I supposed if rough and crass is your thing…” She shrugs, like there’s no accounting for preferences, and then adds, like poison, “Ty Lee certainly seemed to hit it off with him.”

Instinctive, misplaced, protective anger boils up in his chest at the idea of Azula knowing *anything* about Sokka, let alone enough to have judgments about his fucking suitability. It rises in him so hot and sudden that Zuko can’t hold back his snarl, hating the way her eyes flash with satisfaction to have finally drawn it out.

Agni, Zuko should have planned for this. Should have expected it. Did he really think she would leave anything of his untouched?

“Poor Zuzu,” Azula murmurs, leaning close and watching him struggle. Her tawny eyes are hard, flat, even as her tone pretends at idle curiosity. “How long did it take you to forget yourself? To forget what it means to be descended of Agni? How desperate did you have to be, to choose that? What a typical *boy*—” She flicks his wayward hair out of his face, wrinkling her nose at the messiness of it. “—letting yourself get led around by the dick at the first piece of ass to turn your head," she says, voice dripping acid before going cloyingly sweet. "I bet he loved that, didn't he? You made it so *easy* for him, Brother.”

Zuko’s chest heaves, his unscarred eye burning with how wide it’s peeled, unable to stop the way her words make him want to flinch, make his inner flame twist and writhe in protest. He watches her watch him, his heart stuttering in his throat as he recognizes the expression settling over her features, exactly the same even after all this time. He feels pinned, caught, trapped far beyond the restraints holding him down. Azula has a secret she's waiting for the right moment to share, one she’s been holding for the time when it will hurt the most, and she's finally seeing the opportunity.

“And all along,” she sing-songs like childhood taunts, “He was using you to plan an invasion of Caldera on the Day of the Black Sun.”

…No.

Zuko feels like he’s choking, the whole world lurching to a stop around him, his eyes filling with nothing but Azula’s predator-flat gaze as she waits to see how much he knew. “What," he finally rasps out, barely any strength to the word and unable to care about it. No. No, no, no. He wouldn’t. He *wouldn’t*. He—*No.*

“Oh, you didn’t know?” Azula says with mock pity, something like satisfaction flashing in her eyes. “Poor baby. All you had to do was follow him one day, you know. From your little tea house straight to his plans.”

Zuko's inner flame shudders as he stares, paralyzed by the implication that she did just that. She smiles, reading his silence. She’s always been able to do that, better than anyone, and he’s never hated that fact quite so much.

“The Avatar was never hiding, and neither was your little savage,” Azula says, words going precise and wielded to cut. “And I’ve always known where you were, Brother.”

“Azula,” Zuko manages to get out, a warning that she doesn’t even acknowledge.

“Did you think I didn't *see*? That I wouldn't *notice*? I knew he would lead the way to you soon enough. And he did. Straight to you, over, and over, and over.”

“Azula.” His voice is firmer now, harsh, and she pauses, giving him a considering look.

“What? Am I saying something you don’t want to hear? Is it unpleasant to actually face your own actions?” She tsks when Zuko just glares. “Speak up, Zuzu. Show me all that breath control you claim to have.”

“Why are you *doing* this?” He asks, the words bursting out nearly without his permission. He can’t expect her to answer, not truly, not like this, but Agni—he needs to *know.* “Why—” He tugs against his bonds, eyes flicking to the Dai Li symbol on her tunic, the green bow framing her face.

Azula snorts, tossing her head. “You know why, Brother,” Azula says, suddenly leaning in, viper bat quick, to hiss low and burning against his unscarred ear, “Because *I* never settle for just what someone deigns to give me. *I* take what I’m owed. A lesson *you* would do well to finally learn, Zuko.”

&#45;-

By the time they’re finally escorted to Kuei—past three layers of guards, through four hand-offs to successively important servants, and after signing an honestly disturbing number of forms—Sokka feels like all the wind has escaped his sails. Not all at once; more like there’s a slow rip in the canvas, one that’s pulled taught every time they try to catch any momentum, the tear stretching wider and wider every time they try to move until there’s more air flowing through the sail than pushing against it, until you’re foundering in the water, drifting on the tides.

All the urgency in the world still can’t move the wheels of Ba Sing Se any faster than they want to turn.

The Earth King glances up from his lunch when they finally enter, a scroll in one hand, Bosco at his side, and even in his distraction, Sokka has to suppress a fascinated shudder at the bear. It just looks *wrong*.

“Sokka! Aang! Toph!” Kuei sounds his usual mix of excited and startled. “You’re back early! What a pleasant surprise. Come, join me for lunch.”

“Sorry, but there’s no time,” Sokka says before Aang can muster the appropriately diplomatic ‘no,’ even as servants begin to scurry in from the edges of the room with more place settings. “Katara’s in danger.”

“Katara?” Kuei’s eyebrows shoot up in surprise. “But I just saw her at the Council of Five! The Kyoshi Warriors said she would be spending some time with them.”

Toph shifts slightly, her minuscule nod confirming the truth of the Earth King’s words, and Sokka sighs in relief, exhaling some of his driving urgency in the process. Aang must have seen a future danger, then. Something imminent, which means they can't relax yet, but Sokka so prefers to focus on plans to avert danger than to deal with it when it's already happened.

Sokka shares a quick, relieved glance with Aang, then steps back to let the airbender make their excuses for a hasty retreat back out of the palace. Sokka barely listens, wholly consumed with adjusting his plans. If the Kyoshi Warriors are with Katara then Suki will be in play in her defense. Perfect. Sokka knows he can rely on Suki to be a calm, cool head, and her Warriors to be equally competent. And between Katara's bending, and Aang, and fuck, Toph inventing *metalbending—*

Sokka nearly grins as they make their hasty way back through the hallways. He can’t wait to fight alongside Suki again and kick the ass of whatever danger thinks it can come for Katara on their watch.

&#45;-

The wind is very much back in Sokka’s sails when they reach their house, and not in a happy go-lucky ‘the gang’s all here’ kind of way. It’s more of a slow, creeping sense of dread, crawling up his spine and winding his muscles tighter and tighter with the knowledge that he needs to do something, now, immediately, as soon as he can, but with no idea what he needs to do.

The house is empty. Which could be fine this late in the afternoon. Katara is busy, and she could easily be spending time with the Kyoshi Warriors somewhere other than here.

But there are no snacks. And Sokka's spent too much time on the road and on the ice with hunger gnawing at his stomach to be able to overlook the presence of food, even when he’s not actively hungry. This house *always* has snacks, multiple kinds, at all hours, a constant flow of new offerings. Ever since they first stepped foot in Ba Sing Se, even the days when they barely spend any time in the house except to sleep, there’s always been fruit and pastries and meat skewers and nuts and noodles, tea always fresh and hot.

“Something’s wrong,” Aang says, shifting his glider slowly toward a more offensive grip.

There’s no food in sight, not even empty plates or serving platters waiting for new bites. Like someone knew there was no reason to bring anything today.

Sokka takes a deep breath, refusing to get ahead of himself. “Look for clues, guys,” he says, voice level, firm. “Anything missing, any signs of a struggle. Signs of *no* struggle, of other people. You know the drill.”

They all know how to do this by now, fanning out to work their way methodically through the space. Aang starts at the back of the house, with Sokka and Toph sweeping the common areas at the front, Sokka desperately hoping for some sign of Suki, or Katara, or fuck, even Joo Dee back again. Some sign of *something*. They haven’t been searching for long when Toph suddenly goes still, head cocked.

“What is it?” Sokka prompts, hand resting lightly on the hilt of his boomerang. Aang hurries joins them at Sokka’s words, using bending to make his steps light and nearly soundless, looking tense and ready to fight.

Toph frowns, then snaps around. “Someone’s at the door.”

Sokka eyes the tall, stately wood doors, suddenly finding them ominous and menacing rather than opulent. There’s no knock, no one announcing themselves, and Sokka glances toward the windows, the ceiling, trying to see how they can assess the threat without making themselves vulnerable to attack.

“Dai Li?”

“No…” Toph’s expression twists in concentration, then suddenly relaxes into a look of surprised pleasure. “An old friend.” She strides to the door without further explanation, throwing it open while Sokka and Aang scramble to hug the walls so they can flank her without being visible, which is what they’re *supposed* to do, they *drilled*. “Old Man!”

Sokka can only partially see the backlit shape, can barely hear the low rumble of greeting. But his heart still stutters in premonition, some unconscious part of his brain sparking with recognition a second before Toph steps back and invites Iroh inside.

“Toph, what the f—how do you know him?” Sokka steps away from the wall in shock, drills forgotten and boomerang loose at his side.

“Huh?” Toph frowns in his general direction. “Me and the Old Man met camping. We had some tea.” Of course they did. “How do *you* know him?”

Sokka stares. “…He’s Zuko’s uncle?”

“…Well. Damn.”

Sokka can only gape. How did she not—Toph’s been doling out Dragon of the West facts of the day like it’s her new favorite pastime! “How did you not notice? You were there when he got injured. Zuko was there, too!”

“I don’t know, Snoozles,” Toph scowls, crossing her arms, jaw set defensively. “Maybe because people’s heartbeats sound different when they’ve just been injured to the point of *unconsciousness* than when they’re relaxed in the woods. How about that? Does that work for you? I'm not magic, you know.”

“There is no time for this,” Iroh cuts in before Sokka can work up a reply, managing to sound both apologetic and not at all sorry at the same time. He glances at the others before settling on Sokka, face grave. “Princess Azula has captured your other companion.” Sokka’s heart stops. “And my nephew.”

The world tilts, everything in him grinding to a halt. Sokka stays on his feet through some divine miracle, but he can’t move, can’t speak, his mind caught in a loop, bouncing over and over between Katara and Zuko and captured and *Azula* and danger and both of them, *both of* *them.*

“What about the Kyoshi Warriors?” Aang asks, and Sokka is aware that he is continuing to not react, to not do anything, that Aang is shooting him anxious little glances, but he doesn’t have the capacity to do anything about it right now over the frantic refrain of *both of them,* *both of them, both of them* resounding in his ears.

“I know nothing about them,” Iroh says, shaking his head. “I am sorry.”

Sokka finally finds his voice, if not his coherency. “What—how—”

“I do not know how the young waterbender was captured. But we were invited into an ambush, at the palace.” At the *palace*—fuck, fuck, *fuck*. Why did Sokka ever think that *Kuei* would know what was going on in his own city? Why didn’t he think about the fact that Toph can’t find a lie if someone doesn’t know they’re telling one? “Zuko stayed behind so that I could warn you of the trap Azula is trying to set.”

“*Zuko* stayed behind? So that *you*—”

“Sokka,” Aang interrupts quietly, but Sokka waves him off, intent on Iroh, feeling like every inch of him is on the verge of vibrating out of control as Iroh's expression turns heavy.

“I did not know what he planned to do,” the General says, voicce weighed down with regret.

Sokka stares. “It’s *Zuko*.”

Iroh winces. “My nephew concealed his—"

“He *concealed—*how did you not—do you know *anything* about—”

*“Sokka*!” Sokka flinches back from Aang’s shout, even Toph stepping back in surprise. “This isn’t helpful right now,” Aang says, firm, glancing at Iroh as if he’s thinking about including him in the reprimand too. “We need to think about what to do next.”

Sokka turns to Aang, feeling like his eyes are peeled open too wide, like his knees are too unsteady, like something frantic and dangerous is crashing against his ribs trying to get free. “Aang—” His voice cracks under the reality that *both of them are in danger*.

“Sokka,” Aang repeats, voice going helpless a moment before he rallies. “It’s okay. We’ve— we’ve done this before, right? We rescue people all the time. We know what to do.”

Sokka hears the words, but it’s like he can’t hold onto them, can’t make them feel real. He feels like he’s spiraling, spinning loose. They’ve saved people in the past, plenty of people, but Spirits, it's *Katara* and *Zuko*. It’s *both* of them, at the same time. Both of them not here for the fight, not at his side, both of them at risk. What if Sokka has to *choose*?

Fuck, how could he even—his little sister and his—and Zuko? But at the same time, how could there even be a choice? Fuck, Sokka would give anything he has to avoid the possibility of there needing to be one, but if there is…He feels like he's going to be sick, the awareness of what he would have to do mingling in his stomach with a kind of tacky, sticky dread that says there was never a choice in the first place. Not really.

Spirits, Sokka doesn't have a plan for this. He never thought—he never—

But even if Sokka knows what needs to be done, even if he can make himself believe it, he doesn’t know if he could survive actually doing it, if he had to. He doesn’t know how he could walk away from that and have anything left of himself anymore.

“Crap,” Toph mutters, then louder, putting some snap in her voice, “Hey, Snoozles. *Snoozles.*” Sokka jerks toward her on instinct, mind nothing but blank horror. “We need a plan.”

Sokka looks at her, uncomprehending, feeling like he can barely breathe as his thoughts spiral, spiral, spiral, spinning him around, spinning down toward his core, already feeling like they’re hollowing him out, scraping him raw, shredding parts of himself that feel vital.

“*Sokka*,” she growls again. “So Sparrowkeet is captured. Fine. What does it matter? What’s changed?”

Sokka sucks in a hard, sharp breath, jagged disbelief and fear-driven anger rushing into the hollow parts of himself. “What do you mean ‘what’s—‘”

“Katara is in danger,” she cuts in, setting her jaw and bracing her feet. “We don’t know where the Kyoshi Warriors are. Zuko was never part of the rescue to begin with. So what’s. Changed.”

Sokka stares at her, more dirt-smudged than usual and fresh off a kidnapping and inventing a new form of bending and braced for battle, waiting to be told what direction to point herself in. Waiting for Sokka. Sokka forces himself to take a calming, Zuko-style breath, then another, and another, until his mind slowly scrabbles back into something resembling motion. “We know who we’re fighting against now.”

“That’s good,” Aang says, encouraging, either for the insight or the fact that Sokka is finally capable of responding to a question.

“And we know that Katara is underground, still. Captured.”

Toph cracks her knuckles. “We can work with that.”

“And we have a second target to rescue.”

Toph and Aang nod, with various degrees of agreement.

“But Katara needs to come first,” Aang says, shifting uncomfortably even as his face sets, resolute.

Sokka glowers, forcing out tight words that aren’t allowed to be a snarl. “Whichever one we find first, comes first. Are you going to pass up a firebender’s help to rescue her?” To find her, even, if Zuko had the wherewithal when Katara ambushed him to note the feel of her not-flame thing, if that's even a thing that maybe he can find her the way he can find Sokka…

Aang bites his lip, hesitating before conceding with a nod, and Sokka can finally feel himself falling into that calm-amidst-the-storm state that comes over him when there’s a mission to execute and a battle to plan. His people need him, and Sokka will be there for them. All of them. He turns to Iroh. “Where would she hold them?”

“I don’t know,” Iroh admits.

“Would she split them up?”

“I am not sure. Maybe yes, maybe no.”

“How about what *do* you know?” Sokka snaps, not even trying to hide his frustration. What’s the point of Zuko sacrificing himself to send Iroh if Iroh is going to be *useless*.

“Not much,” the Dragon of the West says, yellow eyes suddenly glinting, hard. “But I have a Dai Li agent waiting around the corner who should know plenty.”

&#45;-

The Dai Li are dragging Zuko somewhere, using their bending on the stone cuffs on his wrists rather than bothering to touch him, which is just…such a gratuitous, prissy display of power, made all the worse by the fact that Zuko actually appreciates not having their hands on him on top of everything else. Though the band of stone over his mouth is a rather terrifying touch, given how fast it formed and how well he can still breathe. Apparently, Azula knows that Zuko can spit fire. Or maybe just didn’t want to risk it.

It should be demeaning, being dragged through the halls of a palace gagged and trussed up. It should be a lot more than that. But Zuko is too busy quietly panicking to care. He’s repeating to himself as loud as he can that Azula always lies, always, trying to drown out every other voice in his head that somehow all sound too much like her.

Her words ooze through his thoughts like the time he got stung by a stingjelly as a kid. Even knowing that he would survive—Azula had told him so, and she was never wrong about the things that would kill him—Zuko had been horrified that he could *feel* the way the venom crept through his veins, sapping his strength, paralyzing his muscles, lighting him on fire from the inside with every beat of his heart. Knowing it was poison, that it was temporary, didn’t make it hurt any less, just like knowing that Azula always lies doesn’t make ‘*you made* *is so* easy *for him, Brother’* and ‘*all along he was using you’* and *‘inasion'* and *'Day of the* *Black Sun’* stop ringing through his head.

Azula doesn’t know Sokka. She has no idea, she *can’t*, and Zuko won’t let himself doubt and question because of her. He knows how she is, how she twists and contorts her words to erode the ground you try to stand on. Lies and lies and lies, until your own panic and uncertainty takes on life and does all the work for her.

Always lies, except when the truth hurts more.

The Dai Li suddenly stop, and Zuko forces himself to belatedly pay attention to his surroundings as the agents open a hole in the wall in a casual display of truly impressive precision earthbending, revealing a long tunnel shaft lit in a familiar green light that Zuko didn’t think he would ever see again. This…doesn’t seem good. Though it also seems *secret,* which Zuko needs to get himself together and start paying attention to. Because if capturing an exiled Prince of the Fire Nation is something for the Dai Li to conceal, then Zuko might still have room to maneuver in whatever game Azula is playing.

The Dai Li certainly give him nothing more to work with, though, as they shove Zuko unceremoniously into the tunnel, his outraged shout breaking free as they bend the stone off his wrists and ankles and mouth. Zuko pulls himself in tight, gaining control of his own limbs again with bare moments to spare before he ricochets off one wall, then another, grunting with impact and trying to protect his head best he can as he tumbles downward.

Zuko hits the ground hard enough to knock the breath from his lungs. He bites back a groan, refusing to dwell on the clawing panic of breathlessness and the way it makes his inner flame shudder—it will come back, it always does—and forcing himself to take in his surroundings when really, he just wants to curl around himself and remember how breathing is supposed to work. It’s hard to see in the flickering light that has to be coming from some kind of reflecting and refracting crystal or bioluminescence, because Zuko can’t feel any fires as he reaches out. Which is frustrating and inconvenient on multiple fronts, but not exactly unexpected.

Zuko’s fire sense flows over something human-sized and warm just as a crunch of gravel has him jerking and stumbling to his feet, breath still only half back, but Zuko’s worked with worse. He whirls into a defensive stance, fresh bruises already protesting and his fire leaping up to bite under his skin as Katara steps into the light.

Zuko doesn’t see any water—he looks frantically enough—but Katara plants her feet and raises tight fists anyway, looking fully ready to fight even if it means physically hurling herself at him.

Perfect. Fucking perfect. Just what he needs right now. Captured by Azula, trying to prevent Sokka from walking into a trap, trying to *figure out* the trap, and facing nothing but a wall of hostility from his…boyfriend’s—lover’s—whatever’s—sister.

*“You,”* Katara spits.

Zuko grunts, hating the way his shoulders crawl toward his ears without his permission at her tone. “Me.”

“What is this, another trap?” Her eyes dart around, suspicious. Checking for threats, presumably, the lack of them somehow making her look even more ready to fight.

“Probably,” Zuko snorts, chancing a quick glance up to where the tunnel shaft disappears into the darkness above him. Azula would never set just one trap if she could set many.

Zuko snaps his attention back down when Katara fucking *growls* at him. “I should have known that someone from the *Fire Nation* would—”

Zuko falls back with a glare, slicing a hand through the air to cut off her words as his inner fire twists, already too high with fear and confusion and anger, always anger, to deal with whatever guilt she’s trying to throw on top. Katara jerks, scrambling back into a defensive stance, her face going tighter and more furious, so much fury that it almost starts to look like fear.

Zuko hesitates, uncertain in the face of her retreat. But Zuko has the advantage here, he realizes. It’s almost the opposite of when she threatened him at the Jasmine Dragon. Her element isn’t available, and Zuko carries his inside himself, and no longer has to conceal its presence.

This could go badly for her, if he wanted it to, and he should probably use that, should probably press his advantage and seize whatever moment this is. But Agni’s tits, the last thing he has space to care about right now is *Katara.* “Can we just…not?”

“What,” she challenges, regaining some of her bravado. “Don’t like being held accountable?”

Zuko glowers, annoyed, because no, he doesn’t, not particularly, and especially not from her, and Agni, he does *not* have the footing or the control he needs right now to treat Sokka’s sister with anything approaching the care he probably should.

“You think you can just do whatever you want and not have to answer for it?”

Zuko inhales, slow and forceful through his nose, trying to leash his temper when nearly everything in him wants to rage at hearing Sokka’s kind of words in that kinnd of tone, the only thing stopping him the thin awareness that doing so would accomplish exactly nothing right now except to waste his energy. “What, exactly, is it that you think I’ve done,” he grits out, the words openly irritated and tight but at least at a non-shouting volume.

“You tell me!”

Zuko stares at her, momentarily mute with incredulous fury before taking a page out of Azula’s book and pointedly transferring his attention elsewhere. He scans their surroundings, looking for tunnels, openings, crevices that can maybe be wiggled through with enough commitment, doing it all as dismissively as he possibly can while still keeping Katara always on his right side and in his field of vision. Just fuck *all* of that. Zuko is *beyond* having any patience left for baseless accusations. He already has more than enough well-founded ones he’s trying to deal with, more than enough real threats to deal with her intangible ones. Katara takes being dismissed about as well as Zuko ever does, making a lot sound of frustration and trying to move into his line of vision. "Tell me," she says when she manages to catch his eye, clearly spoiling for a fight in a way that Zuko recognizes and does *not* appreciate being the object of. He feels a stab of sympathy for Uncle. “Do you even care about Sokka? At all? Or was the whole thing just pretend so you could get closer to the Avatar?”

Zuko should be used to needling, to the sharp tongues of little sisters. He turns on her in an instant, snarling, fire on his breath and sparks spitting from his hands, uncontrolled and dangerous and Zuko isn’t sure if his fire broke his control or if he cut it loose, but either way Zuko and his inner fire are *perfectly* aligned right now in their clean, sharp rage.

“I have *never*,” Zuko hisses, smoke curling from his fists as Katara falls back in open alarm before bracing herself again, “Pretended.”

Katara scoffs in disbelief and Zuko’s inner fire is crawling up his throat, furious. “You have no idea—” He cuts himself off, breathing deep before he says something he can’t take back. He can't lay into her, even when the wild parts of him, the parts that learned early and often the price of seeming weak, want to hit back as hard as she’s aiming for him. She's important to Sokka, and Zuko can’t ruin that. No matter how good it would feel in this specific moment.

When he can finally speak again, the words come out low, just this side of threatening. “How long have I been with Sokka, Katara?”

Uncertainty flits over her face, her expression turning mulish even as she hesitates.

“*How long.”*

“I don’t know—”

“You do,” Zuko snaps, sparks flying with the words. “Sokka told you. The day he found me here. He told you. How. Long.”

“…Months.”

“*Months.* And how many times have I come for the Avatar in that time?”

Her eyes skip away, arms crossing in front of her, and Zuko is so full of anger over her denying him the words they both know that he doesn’t know if the crawling rage in his veins is him or his fire or both.

“You weren’t evening *hiding*,” he explodes. “You put up fucking *flyers,* you told *everyone* who you were. Do you know how fucking *easy*—” He cuts himself off again, heaving in a breath and grasping for a shred of calm. “I care,” he finally says, low, the words jagged in his throat, “About Sokka.”

It’s hard to say, hard to give up a piece of himself like that, here, now, in front of her, when none of those things allow him space for softness. Zuko’s never needed to voice it to Sokka before, and he hates her suddenly, deep and resentful and personal, for making him say it to her first. For hearing it and continuing to look at him like she doesn’t believe.

“If you really care,” Katara finally says, and oh, Zuko could burn down whole cities over that ‘if,’ “Then you should let him go.”

Zuko hisses between his teeth in surprise, immediately wary, tense for another attack and jittery when instead she settles back, still looking stiff and guarded but now marginally less ready for violence, which can only be another trap, which can only mean the blow is going to come another way and Zuko would really prefer to just see the fist when she swings it.

“How is this going to end, Zuko?” She continues, something that sounds like frustration tightening her words. “Not just this—” she waves a hand around the cave. “—but all of it? What are you going to do when Sokka leaves Ba Sing Se? Sokka’s trying to end the war. That can't be a secret. What are you doing?”

It’s Zuko’s turn to skip his gaze away, hands curling into fists at his sides and clutching at smoke as she cuts right to the heart of every unvoiced question Zuko's been agonizing over ever since the beginning, the ones he hasn’t been able to even look at let alone answer without needing to also stare down the end.

Apparently, all those weeks are catching up with Zuko now, all the ones he drifted through with the sense of not really being a part of the world. All that life Sokka was living, when Zuko was just existing in the timelessness of a Ba Sing Se teashop.

“You might say you’re not Fire Nation anymore.” Her tone adds a clear ‘for now.’ “But war and hatred are in your blood. You can't just walk away from that.”

“It’s not like I want them to be,” Zuko says, his inner flame flipping in frustration that he can’t deny it. Look at his family. Uncle is probably the best of them, and the Dragon of the West’s hands are stained with red.

“It doesn’t matter what you *want.* Not if it follows wherever you go,” Katara says, shaking her head, and Zuko wants to flinch from the immutable fate she lays out before him, from the inevitability of the destruction that’s followed in his wake his whole life. Everything he touches breaks, eventually, and Zuko feels another sharp stab of fear for Sokka. Agni, is Zuko breaking him too, by trying to hold on?

“Could you even?” She suddenly asks, and Zuko stares, uncomprehending.

“...What?” He feels like he's floundering, drowning with no water in sight, desperately trying to keep himself away from anything else that will force him to flay himself open and reveal how weak he is, when he desperately needs to be strong.

“Let him go. Are you even capable of it at this point? If it was to save him?”

Zuko…can’t think about that. He doesn't *want* to think about that, can’t barely even comprehend voluntarily letting go when all his life has been about trying to hold tight. He doesn’t know how to do that, wouldn’t know where to even start, and the idea of figuring it out is like a wild, clawing thing in his chest. “I wouldn’t try because *you* asked.”

Katara scowls, shaking her head and muttering something to herself that sounds like ‘the two of you…’ “You’re going to hurt him, you know.”

“I don’t want to.” Has never wanted to.

“But you will anyway if you keep going like this."

"You can't know that," he whispers, hating the absolute certainty ringing in her words.

The look she gives him is nearly pitying. "It’s what the Fire Nation *does.* And you’re their Prince.”

And Zuko knows all too well what the role of Fire Prince requires. He fixes his gaze over her shoulder, searching for words and finding nothing he could say. He can't exactly protest it. Zuko could never be a good enough liar.

Katara is clearly looking for a battle, though, eyes narrowing at his silence before poking with far less precision than Azula for something that will make him fight back. “You just take and take and take, just like all the rest of them, and you don’t care who gets hurt in the process—”

“That’s not true.” Zuko has never been able to not care, even when he should.

“—because you will never know what’s it’s like to lose someone to the Fire Nation—”

Zuko stares, his inner fire dropping back under the force of his numb surprise.

“—You will never know the pain of the Fire Nation taking everything away from you! Destroying your home and killing your mother and—”

“Sokka didn’t tell you?”

Katara stutters to a stop, glaring, uncertain. “What?”

Zuko’s inner fire pulls back toward his center, not entirely certain what to do with this, if this is just a game she’s playing. “That we have that, at least, in common.”

It’s Katara’s turn to stare, blankly uncomprehending. Or maybe disbelieving. Zuko’s lips twist into a humorless smile.

“Sokka never told you?” This…Zuko doesn't really know what to do with this. Zuko hadn’t really thought about it, had maybe just assumed…it was so early, when Sokka found out. And so much happened between then and now. “That’s how we started talking. About missing our moms.”

“…Your mom died?”

“My mom was killed.” Zuko knows that Katara will appreciate the distinction.

“By the…”

“Yes.” Zuko looks away from her dawning comprehension and something else that looks like pity, or maybe sympathy, or quiet horror. He doesn’t want any of them. Grief crosses all borders in war, but that doesn’t mean that Zuko's willing to hold all of his up for her to pick apart.

“I…didn’t know.”

Zuko shrugs. “I guess there’s no reason you would.” And there might be a statement in there somewhere, about how in other circumstances maybe Katara would have reason to know something so important to someone so close to her brother. About what this might mean for all the other pieces of himself that Sokka might have chosen to hold close. But Zuko doesnt have time to think about it now, doesn't bother trying to figure it out. These circumstances are all they have.

“I’m sorry,” he adds after an overlong silence, shifting under the awkward emptiness of the words, wondering if there’s even any use in saying them. “For what it’s worth.”

She eyes him, scowling in a way that Zuko of all people can recognize as habitual. “For what?”

“That it happened. To you both. That everything happened.” Agni, Zuko is sorry for more than he can ever make amends for.

Katara is silent for too many heartbeats for Zuko to count, face unreadable, before finally uncrossing her arms and glancing away with a sigh. “It’s not like you ordered it.”

“…Does that make anything better?”

“…No. Not really.”

Zuko shrugs, understanding. Some things don’t become better. They just become…there. Something you learn how to breathe around with enough time and distance.

The silence that falls between them finally holds, thank anything listening, because Zuko just…needs a moment. They’re each brooding, neither quite willing to take their eyes off the other, but slowly Zuko’s thoughts pull away from the immediacy of her presence and her anger and turn toward the nagging fears and worries he never should have let himself get distracted from in the first place.

Zuko watches her out of the corner of his unscarred eye, wondering if he can risk turning her back toward anger, if he should upset this fragile peace between them or just work with what he has. But he needs to know. And Katara has talked plenty, in the past, when Zuko needed her to, if he can just find the right way to get her going.

“Katara…” He waits for her to glance over at him, bracing himself. “Where’s Sokka?”

“Not in Ba Sing Se,” she sighs, glancing up toward the palace above them. Zuko already knows that, so he waits. “Sokka went to see our dad, to talk to him about the invasion.”

Zuko pounces, even as he takes a page out of Uncle’s book and tries to keep his voice as neutral and casual as he can make it. “An invasion?”

“Yeah, on the Day of the—” She snaps her head around, blue eyes going wide before narrowing into a glare. Shit. “You—! I’m not telling you *anything*.”

“I’m not—fuck, Katara, I’m not trying to—” Except he needs to cut himself off because he can’t say it convincingly. He *is* trying to get information from her, just not the way she thinks. He blows out his frustration, trying to hold onto some semblance of calm even as his heart starts buzzing at her confirmation. Fuck. Azula always lies, except when the truth hurts all on its own. “I just want to know that he’s okay.”

“Because you care?” She challenges, nearly mocking.

“*Yes*, because I care,” Zuko snaps, feeling smoke in the back of his throat. “Agni’s balls, Katara, why is it so hard for you to believe that someone would care about your bother?”

“It’s not *someone* I have an issue believing,” she says, all protective, defensive hostility that Zuko recognizes far too well. “It’s you.”

Zuko pinches the bridge of his nose, holding in a scream, because what is he supposed to *do* with that? “I would never hurt him if I could help it.”

“I guess the issue is whether you think you can help it or not,” she replies, tart, and it's such an infuriating little sister thing to say, in such a *tone*, but the words so much Sokka’s that Zuko can’t help the way it makes his heart flip.

“You sound like him,” he murmurs, a useless observation and he hates how that similarity has the power to make him feel so much fondness and warmth when he needs to be wary, to be ready, to be prepared to fight. Except Katara doesn’t seem to know what to say to that any more than Zuko knows why he said it, clamping her mouth shut and sitting back in confused, frowning, thinking silence. Zuko supposes that’s as good an outcome as any as he slowly feels himself beginning to unwind bit by bit into the quiet.

It’s hard to track the passage of time so far from Agni’s light, and he can't exactly rely on counting the beats of his always tripping heart, so Zuko doesn’t know exactly how much time has passed when Katara suddenly speaks, her words so soft they barely reach him. “Have you really changed that much?”

“Huh?”

“Would you really put it all behind you?” She studies him, brow tense, none of her earlier hostility in the look she gives him now. “Being a Prince and the Fire Nation and everything? Just—what, for him?”

Zuko stares, feeling beyond helpless as he searches for words. Agni, he wants it to be that easy. He would give so many things for it to be that easy. But how could he just walk away from parts of himself like that, parts that are built so deep into the core of who he is that he hasn’t known what there is left of himself without them? How could he do it without always seeing what he left behind?

Zuko isn’t a collection of personalities and traits that can be stripped away and traded in and out to suit the audience and the circumstance, even if Uncle and sometimes Sokka and really most everyone else seems to act like he is. He’s just one currently-imprisoned person. “I would give up a lot, for him.”

“But not that?”

Zuko wants to be able to spark with anger, with outrage, but he just feels…exhausted. “Katara, I don’t know what you want me to say. It’s not like he’s asked.” But that feels uncomfortable on his tongue, because Zuko knows that Sokka *would* have asked, if he knew. And that soon Zuko will be making a choice that could be for both of them, that with Azula here it might happen before Zuko can give Sokka the chance *to* ask, because Azula wasn't exactly wrong, when she said that Zuko can learn from her example when it comes to refusing to accept what the world would give him. But Zuko knows you only get so many chances to reach for what you want to have, isntead.

Katara suddenly makes a frustrated noise, scrubbing her hands over her face. “Sorry,” she mutters, the words so wholly unexpected that Zuko briefly wonders if he's feeling the delayed onset of a blow to the head. “I’m sorry. I shouldn’t—I’m just—worried, and stressed, and— fuck.”

Zuko eyes her, wary and entirely unclear on what he’s supposed to do with those words. He doesn’t get apologies. Only from Sokka, really, and Zuko can’t exactly respond the same with her as he would with her brother.

“Sokka wouldn’t want me to be…” She exhales hard, bracing herself. “I know you make him happy,” she says, and now Zuko *really* doesn’t know what to do with that, particularly when she sounds like she's being slightly strangled by the words. “I just can’t help thinking that this thing you guys are trying to do is foolish, the whole way you’re going about it.”

Zuko lets out a bark of surprised, humorless laughter. “Probably.” He’s nothing if not a fool according to the people who’ve known him longest.

They fall into silence again, a tenuous peace that feels like it could shift back to animosity at any moment, the thin thread of Sokka’s wants all that’s holding them in balance. Zuko wants to sit, to rest, to prepare, but he can’t make a move until Katara eventually slides down a stalagmite, sighing and seeming to give up on bracing herself for something that might not come.

Zuko can let him loosen then, just a bit, taking his own seat across from her, making sure she’s on his right side because she’s still closer than he’s completely comfortable with even without water nearby. Close enough that he can see her shiver, intermittently, in what he belatedly realizes is a damp chill. He bites his lip, wavering. It would be a…nice…thing, to help where he can. Right? And…it might dry the air out some, too, which might make no difference to her bending, but he thinks would help his still-racing heart.

“You’re cold?”

She glares over her bent knees.

“Can I..?” Zuko deliberately and slowly raises his hands, extending out a slow cone of heat, gesturing huge to signal what’s happening, to give her a chance to say no. She stiffens when teh edge of it reaches her, startled and tense before realizing that warmth is all there is, not the fire. He can see her visibly debating before she finally sags into the heat, nodding, accepting what he’s offering. He lets out a breath, relieved in a way he doesn’t wholly understand, and sends out warmth in a careful radius around her, concentrating on holding the neat edges of the circle he's forming and ignoring her pensive stare. He’s used to those, even if they tend to be a bit less thoughtful.

“I used to have nightmares about you, you know.”

Zuko blinks in surprise, wondering if he misheard. “Uh—what?”

“I sometimes still do. The whole—” she gestures toward her head, and Zuko nearly loses his hold over the heat as his inner fire contracts. “—thing, with the ponytail and glaring and whatnot. I pictured you whenever I thought about the enemy.”

Zuko holds in his flinch through years of practice, turning his left side away from her like it doesn’t matter. The sudden attack took him dangerous unawares, the mildness of her tone and the harshness of the words jarring and unexpected. Stupid. Foolish of him to think that the tentative bridge they’d build between them meant anything to her, that her being willing to tolerate his bending actually meant anything.

“It was like you crashed in with your ship and brought the war back to our home.”

“The war never left,” Zuko grinds out, voice brittle, refusing to rise to her bait because he knows all about feigned-innocence, all about being goaded into the first visible violence.

“No," she says after a moment, "I guess not.”

Zuko doesn’t bother trying to come up with a reply, grimly trying to find that quiet space again where he could loosen enough to think. It wasn’t exactly comfortable, with Katara in it, but it was tolerable, and he needs that again, needs to be thinking of Azula, of the Fire Nation in Ba Sing Se, of Sokka. Not about this, not about the stab of shocked pain that it’s his own fault for not seeing coming.

He can’t relax, though, not even the little bit he’d managed before, every inch of his skin tingling with hyperawareness that she’s staring. Zuko can always tell when people are staring at his scar. He knows exactly the kind of look on their faces when they try to be subtle, when they try to be unimpressed, when they gawp outright. She isn’t trying to hide it, at least. Which means she’s probably working her way up to the inevitable question.

“Does it hurt?” Her voice is quiet, thoughtful, not at all the question Zuko expected.

He risks a sideways glance, considers but doesn’t bother pretending he doesn’t know what she’s talking about. Better to get this over with. “Not usually.”

She frowns, leaning like she’s trying to get a better look in what little light they have. “Can you see and hear on that side?”

Zuko eyes her with significantly more wariness. “Um.” He doesn’t exactly trust her with that information, especially not if Sokka kept it from her. Sokka might have just been respecting Zuko’s privacy, but Zuko isn’t about to take chances that there was a larger reason behind his silence.

“I have this special water,” Katara suddenly says, and Zuko wonders if she’s about to suggest they get drunk down here.

“Okay…”

“It’s from the Spirit Oasis.”

Zuko barely hides a whole-body flinch. Not drunk, then. Or at least not off alcohol.

“It has special properties, because of…” She trails off, clearly thinking out loud, a furrow of concentration on her brow as she stares at his face, which would be unsettling all on its own, even if it didn’t make her look suddenly so much like Sokka. “I might be able to heal it.”

Zuko flinches for real, at that. “I don’t—” want? need? “—deserve that.” He couldn’t take something like that from her. Not when he doesn't understand why she'd offer it on the heels of an attack. Not when he has nothing to give in return. Not for something that he’s long resigned himself to. And especially not when he’s about to—

“Sometimes,” Katara says, gaze cutting away, tone careful in that way of someone pretending they aren’t invested in their own words. “It’s hard to see what you deserve when you’ve been told for so long to settle for what people decide to give you.”

Zuko shoots her a quick, hard look. But Katara doesn’t look knowing, or taunting. She just sits quietly, hands folded loosely in her lap, waiting for him to react. Which Zuko would, if he knew what to do. Except he doesn’t, so he does nothing, and after an endless minute she leans forward onto her knees, moving just as slow as he did with his firebending, giving him time to stop it or pull back as she reaches out to touch his scar.

Her touch is so light that Zuko can barely feel it against the thick skin, but it still makes him tense, uneasy even as he allows the contact. It’s uncomfortably familiar and strange for her to do this thing that Sokka does so often, while wearing a face almost like his but with none of Sokka’s affection behind it.

“Zuko,” she begins with a deep breath, and the wall shatters.

The air is suddenly an explosion of dust and shards of rock, crystal fragments sharp as glass flying across the cave. Zuko and Katara both throw themselves down, hiding their faces until the debris stops falling. Zuko can feel bright points of pain down the back of his neck, over his hand, as chips of crystal slice against him. He surges to his feet the second it feels marginally safe, calling fire to his hands and narrowing his unscarred eye against the grit in the air, tense for an attack and the Dai Li and—

“Uncle?”

Zuko actually extinguishes one hand to rub at his good eye, like maybe the dust in the air is making him hallucinate. But it’s still Uncle, somehow here, still in his tea-serving robes and hurrying across the uneven ground, looking dirty but unharmed, face urgent as he looks Zuko over for injury.

“Zuko!” Uncle catches him into a hug, hauling Zuko in tight against his heat and bulk. It’s so unexpected that Zuko can only make a little gurgling noise of surprise, managing to extinguish his other hand before he lights Uncle’s robe on fire.

As the dust settles Zuko registers another body over Uncle’s shoulder, one that isn’t Katara, one that makes his hands nearly catch fire again. Sloppy, to notice so late. He let Azula get into his head and now he’s getting sloppy.

Zuko stiffens, half-bent over in Uncle’s embrace still as the Avatar steps forward, every instinct he has screaming at him to get his hands free, to get himself in position to fight. Zuko glares, automatic as his heart begins to race, and the Avatar scowls back before hurrying to Katara’s side. Not here for Zuko, which makes sense, but somehow with Uncle, which— Zuko wants to scream, grinding his teeth and clenching his jaw because what the actual *fuck*. Zuko is trying *so hard* to do the right thing here, just to keep getting this fucking mockery of a destiny thrown back into his face.

Uncle steps back at Zuko’s tension, following his gaze to where Katara and the Avatar are reuniting. “There is no time for old rivalries,” he chides, loud enough for all of them but looking at Zuko. Like it was ever a fucking *rivalry.* “Master Aang, Master Katara—you need to help the others.”

The Avatar jerks like he’s suddenly remembering, facing moving from relief back into firm purpose. “Right.”

“What? What’s happening?” Katara asks, blinking at the Avatar’s back as he takes off back the way they came. She hesitates, giving Zuko a quick, half-apologetic shrug before rushing after him.

“The others?” Zuko echoes, frowning into the dark tunnel they just disappeared back into. What’s going on? Who else needs help, and why would Uncle send them off instead of helping, or hustling Zuko along with them?

“Nephew—”

“What others?”

“Zuko…” Uncle reaches out and Zuko takes a careful, precise step back, his inner fire shuddering back to readiness.

“What. Others.”

“Nephew,” Uncle says again, low and urgent, trying to close the space between them, face twisting in something like pain when Zuko falls back ahead of him again. “Zuko. You are a changed man. You are stronger and wiser than you were before. You have more *choices* now than you did before. It is time for you to choose the path of good.”

“*What others?”*

There’s a single, deliberate crunch of boots on stone, and then blades of green crystal explode from the ground, jagged prison bars forming around Uncle in the space of a thought, immobilizing him as Zuko stumbles back, just barely managing to keep his balance as the uneven floor ripples beneath him.

“I think you know exactly which others.”

Zuko whirls to see Azula standing in the opening the Avatar had blown in the wall, the Dai Li at her back.

“Curious, though, isn’t it?” She raises one perfect eyebrow. “That he doesn’t want to tell you.”

Zuko’s heart starts pounding so hard it feels like the inside of his chest is bruising, caught between shock at Uncle’s sudden capture and panic over why ‘the others’ would need help. He knows exactly who they are, much as he doesn’t want it to be true, much as he doesn’t understand why Uncle won’t confirm it, but if Azula is here and Sokka isn’t—

“Maybe he was scared to test your loyalties, hm? Don’t worry, Brother.” Her smile is all teeth. “I’m not afraid.”

“Azula, what—”

“Get your mind out of your pants for one second, Zuzu,” she cuts in, face going abruptly flat as she tsks at him. “You always were excitable, but you never used to be so *hormonal*.” Her voice turns hard with annoyance. “Stop being distracted and see. The big. Picture.”

Zuko shuts up and waits for her to show it to him, then, since she clearly wants to, keeping a wary eye on the Dai Li, trying to keep a corner of his vision on Uncle, refusing to lose sight of Azula. There are too many threats in the room, even with his fire sense to try to keep track of bodies. And they’re spread out too wide to possibly see them all when he needs to keep Azula squarely on his right side. Which she would know.

“This is the most glorious day in Fire Nation history, Brother,” she says, a little smile on her lips. “The Avatar and Ba Sing Se captured, all at once, all without sacrificing a life.”

“A Fire Nation life,” Zuko corrects softly. There are only three Fire Nation citizens here— five? Mai and Ty Lee must be around. Though maybe still three. Zuko doesn’t know if he and Uncle count anymore. It’s easy to make sweeping statements when you ignore the qualifiers.

Azula just shrugs, flicking his words away like a particularly annoying bug. “If the Earth Kingdom puts up a fight. Sure.” As if they wouldn’t, as if they would have brought it on themselves by doing so. Zuko knows exactly how this game works.

“You haven’t captured the Avatar yet,” he points out, deciding to get away from the subject of pending battle, because Azula wouldn’t be here with Zuko if she had Aang, which means there's something she wants him to do, something he needs to figure out before she leads him into it.

“You’re right.” She says easily, smiling, pleased, like he finally noticed a surprise she’d organized just for him. Dread sweeps up his spine. “I wanted to give you a chance, after all.”

“…For what.” Zuko knows plenty about chances, after the last few months. He doesn’t know if he has the willpower to make it through any more fresh starts or second chances. He doesn’t know if he has the choice.

“At redemption, Brother.” She says the word slow, like she’s savoring the taste of it, tawny eyes intent on his reaction. “Join me, Zuzu, and you can gain back Father’s love.” She smiles as she plays her trump card. “You can regain your place. Your honor.”

“Nephew,” Uncle cuts in, pleading, voice nakedly desperate in a way that makes Zuko want to scream. “Do not listen! What your sister offers is not the kind of redemption that you need!”

Zuko exhales slow and hard, smoke sliding between his teeth, refusing to look away from Azula. She smirks, able to read him as well as always. Her expression says that she knows him still, that she knows him best, and Zuko is afraid that she isn’t wrong. That after nearly four years apart, Azula can still pick him apart better than anyone. That after nearly four years together, Uncle still doesn’t understand, because what *redemptions* does Iroh think Zuko *needs*. What new destiny does he have set out for Zuko? What new plan to move Zuko like pai sho tile wherever it’s most convenient?

Ba Sing Se tea servers don’t need *redemption*, so what have the past months fucking been *about.*

“I have it all planned other, Brother. You know I do.” Her expression is as gentle as it can be while still being hers. “All the way to the end. I can do it without you, of course. But it’s better if you join me.”

“Zuko,” Uncle begs, and Zuko reluctantly glances toward him, lightning-quick before finding Azula again because he isn’t so foolish to let her out of his sight when he can help it. “Look deep inside your heart, Nephew. See what you truly want!”

Zuko nearly laughs, at that, something nothing like humor bubbling up, trying to claw up his throat. As if Zuko didn’t already do that days ago, writhing in the grip of fever. As if Zuko doesn’t already know exactly what he wants, hasn’t already resigned himself to it. As if he isn’t already fully aware that Uncle won’t be happy with it.

Which makes something in him feel fragile and dangerously thin, but still isn’t enough reason to look again and reconsider.

Zuko studies Azula carefully, looking for the trap, taking the time she's giving him to step back through her words. He can pick out the lies, but parsing the truth underneath is harder. And she’s smart, to dangle those things in front of him. She always did know what made him tick. And it makes him fear, again, for Sokka. Not that Zuko ever stopped fearing for him and flinching from the idea of Azula and Sokka occupying the same space. Because Zuko knows her, too, and Azula was always more than willing to break her own toys to keep others from having them.

“Decide what you want, Zuko,” Azula finally says into the silence, giving him a disdainful look as she sends the Dai Li away with a lazy flick of her hand. “But make a decision. It’s time to choose.”

Azula walks away with that, unhurried, strolling toward her victory in composed silence except for the crisp sound of boots on stone, leaving Iroh trapped and Zuko immobilized by uncertainty behind her.

Iroh is still talking, repeating himself—which Zuko *hates*—urging Zuko to look inside himself, to read his own heart, to see the good inside, to see what he truly wants. As if Iroh somehow still has no idea that the core of Zuko’s heart beats to the wild rhythm of Sokka’s inner flame and the soft rustle of tea leaves in the morning and the even drum of breath and fire moving in total harmony. As if Iroh somehow thinks that Zuko’s most desperate want could be anything other than to sit at the turtle duck pond with Sokka at his side and the sun on his skin and the knowledge that all the people he holds dear are safe.

Azula knows it, even if Iroh doesn’t. It’s a dangerous want, left only in her hands.

Zuko spits a tight curse and presses the heels of his hands to his temples. He squeezes his eyes closed and shuts out Iroh’s pleading and tries to *think*, for once in his life, of what comes next in all the plans suddenly in motion around him instead of just within his own.
