## Chapter 33: Brave Enough to Burn Bridges

### Notes

#### Chapter Notes

Warnings for canon typical violence in this one

(Guys I forgot what day of the week it is and almost didn't post, man wouldn't that have sucked haha)

### Text

Zuko follows the sound of battle deeper in the caves, trailing after the Avatar and Azula and isn’t that just a perfect little summary for his entire fucking life. His fire sense rolls out before him, seeking hidden enemies, brushing up against firebender-controlled flames that he isn’t going to waste energy trying to wrest from Azula’s control.

Zuko doesn’t know if it’s a good or a bad thing that he can’t feel Sokka’s familiar heat, and he doesn’t have time to figure it out. He bursts into another—wetter, shit*—*cave just in time to see the Avatar and Katara corner Azula, perfectly flanking her to trap her in one of the huge cavern's few tight corners.

Zuko reacts on instinct, his fire already open wide for a strike that redirects Katara’s water whip to cut shards off the wall instead of Azula’s face. There’s a moment of tight, fraught silence, all of them staring at him in varying degrees of shock. Then Azula smiles, full of teeth, and Zuko has a single moment to think *oh, fuck* while staring down her savage delight before the battle roars back to life with Zuko at his sister’s side.

Zuko doesn’t have time to think anything then, his world narrowing down to the fight around him. His body remembers the rhythms of battling the Avatar even if he's months out of practice. The Avatar’s waterbending is better than before, and the earthbending is new, but Zuko's been fighting Dai Li on their own turf. He knows how to counter earth even if it’s a scramble to adapt to earth blended with water and air.

Zuko keeps a portion of his attention on the other struggle underway, as much as he can risk, looking for an opportunity and seizing the chance when it finally comes to switch off with Azula and face Katara himself. He doesn’t trust her with Sokka’s little sister, even though tactically Azula might be the better match. The mere sight of him seems to feed new rage and focus into Katara’s attacks.

Azula and the Avatar flip and leap and dive around the cavern, but Zuko doesn't have Azula's precision, or Katara the Avatar's light-footedness. Instead, they square up on opposite sides of the underground river, because of course Zuko's luck would find him in an underground battle with a waterbender and still be next to a continually replenishing body of water. Of course. They exchange attacks and blocks, back and forth, nearly rhythmic except for the ferocity of it, fire and water and ice, and beneath it all, heat. Zuko draws on his heat to steam away Katara’s attacks so they never fully land, to melt her ice before it reaches him so it’s never truly razor-sharp. He makes her element waver in her grip, on the verge of evaporating, forcing her to draw on new reserves and new focus to keep her water from misting away. It’s not something he’s ever done in combat before, but Zuko’s spent far too long in teashops not to know how to heat water to his needs.

He fights with grim resolve, tight control, measured purpose. Katara rages, fury adding power to her attacks and unpredictability to her strikes. Zuko focuses on his breath control and ignores the part of him that clamors to rage back.

“I should have known better than to ever trust someone like you.” Katara spits the words across the water along with two fistfuls of ice daggers. “You’re good for nothing.” A sudden sheet of ice beneath his feet. “Just a betrayer." A water whip. “A liar.” Discs of ice flying off her foot. “You *disgust* me.”

She falls back then as Zuko snaps a crackling rope of fire her way, her face twisted with hatred as the steam of her block clears. “I’m glad that Sokka isn’t here to see this.” Her hands snap down, open-palmed, gathering more water. “I *never* want him to find out what you really are.”

Zuko’s breath slips a little, at that, inner flame flaring out before he can pull it back under control, and he needs to twist out of the way of her next attack as it breaks through the edge of his defenses. Sloppy.

“How could you—with—he thought you *changed*.”

“I *have* changed,” Zuko grinds out, bracing himself against her next attack, watching her face as it tenses in confusion now as well as anger. She hesitates a single heartbeat, water in her hands, and he presses the opportunity. “You should ask Sokka about how I play pai sho.” Zuko slides sideways as her anger visibly wins out again at hearing him speak, a sloppy ball of ice exploding somewhere behind him. “Ask him what a world with hope in it looks like.”

Katara glares, whatever response she might have made lost as the Avatar suddenly goes flying across the cavern in a roar of flames. Both of them instinctively jerk backward, Zuko turning it into a hasty full retreat as Katara's face twists, as the entire river seems to shiver before she opens her mouth and screams out her rage. The noise sounds like it's coming from so deep inside her that Zuko’s own gut throbs in sympathy before she unleashes herself on both siblings.

Zuko throws himself into formation with Azula, doing his best to position himself in the right spot relative to her constant flipping and jumping and pirouetting, to maintain the consistent heat of his flames, to resist as he's been resisting this whole time the frantic urge to reach with his fire sense for Sokka and assure himself that he’s okay when Zuko doesn’t even know where he is and certainly can’t afford the distraction of looking.

Katara is majestic in her fury and a force of nature with her element at her feet, but she’s fighting on two fronts—Azula really did plan this all out, apparently—and it feels almost inevitable that eventually Azula sends her crashing down in a truly masterful display of precision bending. Zuko’s heart stutters, his flames guttering for a breath, eyes fixed on Katara even as he throws himself clear of a sheet of rock as the Avatar hurls himself back into the fight. Katara’s chest moves, then she coughs, whole body hitching before she rolls to her knees, wrapping tentacles of water around herself with the motion, and Zuko’s heart is sprinting to catch up to where it’s supposed to be as fire and water clash again, this time with no room for words between them.

Flames and water and ice and earth and air and heat fill the cavern until it feels like they’re somehow at an impasse, the four of them inexplicably matched. Zuko wonders how long this can possibly go on for, a crazed part of his mind wondering if they'll still be locked in battle in a hundred years like some Spirit tale, still perfectly matched, when a shudder goes through the stone floor that did *not* come from the Avatar.

Fuck. Zuko spins away, opening his line of sight as the Dai Li flow into the room, perfectly synchronized and choreographed, hands raised in threat, robes flaring and dramatic behind them and Zuko can see in that moment why Azula would have been inclined to take control of themi. She always did have an appreciation for the power of pageantry. And she really did think of everything, didn't she.

Katara takes a quick, instinctive glance toward the new threat, so fast that it doesn't even last a heartbeat, but Zuko knows what's coming the moment he sees it, his body tensing in anticipation a breath before Azula seizes on that hint of a distraction to lance a fireball toward Katara, huge and hot and savage in a way that makes it clear she’s been feinting the whole time up until now, holding back for a moment just like this.

The blow catches Katara square across the body and sending her skidding and tumbling across the cavern floor. Aang shouts in alarm, leaping away from the Dai Li and toward Katara who isn’t moving, who isn’t getting up, shit, shit, *shit*. The Avatar falls into a defensive flurry, renewed power behind his blows that send Zuko and Azula and the Dai Li all dodging behind stone and blocks and each other. It's chaotic and dangerously uncoordinated, and between bodies and attacks and blocks, Zuko just manages to catch sight of Katara shoving herself to her forearms, his feet slowing just a bit as a dangerous pulse of relief threads through his inner flame.

That moment of distraction, of losing just a hint of his edge, is just enough for Zuko to suddenly lose the rhythm of the movement around him, to suddenly not know where to put himself in this fight. He doesn’t know where to be so that he can see the Avatar and Katara and not have the Dai Li at his back and not lose track of Azula in the chaos, can't see a place in the flurry of bodies and elements to get his back to a wall, isn't sure who he’s going to need to wield his flames against between one breath and the next.

Azula has no such hesitations. Even as Katara finds her feet and begins to weave her waterbending back in with Aang’s defenses, the tide is turning. Zuko can feel it in the extra spark on his fingers and in the thrum in his blood and in the quickening of Azula's steps. He can see it in the tightness on Katara’s face, in the renewed intensity of Azula’s blue flames. And Aang—the Avatar is stepping back, looking serious, sad, resigned, as he suddenly raises a protective cocoon of crystal around himself, a move that would be a retreat on anyone else but that sends a bolt of pure fear through Zuko's core.

Agni’s balls, Zuko can only guess at what glowing madness is about to come out of that.

Zuko scrambles backward, looking for the spots in the cavern least likely to cave in under a sudden onslaught of elements, frantically checking for Azula as he goes. He breathes a sigh of relief when he sees that she’s also hugging a wall, two fingers raised on the verge of a familiar pose, strands of hair beginning to almost lift around her face from the force she’s containing. But still she holds back, letting the Dai Li exhaust Katara for now, waiting for her moment to strike.

Azula might not have time to wait, though. Zuko's heart is beating so fast in his throat he can barely breathe around it—dangerous, dangerous—as the Avatar’s crystal shell begins to glow with an unmistakable light, brighter and brighter until it’s too much to look at, a pillar of white that washes out the greenlit cavern until Zuko can barely see, can barely hear over the sound of drowning screams and rending metal, can barely feel anything against his fire sense except the blazing pillar. He feels it in his bones as the Avatar suddenly rises into the air, Zuko's whole body vibrating at a frequency far too low for comfort as the force of it shoves everyone back. The Avatar's tattoos are glowing, his face blank, nothing in his eyes but white, inhuman, inhumane, ready to—

Zuko feels the spark of lightning in the air a bare second before it arcs, the potential suddenly coalescing into a perfect line from Azula’s fingertips to the Avatar’s spine. He knows it must be happening faster than thought, almost faster than sight, but it feels like Zuko is seeing the world in slow motion as Aang arches, freezes, spasms. For a second Zuko thinks that the Avatar will know what to do, that in two thousand years of lifetimes, someone would have learned the trick of letting lighting play along your bones and in your blood like it was always meant to be there. But Aang stutters instead, gasping, falling as the piercing brightness collapses back into his small form like all the air suddenly leaving the room, and Zuko can only think *oh, Azula really did have it all worked out* as his inner flame goes small, tight, cold.

Zuko did his best to think through every plan he could. He really did. He still didn’t expect this.

Katara *howls*, ripping a wall of water from the river to scatter them all back, face ferocious as she launches another tidal wave right after. It’s wild, uncontrolled, foolish to be wasting her element across the porous stone, and it sweeps the Dai Li off their feet, slams bodies into unforgiving rock with crushing force, even the earthbenders unable to cushion the blow. Zuko clings to his spot on the wall, nails biting into and breaking against stone, hiding his face from the water, gasping in the pockets of air between waves—he knows what to do after so much dreaming—until finally he can find his feet again. Zuko has no idea what to do when he gets there, though. He feels dangerously numb, even as he registers the fire suddenly rushing toward him, furious and biting even through Zuko’s instinctive block. But the flames are orange, not blue, which—which means—

Iroh scatters what remains of the Dai Li with brutal efficiency, taking up a defensive stance in front of Katara and a limp, unconscious, unresponsive Aang. He’s urging her to go, defending their retreat, the Dragon of the West unleashed like Ba Sing Se hasn’t seen in six years. Like it maybe never saw, except once before.

Zuko doesn’t even try to fight, just stays where he is, ready to defend and watching Katara carry Aang away and thinking that this is why he doesn’t let himself look too far ahead, because there's nothing to stop your plan going to ashes before it even begins.

&#45;-

Azula doesn’t try to follow the Avatar either. She stares Iroh down, impassive and unimpressed, before gesturing to the Dai Li. The agents are quick to imprison him again with bars of crystal and cuffs of stone and gags of rock. They’re not taking chances, this time.

“You’re letting them go,” Zuko says through numb lips, distantly shocked by the calm in his voice.

Azula rolls her eyes. “I don’t need a body, Zuzu.”

Zuko flicks his eyes toward her, pausing, and her finger twitches in annoyance. It would be better if there were a body, for what needs to come next. They both know it. Even if it’s easier this way, maybe, than having to transport one back to the Fire Nation. Zuko wouldn’t bet on that being Azula’s reasoning, though. She was always too coldly practical to let things like messiness hold her back.

Azula turns to the Dai Li, snapping out orders and receiving reports, not entirely dismissing him but clearly taking charge of the room. Zuko could go to her side, stand at her shoulder, absorb some of her authority through proximity. Begin to retake his place, maybe. But he stays where he is, looking toward Uncle.

Iroh’s yellow eyes are hard, staring, as if he’s been waiting for Zuko’s attention solely for the opportunity to deliberately turn his head away, the only gesture he has the freedom to make. It cuts, the look of disgust and shame on his face. But Zuko can take it. After all, Uncle was the one to teach Zuko how to push through pain. How to seize onto every motivation possible to keep going when it seems like there is nothing else. And Zuko is willing to push through absolutely anything, for this.

&#45;-

Sokka is trying to hustle Kuei and his bear through the maze of palace halls, ignoring how much the thing still creeps him out and trying to focus on their surroundings. He wholly doesn’t trust that the chirpy girl and the knife-y one—Ty-something and Maya? Zuko knew them—won’t be coming after them.

“Hold up,” Toph orders, slowing to a jog and nearly taking out the bear with her sudden deceleration. “Someone’s coming.”

Sokka grunts, flexing his hands, getting ready for a fight. They have momentum on their side, and maybe surprise, even if they’re closing distance so fast that they won’t have a lot of time to—

“It’s Katara!”

Sokka gasps in relief, steps stuttering, then freezing entirely as his sister barrels around the corner. Her hair is loose, clothes torn, battered and bleeding and that would be bad enough but Aang—Aang looks like nothing more than deadweight in her arms.

“*Sokka*,” she cries, desperate and distraught and for a moment he’s back on the ice, back in that raid. “Aang—”

“Give him here. We need to run.” He grabs the body, which is warm but limp, so limp, fuck, what *happened*. He focuses on that warmth with everything he has and refuses to do the mental calculations on how long it would take a living being to start to go noticeably cool. “Toph, get us out of here.”

“I know a shortcut,” Kuei offers, hands fluttering from his robes, and Sokka jerks his head in acknowledgment. They take off, sprinting through the eerily empty halls, Sokka’s neck itching with every step as he waits for the Dai Li to show up, for Azula to make an appearance, for something to try to stop them. He focuses on running, trying to shove down his fear at Aang’s continued unresponsiveness. Sokka has the airbender thrown over his shoulder, not as gentle as he could be and not the tightest hold so Sokka can still freely run, and that has to be the reason Sokka can’t feel Aang’s chest moving.

But with fear for Aang pushed deep, other worry bubbles up, the same persistent worry that’s been at the back of Sokka’s mind—when it wasn’t very loudly at the forefront—ever since Toph first ushered Iroh inside. Sokka keeps looking around, counting heads, checking down corridors, listening for other pounding steps, shooting anxious glances at Katara’s back until finally the words spill out. “Where’s Zuko.”

Katara doesn’t look back, the words tossed back over her shoulder between panting breaths, “He isn’t coming.”

Only momentum keeps him running, for a dangerous number of steps. “What does that mean?”

Katara glances back as she grabs onto a corner to throw herself into a new corridor at Kuei’s direction. “Turned out he didn’t need to be rescued.”

Sokka settles at that, relief hitting him so sudden and hard that for a moment he really can’t afford he feels like he might cry from it. But Zuko got himself out, which Sokka should have known he would be able to, and Iroh isn’t here either, and the General is more than capable of escaping with Zuko, especially if Iroh ended up not needing Katara’s help to free him.

They burst through a modest set of doors into the broad courtyard at the front of the palace. Appa is there already somehow, waiting, and they sprint across the still miraculously enemy-free space. They scramble up onto Appa’s back, even the fucking bear. Spirits, this is ridiculous. They can’t afford the weight, but who’s going to suggest leaving him behind? They’d have to leave Kuei too, and Sokka doesn’t know if that would make whatever Azula is doing worse, but it certainly won’t make it better.

Appa lurches into the sky as Sokka sets Aang down as gently as he can, trying to project calm as Katara skids over. She fumbles for the vial of Spirit Oasis water that she always keeps on her and fuck, fuck, *fuck*, if she needs that. Fuck.

The water glows blue between her hands, over and over and over, but Aang doesn’t move, doesn’t react, doesn’t *anything*. The water isn’t settling on his skin like Sokka is used to seeing when Katara heals and fuck, *fuck*, what *happened* down there? The wound on his back is raw, charred, but it doesn’t look like it came from fire. From—from lightning? Sokka stares at the scorched, ragged edges and remembers Zuko’s joy in the storm and feels like he’s going to be sick.

Aang suddenly shudders, tattoos gently glowing as they leech the brightness out of the healing water in a swift flow of energy that has Sokka’s stomach lurching in remembered horror. Sokka reaches a protective hand toward Katara to do—he doesn’t know what, *something*, but the glow fades before he can touch her, Aang’s tattoos dimming back to their normal inked-on blue. Aang's eyes slit open for less than a breath, unfocused and dazed and clearly not even close to conscious as his chest rises the barest inch, falls, rises, falls, and it’s barely anything at all, but it’s not *nothing.*

Toph slumps onto her back, covering her face with her hands, and Sokka folds forward in relief. Katara just straightens, scrambling for more water, movements sharp with purpose now, focused in a way that gives Sokka space to be a little less calm. He glances down over the edge of Appa’s saddle, an automatic check for landmarks to bump up against his mental map. That’s the Outer Wall, moving behind them so they must be going west, toward Chameleon Bay back toward the fleet, maybe, and—

“Wait.” Sokka jerks upright, getting halfway there before his bruises protest and seize. “Zuko.” Sokka never told him—he might be free but he wouldn't know where to *go.*

But Katara just twitches, bending her head more tightly over Aang, jaw tight, and Sokka stares, a feeling like ice sliding down his spine, cold and shocking and sharp enough to draw blood.

“Katara. Where's Zuko.”

“And this is how the Earth Kingdom falls to the Fire Nation,” Kuei murmurs, like he was just waiting for someone else to signal permission to speak. “With barely a whisper in the night.”

How the Earth Kingdom *falls* to the— “Katara,” Sokka says, voice hoarse and overly loud, something frantic beginning to crash around his ribcage. “*Where is Zuko*.”

“He sided with Azula,” she whispers, harsh and low and Sokka doesn’t—he doesn’t understand.

“What? He—what?”

“He fought on her side,” Katara says, a little louder, just as tight.

“No,” Sokka says, shaking his head, sliding along the saddle away from her words. “He wouldn’t. He—There has to be something else—”

“I was there,” Katara says, words suddenly hollow as she pulls Aang in a little tighter. “I know what I saw.”

“Well maybe you didn’t see it right! What happened? Maybe you didn’t—maybe you just didn’t understand.” This is—it doesn’t make sense, it doesn’t make any *sense*. Azula *captured* him, why would Zuko—what would make him—but why would Katara just—

“He fought against Aang and me,” Katara snaps, eyes flashing, hands tightening into fists, and some small voice in Sokka’s head points out that they’re both afraid and both letting that fear become anger, and he ruthlessly strangles it into silence. He doesn’t have time to listen to that crap right now. “What more do you need to know?”

“But what *happened*? What did he say? What—was Iroh okay?” He needs to know *everything*, every word, every glance, everyone in the room. Fuck, Zuko speaks with his body and his actions and reactions more than his words. Katara won’t know how to read that, which means she doesn’t know what she saw, so she *can’t* be right—

Toph can’t read heartbeats on Appa’s back, not without earth. Sokka isn’t sure if that’s a good thing or if it’s only letting him spiral deeper.

“Iroh got captured,” Katara says. “After Aang had already—” She cuts herself off, marshaling herself to speak again and Sokka barely resists the clawing need to grab her by the shoulders and shake the answers out of her. “Zuko didn’t say anything worth hearing.”

“But he said something,” Sokka says—demands—leaping for anything that might make what she’s saying make sense.

“Why does it *matter* the exact way he—”

“*Tell me.”*

Katara shakes her head like he’s bringing it on himself before finally relenting. “Just some shit about pai sho.”

“What,” Sokka demands, his heart leaping up into his throat, his mind already racing. Zuko and pai sho—Sokka needs a bit more, but he can—he can make something of this. He can figure this out. Sokka’s spent so much time thinking about Zuko and what he does and why, he just needs more information because none of this *fits*.

“It was just stupid taunts, Sokka,” Katara sighs, finally meeting his eyes, flinching away from whatever is on his face. “Why do you want to hear it? Why do you want to do this to yourself?”

“Because I need to know!” As if she doesn’t know exactly why. As if they all don’t know. Fucking *Bosco* probably knows.

“Fine, make it worse for yourself,” she mutters, turning back to Aang. “We had this whole— conversation, or whatever. And he seemed so…Spirits, for a second it was like I got it, you know? I saw what you—but then he just…did that. Sided with her. And he taunted that I should ask you about how he does pai sho or something. That I should ask you what hope looks like.” She practically spits the words.

For a moment Sokka can only stare, uncomprehending. Then the words slowly attach themselves to memories, memories of *his own fucking words. O*f *himself* spouting some shit about hope and change*,* and something like a scream rises in his chest. It bursts out as a laugh, an uncontrollable, hysterical, terrified laugh that he can’t quiet and can’t stop, even as Toph sits up in alarm and Kuei scoots away and Katara momentarily loses the blue glow of her water.

“You idiot,” Sokka manages to choke out, folding over and pressing the heels of his hands to his eyes. “You stupid suicidal *idiot*.”

“Sokka?” Katara ventures warily, his name tentative and traveling three pitches.

Sokka ignores her, trying to pull himself back together and recall every single thing he can about their last pai sho game. There was that moment—fuck, what had Zuko said? The words were nearly overshadowed in Sokka’s mind by the hand traveling up his thigh, the sweet torture of Zuko deliberately winding him up, but some part of him latches onto everything Zuko ever says or does around him. ‘*I could be good at long-term strategy. When I want to* *be.’* With the glare and the glower and the immediate fucking proof.

Oh. Oh Spirits. Talk about suddenly deciding to want.

“Sokka,” Toph says, nudging him with one callused foot. “Get it together.” Another burst of hysterical giggles spills out of him instead. “Are you—are you okay?”

“He’s playing the long game,” Sokka gasps out, a numb kind of surety settling over the sharp edges of his hysteria as he gives the words voice.

“…What?”

“He’s playing the long game,” Sokka repeats, shoving up to sit back on his heels with a disbelieving kind of laugh—and Spirits, when he finally gets space to process and think about this he is *not* going to be laughing anymore. He scrubs his hands over his face, finally looking up to see everyone else’s expressions of blank incomprehension and concern.

Toph screws up her face. “What does that even mean? That he’s got some plan?”

“I—yeah. I think.”

“You *think*,” Katara echoes, sounding torn between disbelief and anger and something that might be pity, and Sokka swallows hard against the thing in his chest that could just as easily turn back into a scream.

“I didn’t exactly have a chance to *ask* him, Katara.”

“What would the plan be for?” Toph jumps in, for once trying to disperse the fight before it sparks.

Sokka shifts his attention to her, looking for words and finding nothing. He can only shake his head, mute. He…doesn’t know. He doesn't know. He can try to guess, but that could take him...to so many places. And Sokka isn’t willing to offer any of them up without being sure, first, not when it could mean peeling back every bit of Zuko for their examination, not when he doesn't know if they'd see it all and still turn to him with pity in their eyes. Sokka knows so many things about Zuko, from the history of his skin to the way he holds his chopsticks to the fact that he holds a special kind of hatred for the charcoal pencils at the Blooming Petal. But they never talked about their hopes for the future, not like that. Not like *this.* It always made Zuko tense, always skirted too close to the Avatar and the war and things Sokka didn’t want to think about and wouldn’t force onto Zuko even if he did, things like the finite amount of time they had together and the choices they might have to make at the end.

For as long as Sokka has known him—and going by Iroh’s teasing, for significantly longer than that—Zuko's seemed to avoid thinking ahead like it was a disease. Zuko went out of his way to avoid pai sho games, always grunted his way through the kinds of hypothetical discussions Iroh liked to have about abstract futures, the ones where Sokka might have seen the way Zuko's mind worked outside the short term, what he wanted and longed for beyond just the cautious bits Sokka remembers from letters. Sokka had always written it off as part of Zuko’s weird, persistent squirminess around Iroh and pai sho, or his general reluctance to get into what amounted to a usually-polite verbal fight when he was already grumpy after a day of work. But what if…

No. Sokka can’t go there. He can’t afford to. Later, when he isn’t feeling like this, he'll make himself consider it. He'll make himself actually think it through. But now, when it feels like every part of himself could break so easily—he can’t let himself doubt now.

And Sokka isn’t sure it even matters, anyway. Because regardless of the reason Zuko might have, Sokka still has no idea how Zuko could be playing this. He is painfully, hugely aware, like a knife in the gut, that he has no idea what Zuko could be playing *for,* because he’s never seen Zuko play these kinds of games outside of swordfights and occasionally the bedroom.

Toph and Katara and Aang—please, Spirits, Aang—will want reasons and justifications and hard facts to examine and hold up and plan around. And all Sokka has to offer right now are hopes, desperate ones, ones that he wants to be right with everything in him, about what he thinks Zuko could be doing. But he doesn't *know.*

Which means that all Sokka can do in the face of Toph's doubt and Katara's anger and Aang's still, still form is cling to his faith in Zuko, to hold hard to his belief in the truths that Zuko always gave him, to the fact that whenever Sokka ever asked him what he wanted, Zuko always replied ‘you.’

&#45;-

Zuko stands with Azula in the Earth King’s palace, looking out of the hole that Uncle blew through the wall this morning. Agni, that feels like lifetimes ago rather than just the space of the sun's arc. Zuko isn’t sure why Azula decided to walk this way, beyond her general fondness for symbolism and grinding your rawest emotions against each other until they bleed. But it’s nice to be able to look out over the city instead of down the hallway as Uncle is dragged away, expression as righteously disappointed as it’s been since he was captured.

Uncle’s tea things were still in the throne room, Zuko noticed when they passed by the wreckage earlier. Maybe he should go back and pack up the tea blends. The leaves will go stale if they're left out like that.

“Don’t worry, Brother. You’re not the betrayer here.” Azula’s voice is deceptively drawling, expression acid as her eyes follow after Iroh.

Zuko…isn’t going to engage with that. “Do you really think that I can return to the Fire Nation? That I’ll have my honor restored without the Avatar?” Or will Zuko just be sent on another quest, this time for an infant somewhere in the Water Tribes?

Azula leans against the edge of the blown-out wall, smiling. Amused by his hesitancy, he supposes. “Zuzu, they will welcome you with open arms.”

Zuko grunts, nodding, turning to look out over the city and crossing his arms to hide his jitteriness. He needs to appear calm, composed, sure of himself. He can’t show any the hectic worry bouncing through his chest over whether he actually made the right choice, over whether he read the right things between the lines of Katara’s words and in the spaces Azula spoke around.

Zuko was ready for this, in theory. But it all came up so much faster than he expected. He had hoped—foolish, foolish, to hope—for a few more days at least. One last time seeing Sokka, a chance to explain what he could. Space to ready himself for Azula and the way she always sees too much.

But now it's here anyway, with no time and no chance and no space, and Zuko knows its useless to think about what might have been in the middle of how things are now. There’s only the path in front of him, the one he carved for himself outside of the boundaries that had been set around him. The one he's still carving, because things might have gone completely to shit but that doesn't mean they're done, they're never done, not when the first lesson Zuko ever learned, the one carved deepest into his bones, is to never stay down, to never stop getting back up.

Sokka. Uncle. His home. His three most important things, within reach if he can just balance on the knife’s edge opportunity that Azula has opened for him.

“Snow.” It’s floating down in heavy flakes, the kind that will accumulate quickly against the cold earth.

“The first of the season.” It feels strangely appropriate for this day to be so clearly marked by autumn finally giving way to winter. Like the world itself is marking the quiet, unseen, hopefully-monumental shift that took beneath the palace halls.

Zuko watches Azula reach out to catch a flake on her finger. Her expression is thoughtful as she watches it melt against her skin before casting a considering look toward the sky. This is her first time away from the Fire Nation. She probably hasn’t seen snow before. But there's plenty to see now. It falls quickly, making up for lost time maybe, painting the city white and clean, building the fragile illusion of an untouched canvass and blanketing it all in a heavy silence broken only by their barely-audible voices.

“Are you ready for this?”

“Does it matter?”

A shrug. “Not if you want to win.”

A huff. “Burn bright, then.”

An annoyed glare. “Religious verse? Really?”

“Burn bright, Child of Agni.”

An eyeroll, but following along, “Be Agni’s hand upon the earth.”

“Light the way ahead.”

A flick of fire into the falling snow, carving a swathe of steam. “Because there is no way out but forward.”
